review_text:
I really like this game, the combat and movement feels really good and rewarding, to me, movement is one of the most important aspects of the games I play, and this one achieves an amazing level of freedom at traversing the map.

There are a few things that feel kind of rough and that in my opinion could be polished in order to provide the player with better quality of life.

This game is difficult, it can be really challenging, but there’s a difference between difficulty and unfairness, those rough spots I mentioned are derived from the feeling of unfairness at certain areas of the game.

First, it can overwhelm you quite easily, you have to keep so many things and variables in mind that at some point you feel like you can’t just perform enough actions to save yourself, I’m talking about hordes of enemies just closing in on you from all sides, of course this is the objective the devs are probably trying to achieve and honestly, I think it is the right approach but here’s where some of the rough spots also show up the most:

- Enemies simply spawning behind you without giving you any hints until right before they attack, making it hard to plan and organize yourself with the environment 

- The poison mechanic, it is really frustrating when you are surrounded and trying to survive and you become poisoned from almost an unknown source without any real chance to fight it back, I really think this game would benefit from having a poison meter that quickly fills up instead of poison being an immediate status right after you get hit.

You don’t even have to get hit to become poisoned, just being close to a poison cloud is enough to immediately poison you, this becomes problematic when you can’t see the poison cloud but you still get the effect, and it’s even more problematic when you feel that you’re losing health just for existing in the world.

- The calamity counter, there’s this little counter on the top left of the screen that keeps track of how many mistakes you have made in a run, usually a mistake is when you get hit by something or suffer damage, except from fall damage, when it gets to 5 a calamity event starts, this is a fantastic mechanic, however based on the previous points I made, there are times when you inevitably end up with 2 or 3 points out of 5 by things that you as a player feel like you couldn’t have possibly avoid, (like poison)

These are a few of the things that keep this game from being a truly challenging but enjoyable experience and turn it more into a challenging and frustrating experience with enjoyable moments here and there.

And again, I don’t mean to bash on the game at all, it’s genuinely an amazing game if you like difficult games, and I’ll probably keep playing it because it gives you a sense of achievement after going through hell, but it’s important to recognize that some things are not as good as they could be.

- In the real NHL speed is pretty much around the same for all players except a select few who have incredible speed or are really slow. In game most players have speed ratings difference of ~10 except a couple of players (Hagelin, Kreider).

- In game ratings are mostly well balanced and are very close to that of the real life player. (Note that ratings can be changed with a 3rd party freeware).

- Drafting is very nice having good players in most drafts lets you get good prospects on a yearly basis.

- Player development is good. Keep in mind that you need good coaching staff with the rating "working with youngster" high enough for the prospect to develop well.

The Bad ; 

- Trading is awefull, Wanting to trade my Stamkos, i was offered a 2nd round pick and two 3rd round picks by all of the teams that had interest into him, Same goes when trying to trade for a player. EG : I needed a first line key winger and i had a surplus of Key 1-2 defender. I offered Subban for Kessel and they did not want to negotiate, so just out of curiosity i add four 1st round picks and they still would not want any part of it. Overall trading needs to be tweeked but you can get a steal every now and then when a team is desperate or overly incompetent.

- Way to many injury blows or long term injury. At one point in my game, Galchenyuk, Subban, Price and Pacioretty had over 3 months injury. the longest was Price with 8 months. This to say, i was left with an AHL team in my hands.

I actually really liked this game until just now. 

I really enjoyed experimenting with how to conquer as fast as possible one region with balanced economy. 
But then when I was about to win and destroy last corner covered with corruption. I sent 4 builders to build a Stone Wall so I could attack with long distance Ballista tower however they instead of building the wall attacked one of the last 2 Graveyards and one after other hit the Graveyard and with each hit there came small army of enemies = 4 hits = +/-25 monsters (Out of it was like 8 Fire Elementals and 5 Skeletons) = Which destroyed my entire defense with blink of an eye :/ 
Over 14 hours put into this region for what? Not being able to set priorities to Workers what to do when I give them specific work? Why do I select Workers as "Builder", "Farmer" when they still do what they want? 
There should be possibility to choose if I want Worker to fight or not - Not that they decide themselves (Some run away from threat, some march towards it). 

Until this moment I would give positive feedback, but if you choose in any scenario to build something close to an enemy structure, Builders just go attack that structure instead of building a building with highest set priority.

Also there is no way to "Cancel" dismantling an already build wall or wall with resources already on place (Or any structure). Only way how to destroy/dismantle something is that you take all the resources with your "God power", like... Why? Are my Workers that stupid that they don't know how to use a hammer and smash things to pieces? 

One last thing which is quite bothering is that if you select rock or tree to harvest, there is no way to cancel it after. So after you select harvest something, it will be harvested sooner or later. So if you decide to be more strategic in the future in the game, that you decide that "Rock" or "Tree" could be like a piece of wall, you can't because you never know when your Workers will decide to harvest it since you can't cancel that harvest... Eh, great...Also if you select too many trees to be harvested they randomly go harvest those trees all over the map instead of most closest place to the structure they are building... *facepalm*

I DON'T RECOMMEND THIS GAME:
 - If there will be priorities what Workers should prioritize (If fight or do their selected work first) and 
- "Cancel" button when you choose to dismantle things and 
- "Removal button" for already selected harvested areas.
After this I would recommend this game.

review_text:
Was quite excited for this since it looked like the perfect game for me. I have been craving a game like this for a very long time, and couldn't wait to fire this up on my steam deck. I felt a huge sense of relief after controlling the character for the first time. Movement and animations in this game are clean as hell, so I was buzzing to get into the main game and start pulling off some crazy tricks.

The disappointment followed pretty soon after when I realized that in order to do tricks, you just press 1 button. There are a few combinations that allow you to do some extra moves yes, but after less than an hour in I felt as if I had reached a skill ceiling and exhausted the mechanics of the game.

There is a severe lack of challenge in BRC, and I'm surprised that there is hardly anyone bringing this up. You can't modify any of the tricks by adding your own flair to them like spins and flips, they're all pre-programmed in and require 1 button press to do. This leads to a massive lack of self-expression since, and all the videos I've seen on YouTube of BRC show everyone doing the exact same combos in exactly the same places. You can't bail either, so playing the game got super stale very quick and I hate to say it. I want more games like this so badly, but in general with BRC there just isn't enough of a skill ceiling involved and essentially no challenge. 

Genuinely one of the most annoying reviews because I wanted to love this game so badly, but I can't.

review_text:
Let me be very blunt: this is an extraction shooter game, but single-player only. If you enjoy games like Helldivers II and Space Marine II, this is a decent game to play as well. However, the lack of multiplayer makes this a very repetitive and boring game, and I find that I can only play one or two runs before quitting out of frustration. I'll explain:

There are many aspects in this game that seem to contradict each other. It's a shooter game, but almost all the enemies don't drop ammunition. You can only obtain ammunition from ammo chests, which are scattered throughout the map, or by killing enemies specifically spawned from the portal. Now, there is also a melee attack, as well as spells you can use to further aid you in killing your enemies, but the main source of damage is your guns. As a result, ammunition is usually the limiting factor from advancing through the map or extracting early.

There are groups of enemies scattered throughout the map. These are alright. However, there seems to be an alert system that spawns more enemies when you kill one in a group, which can quickly get out of hand if you don't expect it. Furthermore, there seems to be no warning. You could kill ten enemies in a row without an alert, but all of a sudden you kill an enemy, and then enemies begin spawning all around you, even if you instakill them. It's annoying, especially because you NEED to kill enemies on the map to progress, so you can't avoid them either. 

The story of this game is very shallow, and it's clear the developers didn't intend on implementing storyline aspects in the game. You are introduced as a 'preyer', who is an agent of a Church. Your goal is to eliminate evil witches and their minions, using guns and spells. That's it. Nothing else. There is no insight into who you are, why you became a preyer, how the world changed around you, etc. Even the Steam description of this game has more story in it: "you play as a wicked inner turned witch hunter on his final mission to reach salvation." But when you get into the game, there is absolutely no mention of this through out the playthrough. You can see hints of the developers' efforts in a half-hearted story by reading the location descriptions and any notes around the maps you get, but the location descriptions are clearly flavor text, and the notes are used to describe the mechanics of the game more than actually providing a story.

In line with the issue of storyline, there is no end-game goal. Let's say you fully clear a map, get all the loot, and extract. Congratulations, you can level up, get new weapons, and go in again. There is no global impact. It doesn't feel rewarding at all. The map just shuffles a bit, and you go again. And again. And again. Eventually, only one clear of a map isn't enough to level up. So, without spending your witchfire (which is used to level up), you must go to another map. And if you die in this map, you drop ALL your loot. Of course, you can pick it up again by going back, but it just feels hopelessly endless without a goal. 

Lastly, there is no multiplayer. I understand that this game is marketed as a single player game, but without storyline, endgame goal, and with more and more enemies that get stronger as you progress, it just feels numbing. What feels worse is that on the developers' FAQ, they specifically stated that they have no plans to implement multiplayer even when fully released. 

Now, a few things to keep in mind: When I wrote this review, I had 11 hours accrued in this game. As I progress, I might find things that would cause my opinion to change. Also, this game is in early access. The developers might read this review and change some things. But until then, this game, in its current state, is, in my opinion, not worth its current price tag of $40.

review_text:
What can I say? Lucius is without any doubt an original product in terms of plot, putting the player in the skin of a 10 year old antichrist on a killing spree, intent on sacrificing is own family members for his satanic daddy by making every kill look like an accident thanks to unholy supernatural powers acquired throughout the game. At the beginning of Lucius I thought the narration would bring me to dislike each one of the victims, instead I almost felt sorry for them 'cause they were actually nice people with feelings and emotions. Some of the deaths were slapstick horror fun, while other a little more serious and those made me feel a bit guilty (or maybe I am just aging).
Personal feelings towards the poor Wagner family apart, in terms of gameplay Lucius is some kind of Hitman lookalike but far more linear. It's more of a puzzle game where you have to figure out what to do in order to kill someone and make it look like an accident, which is awesome. The whole game setting is the giant family manor, well detailed and fully explorable. The graphics are okay, while the voice acting is really good for a low budget game. I had to turn off the music 'cause it was the same classical tune repeated over and over that ruined the creepy atmosphere of the game. 
That said, I really  recommend this game if you want something different, but do not expect any freedom or choices. 

\m/ -_- \m/ 

Peace!

With this kind of game you really have to take a gamble based on reviews and in this case, the reviews really let me down.  I'd really like my 4 hours back.

All of this could be forgiven, however, if the story made up for it.  It did not.  I had to wait an hour for the hook, then got dragged along a poorly paced and poorly told story that concluded with an ending which was unneccessarily empty and disappointing.

There are several great examples of indie games that focus on story, but this is not one of them.  Save yourself a lot of wasted time and play something else.

review_text:
This game is just... really good. It's essentially a village sim that has difficulty for all sorts of players, casual, challengers, etc. The gameplay itself is super in-depth, and I found it very enjoyable. The challenging difficulty is a really nice change of pace from most village sims. 

That being said, there are a couple complains I do have. Firstly, it takes a VERY long time to unlock things. It took me 7 hours to unlock my first perk, so yeah, way too grindy. Second, the tutorial is very bare-bones and if I'm being completely honest, really bad. I can definitely see how it pushes new players away. I get it's a high learning curve but it genuinely felt like the tutorial was really lazy... I had to resort to multiple external sources (Wiki, YT tutorials, etc.) to get a hang of the game, which is almost never a good sign. Hopefully the tutorial can get an overhaul in future updates, since I would hate to see players get pushed away from this amazing game.

Overall, this game is a hidden gem, and I really wish it got more popularity. It's got an amazing concept rooted and I'm looking forward to future updates the game has. Would definitely recommend, just be wary of the rocky start you may have when trying out the game.

review_text:
-- The Short Review --
This is going to be long-winded, and probably expanded upon much like my MW5:M review as I play more. The TL;DR is that yes, I think this game is a fun time if you like sci-fi horror and melee-focused action games. However, going in to this game expecting a 'true' survival-horror experience will set you up for disappointment. Graphically impressive and with some tense moments, an open-minded person will still have a good time as long as they feel the price for admission was worth it. For ~$20, I'd say go for it.

-- The Long Review --
To get the technical stuff out of the way: the game is visually stunning. The fidelity of the environments, character models, gore, monsters, etc. is truly impressive and maybe it is partially due to not being 'current' on modern blockbuster-esque games but the graphics alone have left much more of an impression on me than I ever thought they would. The animations have lots of nuance and fluidity and look amazing. I love looking at this game and taking in the carnage of the environments as I walk and run and fight around them. The sound is great as well; I've not noticed any bad or out-of-place effects and sounds are appropriately powerful or guttural for the weapons and monsters respectively. The music has been good, not 'put this in my playlist' good but also the game would lack something without its presence. After close to two years since its release, I have not had any performance issues apart from the weirdness that can happen from running a game on native LInux with Proton. Honestly its ran far better for me than RE4R despite possibly being the more demanding game.

Now, we can get into the real issues.

The monster design is cool! They are gross and mean-looking and are definitely not out-of-place in sci-fi horror. But... they're not scary. I know that I'm also not all of the way through this game and probably haven't seen everything, but I had to start this review because it just doesn't scare me. Sure it has tense moments and some environments are genuinely creepy, but the horror element is severely let down by the mechanics of the game. The game sets you (Jacob) up as a surprisingly durable killing machine, that can swiftly dodge and dismantle the creatures that set upon you. Against a player that can handle the combat system, these creatures don't stand a chance. You will beat the ever-living shit out of them until they are convulsing in a pile of broken bones and mangled flesh and then you stomp on them some more to let them know how pathetic they are (and to get your loot drops of course).

In a real survival-horror game, combat is a gamble. Is the cost of resources worth the investment of dealing with this threat? (ex. Zombies in RE2R) Can I even deal with this threat? (ex. Mr. X or the Ubermorph) Or, for the more apt comparison of Dead Space (2008) or Dead Space 2 (2011), will I be able to deal with the enemies before they ever get close to me? In my opinion, survival-horror is at its best when you can technically deal with the threats before you, but at the same time you are sacrificing something to do so, while also not wanting these creatures to ever even think about touching you because the consequences are severe.

Conversely in Callisto, when I see an enemy I buckle up and charge in to start beating the ever-living shit out of them with a big smile on my face. The combat system isn't even that technically deep like a Souls-like game or a fighting game, but I find it to be quite satisfying. This is the complete opposite feeling I should have about combat in a game that wants to be a horror game, where the game clearly wants you to fear the creatures that you are fighting. While I enjoy Dead Space combat, I don't necessarily *want* to be in combat in Dead Space. I do everything I can to deal with the necromorphs as quickly as possible so that I can stop being in danger. Callisto has for better or worse, turned you into the danger. I am actively looking for fights because ironically that is the safest place to be in as well as the point when I'm having the most fun. Dodging is simple and easy enough to pull off, and is almost completely safe when doing so. Ranged enemies still pose a threat as your dodge animation only saves you from the enemy you are currently engaged with, but management of ranged enemies or the environment will reduce that risk. Getting grappled does not instantly deal damage to you with all enemy types as far as I can tell, or does not deal enough damage to be a big factor because of the ease of dodging. There is at least a balance issue if I'd rather be grabbed than block an attack because blocking feels like I take more damage from bleed-through. At risk of repeating myself, we'll leave it at that until my inevitable comment-extensions.

My only other major complaint is that the first three chapters of the game and somewhat into the fourth, I was drowning in items with not enough places to offload them. We don't have storage this time around so you have to sell or use what you don't need, but you can't pick up everything because the game starts you off with a measly SIX INVENTORY SLOTS. With how much stuff there was to pick up, this was incredibly frustrating. Instead of being relieved that I found another health injector or ammo for the pistol, I had to play the "Do I have enough space for this item?" game every couple of minutes. What added insult to injury was instead of being able to back-track reasonable amounts to pick up items I had to leave behind, the game pushes you forward several times with permanently locked doors or sequences that cannot be undone due to the game's linearity. Dead Space managed this finite balance well, and offset some of the pressure by allowing you to store items for later when in an excess, so that if you ever found yourself in a drought you could address it. What I will say is that I have so far found the ammunition for the pistol to be a pretty good balance of 'just enough'. Once I'm further into the game that may change.

What about the story? Oh yeah, it's there. I'm enjoying the characters enough and I'm engaged because it does feel like a horror-movie story but its not the 'best story ever told'. When thinking about Callisto's story I'm reminded of The Belko Experiment, which while I had fun with that movie it wasn't a movie I'd rush home to tell everybody about.

Despite my issues with the game, I am still having a good time and have been trying to fit it into my busy schedule. Will it hold up on repeat playthroughs? Higher difficulties? I'll know soon enough. More thoughts TBA as I get further along. Although...

review_text:
Any one who ever watched the movie The Omen will already pretty much know what to expect from Lucius, it's the story of a child that is pure evil.. born of Wealthy parents, but with a secret, his actual father is Lucifer, Satan, Beelzebub, or any other name people have for the Devil.. This game plays as if it was meant to be the Omen in all honesty, the story while not identical to the movie, shares alot of the same general ideas and principles as if the son of the Devil has a playbook you need to follow..

So remember when we were all wishing to play a game where we are the bad guys, and all we got was a funny comedy game called Overlord, where we played as somewhat of a bad guy but not really.. Well this game you are the bad guy,, err bad kid.. you go around, plotting and murdering people.. watching people have sex, and seeing nudity.. it's one of those games that will leave you feeling kind of dirty...

Gameplay,

you play various chapters where you can set up elaborate traps to kill employees of your wealthy parents and anyone else who gets in your way including your own family,... Whether it's locking them in a freeze, putting them in the oven, poison, gunshots, crossbows,, you're in the words of Samuel L Jackson a BAMF....

The game takes place in third person, you pick up various items, combine them, and then use them on various objects.. most of the time the kills are very straightforward, and the game pretty much only gives you one way to kill the person but you're normally given a few extra task during the game, whether it's cleaning up your room, to finding pictures etc etc etc... Although most stages are fairly large and give you lots of freedom, the actual chapters normally only require you to move around a few rooms, collect 4 or 5 items and then get a really satisfying kill.

Also has a Tricycle you can ride around on like a Pimp, while you plan and carry out your killing sprees,, Don't forget to turn those crosses upside down,, nothing worst then getting ready to set someone on fire only to find out that Cross chilling a foot away from them drained you of power like that time Lance Armstrong forget his injection..

Pro's
Interesting story
unique gameplay mechanics
Nice flow, artwork and soundtrack

Con's
grindy achievements to flush out gameplay time,,
a few bugs and glitches
needs more freedom in the kills..

recommendation

Since you can pick this game up for pretty much the cost of a dollar menu item from McDonalds no reason exist not to buy it. You'll be glad you did, and enjoy the interesting, unique and fun story of playing as the Anti-Christ.. I say buy it now, but considering the game came out in 2012, you probably already owned it and beat it.. so.. meh,, have at it..

review_text:
Played through the series; every entry I've played (0-4) up to this point have been absolutely top notch until now. It took me three tries to finish this entry in the series because I just could not get through it.

Kiryu's part is alright, but right as it starts getting interesting you're whisked away into Saejima's section which consists of a prison break (again), boring sequences in his 'imagination' where you go round the city doing pointless things in his head with a horrible blue filter over everything, and after breaking out you have to painstakingly hunt deer in the wilderness rather than actually playing an interesting story.

Then, Haruka's section is also horrendous, you get thrown into 'teenage girl becomes a pop star simulator' with dancing minigames as the primary gameplay and... it is just not enjoyable. You have to watch a young girl go to dance recitals and dance about the screen which is not exactly what I feel like sitting through, and while the story becomes mildly more interesting than Saejima's here I could not wait to actually get into some decent Yakuza gameplay which we still haven't seen much of until this point, bar Kiryu and a tiny bit of the last section of Saejima. During this section I was getting worried somebody might walk in and wonder what on Earth I was playing since the dancing stuff looks like it's targeted towards little girls if you don't get the context it's a Yakuza game. But hey, I suppose there's only one manlier thing than shirtless dudes beating each other up and that's watching your daughter achieve her dreams (not that I have any experience lol).

Akiyama and then especially Shinada's section do bring it back a bit, but it's too little too late and the only chapters of the whole game I found myself actually enjoying to a similar degree as the rest of the series were the very final one or two. Even then, the circumstances and writing surrounding everyone coming together for this part of the story are not great. The overall story was also much weaker than the rest of the series.

Overall, this is the only game in the series so far that I have a negative opinion of coming out of it. and I was honestly glad to finish it. I'm happy to finally break the curse of being stuck here as I'm playing them in order, and now I can get back to the good things about this franchise in the next entries. I do hear the side content is good though, but I ended up skipping most of it in favour of putting the overall game behind me and experiencing the side content of a better entry to the series. If you don't fancy hunting deer in the snow or watching a teenage girl sing pop songs for hours, skip this entry.

I am writing this review upon my third playthrough of this game - I can't believe I put myself through the torture of the console version twice before playing it on PC. The PC version is a massive improvement from console in regards to optimization, graphics, and bugs. If you've been hesitant to buy the PC version after playing on console - don't be. It is absolutely worth it to experience this masterpiece as intended.

This is one of the most unique experiences gaming has to offer. Similar to that of Russian literature, this story involves one of the most tragically beautiful blend of spiritual themes and philosophies I've seen in a video game. The developers use of Eurasian folklore brings attention to a topic that I feel isn't widely discussed, and I really appreciate that. 

Pathologic 2 is an anti-power fantasy where the main character... really isn't even the main character once you dig in and peel back the layers. Your choices in this game can reveal a lot about yourself while drawing lines between surgeon Artemy's history and the secrets of his small Steppe hometown of Gorkhon. While the RPG elements are fairly linear regarding dialogue, this game emphasizes that you can't do everything and you can't save everyone, offering you only your free will to complete the tasks that are important to you with time as your only limitation. A fascinating thing about this game's mechanics is that time will always move forward. No matter what you're doing, whether you're working the hospital, talking to townsfolk, playing hide and seek with the local orphans or sleeping, things will happen and the opportunity to interact with these things will pass - much like in real life. When you aren't engaged in conversation you will run around frantically at times scavenging to collect supplies, running from person to person to perform your doctoral duties while also maintaining your own health needs, running from thugs... or towards them if you prefer to fight head on, crafting folk medicine, and managing your sparse inventory space.

The design of this game is one of my favorite aspects, especially regarding environment. A big difference I have noticed between experiencing this on console and PC is how detailed the weather can be and how that can change the mood of the day in game. As you move deeper into the pandemic, the weather has a tendency to get foggier, rainier, and darker, whereas at the beginning of the game you bask in much more sunlight. The architectural elements of this game is also interesting, and plays a huge role in explaining the town's history. As a survival horror/dark fantasy game, you will find some of the most intimidating parts of the map to actually end up being the safest, forcing you to accept and even seek comfort in the dark.

Knowing how few people complete this game based on achievement history across platforms with a massive drop off after the plague hits, I'd like to add this to the discussion: I'm not going to pretend this game is easy in gameplay or easy to get through with it's heavy themes. It's not. It's quite frustrating at times and incredibly challenging and honestly sometimes really uncomfortable to sit through. If you're reading this and have avoided playing this game because of the potential for frustration - don't!! Experiencing this game is so rewarding and failure is part of the experience (and even leads to unlocking new bits of lore at times!!) 

All in all, this is one of my favorite games of all time and I wish I could see this series get more traction. Thank you, devs, for this work of art.

review_text:
(Warning: This is written from the POV of someone who played this at launch. A lot has been patched/added)

I'll be honest. I wasn't enthused when I first tried bonelab. It wasn't really the game I was expecting. Coming off of boneworks, which I loved and am willing to admit had quite a few issues, I found a lot of problems with bonelab. 

For one, I regocnise that the whole game's purpose was for it to be a modding sandbox. Has it lived up to that? I don't know. I never got mods working. I tried many websites, launchers, guides, the whole nine yards. It just never worked (I'm on PC for reference). The campaign was alright, but not too enthralling and a bit immersion breaking. 

Secondly, the cool environment and aesthetics that boneworks had (and I loved) wasn't present within bonelab. It made sense, yea. You get a new character to unlock and the environment thematically matched that character. That's fine. But, it felt like it switched way too fast too often. Furthermore, there were only two characters that I personally liked, and only one that I used (these being the big strong guy who looks straight outta dark souls and the slim fast girl in the body tight suit (I used the girl mainly cuz she was the only one who was close to matching my body irl)). 

And lastly, and this is a personal gripe of mine (take it with a grain of salt), I never liked how boneworks or bonelabs did full body. I just didn't enjoy it. It's probably the most immersion breaking part of either game. None of the movements feel like something I instigated. If I had to describe it, it feels like riding a segway made of jello. They got in the way of my actions (I.E. making two handing rifles almost impossible), got caught on terain and props that I didn't notice (causing a slight out of body experience as I try to figure out why the character isn't doing what I thought/wanted), and not really tied to what I imagine I'm doing (no, I don't think my foot should be ontop of the box that I just wanted to pick up). If they added an option for full body tracking (which I have and would love to use), then I'm sure a lot of the aforementioned issues would be more/less solved. And, no doubt, there's a mod to fix them. But again, I couldn't get mods working.

Was it fun? Yes. I enjoyed it a bit.

Would I recommend it? No. There were too many bugs when I played it (2 majorly game breaking ones that had me frustrated for hours), and I'd say there are better games for cheaper. 

Overall, I'm disappointed but always willing to give it a second chance. It's a sandbox after all. I'm sure that (if I ever get mods working) I'll find my niche within it given enough time.

Nice rewards for exploration and fun, vibrant areas. 

Okay music.

Some challenging if not kinda annoying enemy types and decent variety.

review_text:
Well, it's sad I have to do the review this way, but so far MXGP PRO was a major disappointment for me. They really built up a lot of hype for me with the first announcement, but now we are sitting here with MXGP 4. 
Don't get me wrong, if you like the other MXGP games this game is great aswell and they managed to improve themselves just like with every other MX game they made since MXGP1, but it's not what you would expect with the pro advertisement.

Before I can start with my pro and contra points, I have to mention something that wasn't clear for me and some of my friends.
It's known that there are training missions in the game, but I didn't realize you actually have to do them before you can enjoy the game. They have a major impact on how the bike feels.

negative:
- the game should direct you after or without the tutorial directly to the necessary training missions, but it doesn't
- after doing the missions the bike feels way better, but thats the reason the game became just as easy as all the games before --> first 2 gps without training I struggled to not get last, first gp after the training was a win (pro physics vs realistic ai and ~18 years of playing mx games...)
- terrain deformation looks not that bad, but to feel your rear wheel sliding into a rut is a rare occasion. impact on riding is nearly 0
- whips are way better, but still not what you would expect from the free whip advertisement
- perfomance is disgusting. the steam fps counter shows locked 60 fps, but the game feels like 20-30 maybe and sometimes i have actual small fps drops too with a ok rig
- when changing from window to fullscreen, my game is flickering green all the time until I change back to window mode
- surname only 8 characters. This wasn't a thing in the previous 4 MX games, why tf now?

positive:
- you crash easier now, which was kinda a challenge in the previous game (not that much that the game got hard now...)
- beside the mentioned negative points, the game is a improved MXGP3 which isn't bad
- mid air bike adjustments are finally here
- whips are way better in comparison to previous games, but don't expect free whips like in REFLEX or ALL OUT
- more options to change the settings on the bike
- in carreer mode you now have influence on the rivalry with other riders when reacting positive, negative or neutral to the social media posts that were senseless in previous games
- in general the carreer is fun and improved further to the other MXGP games. now you not only choose a main sponsor with a season goal, you choose part sponsors aswell with smaller goals you have to reach for example in 3 gp races
- the few training missions are something i haven't seen so far and are quite fun, even tho they don't last that long

I would really like to recommend this game, but I think misleading marketing has to be punished.

my rig:
Ryzen 1600 @ 3,8GHz
Palit GTX 1060 SJS
16GB RAM

review_text:
Completely honestly, not unless this is on a really good sale AND you really need some more Dead Space-like gameplay.

This game is a really watered down dead space... but even worse. I like how they announced that devs from that game were also working on this, because you can easily spot the similarities from the start and you think "oh hell yeah, I know this. This is gonna be good."  But no, you get the rug completely pulled out from under you. This game focuses on a melee-oriented combat with guns as mostly support, or as a means to just thin out a horde.. except you borderline don't even need the guns and the combat mechanics are a joke. How to combat you ask? simple. just hold left or right alternatively as an enemy swipes at you and your character dodges. That's it, literally. I've been playing a good part of it just on the melee weapon now to sell ammo for upgrades faster. Now enemies can't even block my melee attacks or they lose a limb which limits then to a singular one melee attack. Oh and you have stealth takedowns which is at least fairly cool, and gets really funny when you later encounter the typical blind-but-sound-based enemies a bit later, because you can just sneak and stealth takedown each one so easily, and yet all the sound you make DURING the takedown doesn't alert any of them, even if there's a whole group literally standing next to you. ammo savings at its finest, and a ton of free loot from all the kills.


Inventory is a bloody joke. You get 6 slots.this gets upgraded to 12 slots automatically in the story at one point... but why is it so few? and why can't the game let me progressively buy more inventory upgrades like dead space where I can choose to invest in some QOL for my character? like maybe 1 or 2 more slots at a time.. sheesh. 6 is very little considering how much the game tries to stuff you inventory sometimes with random crap like those useless energy packs that only sell for 10 measly credits and DO NOT stack in your inventory.  One singular starter pistol ammo sells for that much, and stacks to 12 on each inventory slot. you do the math. one singular shit item for 10 credits per slot, one one stack of pistol ammo for 120 credits per slot. I also dislike how chests/boxes/etc have randomized loot every time you reload... why? like what benefit or what purpose is there to this? I've gotten chests with 2 battery packs and i immediately reload because i'm not taking this shit.

oh, and also the saving system is absolute shit. Your manual saves do ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. The only thing that matters is the checkpoint saves. Whenever you manual save, the game basically goes "hey, what's the latest automatic game checkpoint save... yeah just throw the player back there when they load back up."
This means even if you manual save, your progress between now and whatever your latest checkpoint was is completely meaningless. You lose everything you did after that point. all shop purchases and sales, all upgrades you did, all the inventory management, all the loot you looted, all the enemies you killed.... undone,... and you have to do it AGAIN.


so yeah, this game is a bit step backwards for deadspace gameplay. They upgraded the graphics..... but at the cost of everything else. IMO dead space 1, and i mean the ORIGINAL not the newer updated version, is still better than this. That game had much better horror and mechanics. This game is just trying to ride the coattail of its success.

review_text:
I hate to say this, Sega, but you fucked up, big time.

NGS is a technical and visual upgrade to PSO2. In many ways, this game is better than PSO2 - however, PSO2 worked because of an overabundance of content and small, unobtrusive, largely socially focused hub. Part of the issue - in my opinion - is that they did not commit to a direction, but weakly reached in many directions. The Combat is easier and fancier, but with less options. The world is bigger and more beautiful, but lacking in any kind of meaningful content, and most importantly of all, the Fashion aspect is as egregious as it ever was. - admittedly, the final bit is owing to the utter destruction of the original market, and the fact that the global ships always had a worse economical basis than the JP servers, owing to a larger stock due to more customers (and the fact that JP had more things in the FUN scratch, and more things in the regular scratches, too.)

The character creation and customization is amazingly good, As is the combat. The problem is, it's always the same combat.

In PSO2, combat felt weighty. moving around was slow in comparison - you used abilities to move meaningfully most of the time, and combat was alot more rigid and reflexive. In NGS, you have a dedicated dash button and can climb even the harshest mountains with ease - and these would not be problems were it not for the fact that it seems like they did not plan for this at all in map design.

That is what I mean when I say they did not commit to a direction. None of the systems compliment each other. Movement is fast, but as a result, anything else that causes the character to move feels slow. Why would I use a hoverboard if my dash is easier to control, to jump with, and I can more easily attack out of it? why would I use a movement skill if my dash is faster? why would I attack normally, when the dash attack deals more damage (this one's more situational, really, but I feel like it's still a valid point)
The above, mixed with... a horrifically disappointing stream of content. (it took them a *year* to release 10 minutes worth of gameplay, not counting time wasting, soul-sucking grinding, and another year to release a goddamn festival.) and the game is, understandably, dying in player count - or at least, it feels that way to me.

So, I can't recommend this game. Because while I have a soft spot for PSO2 base game, with the release of NGS, they completely abandoned it, and no newcoming hotfixes that try to pump the dead heart of this game series is going to resuscitate it unless they release an altogether new game - and no, not another attempt at NGS. To get people who were fans and are now disgruntled interested again - to get ME interested again. they'd have to make a free MMO that's generous about it's items and content, like the Japan-server PSO2 was, and is supported handily, like said game was back in it's day.

Goodnight, PSO, May they not desecrate your corpse for long - for it is too late for them to not have done it at all.

review_text:
To start, this review was written by a fan of the game "Boneworks"

My major gripe with this game is the inconsistency of the physics. Whether that be while climbing (Trying to climb ledges in particular..), Stepping on a piece of a box and having the game freak out, or simply getting your legs stuck on something.

Other pains I had with this game was all the bits and levels where you had to control a vehicle, crane, or mounted gun. Mostly because the constrained movement was both nauseating and frustrating.

The level design itself was a bit hit or miss, as I found myself enjoying some parts while being annoyed at others (Mainly anything that required awkward climbing). It also felt like the whole thing was just showing off modding potential which I personally feel like would have been better placed somewhere else in the game.

Overall it feels like they tried to replicate Boneworks success while piling on half baked buggy features, that said I do have hopes that overtime they can polish the game and turn it into something truly above and beyond the tech showcase it currently is now.

TL;DR: Frustrating design choices and a very unwelcoming experience for inexperienced VR users, or returning boneworks players.

review_text:
Guns have a max range of about 40 feet and past that they deal 1 damage. Infinite range enemies routinely attack you from outside this range, bosses randomly run away and can't even be shot in the back because they're outside this range the instant they stop fighting.

You have to grind the same map over and over to get enough gold to unlock a single new weapon or spell, it won't tell you what item you're buying until you spend gold on it, and the item might be trash. Item upgrades work the same, you have to buy expensive upgrades without knowing what they do and hope you just gambled on something useful.

Calamities are a system where if you take too much damage it fills up a gauge that spawns a ton more enemies on top of the enemies you're already fighting, as if losing most of your health in a tough fight wasn't a punishment in itself.

Once you start unlocking things the minimap is cluttered with icons for treasure you're not allowed to pick up because you haven't grinded a high enough level yet, and it will be gone forever before you hit that high level. There is no indication if an icon is for treasure you can or can't get.

The tutorial tells you information about Focus that is immediately, obviously wrong ("When Stamina is at max you are in Focus", in reality you can use Focus at 1/100 stamina). I spent hours trying to figure out how it worked, eventually realised my theory was wrong, and accepted that whether or not I had Focus was up to the whims of fate. This is on par for how well the game's mechanics are explained.

Weapon variety is nonexistent at first, you have one gun, but after many hours you'll unlock a nice arsenal that feels good to use, at least if you're within the arbitrary max range. There is some solid core gameplay here but it's buried under way too many frustrating design decisions.

review_text:
I really wanted to like this game but I just can't recommend it.

Everything is such a chore that its just not very fun.

The grid system limitations with stucture placement is very poor with no rotation and sometimes difficult to establish limits on where to place (flowers? really?) meaning that your village will take up much more space than it should.  

Then you have this annoying system whereby you have a certain number of villagers but actually can't assign them all (I could only assign 17 out of 19 villagers).  Furthermore, villagers will be quite happy to stand around doing nothing if you have not assigned them into the correct role.  
There is a good reason why almost every other RTS in existence has buildings auto produce goods with automatically assigned villagers.  If you build a wood cutter you also need to tell the woodcutter where to cut the wood otherwise they wont do it.  But the command you use for this ALSO means that your idle workers will cut wood too.  Why bother with a woodcutter in the first place you might ask?  (there is no reason - is the answer).  

Villagers will pick up bows and arrows but only occasionally use them to actually shoot anything, preferring to go hand to hand.

You have big bodies of fresh water yet have to put down a rain collector then water bottler? Huh?!

I think the problem with this game is it tries to be too many things at once and as a result none of its mechanics are particularly fun.  

If you want a colony builder get Rimworld
If you want a village simulator get Banished or one of the older Settlers
If you want a tower defence game - get one.
If you want a God game play Black & White or Populous

There is an item near the very front that gives you a brief "float" to be able to perform midair attacks. As I can't even get a refund for the game I'm deleting from my library permanently but not before I shared my thoughts on why this is not something I would recommend to anyone.

review_text:
I backed Scorn back in 2017 during the Kickstarter campaign, a few years later or maybe three i got access to the alpha demo. 

I really loved what I saw, but being an alpha, there were a few things that felt lacking. Granted, this was a small slice, but the core mechanics that made it into the full release were all there.

So I was sad to see that the combat aspects of the game really didn't evolve during that timespan. It was clunky, and didn't feel great during the alpha, and sadly this is what we got in the full release.

I really love the look, the feel of the world, the sounds, the music. It's all great stuff. But the combat encounters are just frustrating to the point where i kind of just wish there would be no combat at all.

I get that the game probably needed some suspension of some sort, but maybe there could have been some other element, instead of relying on "guns".

And maybe combat wouldn't have been so bad if the checkpoints weren't so messed up as well. Dying to do small sections over again, not to mention seeing the same slow animations (that were cool the first time) just gets exhausting.

The puzzles were nice for the most part, with one really annoying one, but I'm not a smart person, so maybe that was just my brain breaking itself trying to figure it out.

Overall, I have mixed feelings about the game. I do not regret backing it, and i enjoyed the game enough that i actually ended up finishing it on PC and Xbox Series X. But I'm not going to lie it's not a perfect game by any means, it's frustrating, doesn't control well and in general just mediocre.

But there are no other games out there that nail this biomechanical esthetic, and I guess that is what made my time with the game special.

Would I recommend it, no. At lest not if you are someone who gets frustrated easily. If you like me like the look of the world, maybe wait for a sale, and if you are just interested in seeing the sights and sounds, use a puzzle guide to save yourself some time.

I got this game in early access for $30. It was a great, if simple game early on. As the updates progressed and the launch of 1.0 drew near, things began to deteriorate rapidly. Updates began being a lot more buggy and having performance issues. The engine transition to UE5 made things a lot more unstable and messy overall. After 1.1 the game is in a pretty sorry state. Optimization and stability is horrible, the game crashes almost every every time I launch it, the bug animations are stiff and clunky, and I swear bugs have been double or triple hitting players per animation as you no longer have the ability to get surrounded and extricate yourself or have amazing final stands like before way back in early access. You get surrounded, you're dead instantly regardless of class and difficulty.

review_text:
Overall, PSO2NGS is a great game for anime/manga fans. Here's my review:

Story - This game is catered to anime fans of course, and the story is.. well.. decent. Not the best anime story in a game, but also not the worst. At certain parts of the story campaign it drags on and on to the point you will want to skip through dialog. Just like a lot of anime stories, it tends to over-explain things, which just increases the dialog time and decreases the play time. I noticed myself getting bored with the story about midway through. Your mileage may vary. But who really plays these kinds of games for the story anyway?

Classes - This is one of the things I love most about PSO2NGS. Classes are diverse and most offer a variety of weapons so you aren't stuck using the same weapon the whole time. You also have the option to have a Sub-Class, which is nice because you get the benefits of that classes abilities/buffs as well as your main class's. And it allows you to use another set of weapons, increasing your options. What's even better is that you can completely change up your class and sub-class anytime you like! So you'll never get bored with your fighting style. There are multiple options for melee, mid range, and long range fighting styles depending on your class as well. So you can find the perfect combo of class and sub-class to fit your playing style.

Style - This game is FILLED with style options, and everything can be had for free! Yes, there are AC scratch tickets that require real money to use, but most of the items end up in the game's marketplace for free.. of course some items are priced for ridiculous amounts of gold.. so you'll need to farm a lot of gold to go the free route. I absolutely love the style in this game tho. You can, if you choose, just spend all your time playing dress up if you like.. "forget the monsters, I want to focus on fashion today! n.n" PSO2NGS also offers a lookbook system that allows you to save your outfits and share them with the community. The fashion scene is pretty big in this game, and for good reason!

Customize-ability of Characters - You have a bunch of options here as well. You can spend hours in the salon changing just about ever aspect of your character. No 2 PSO2NGS characters are alike, unless it's on purpose lulz. There is no standard avatar or anything like that. You can generally choose from a few different body types and head shapes, and then you can customize them with sliders/graphs to your heart's content. You could even put male heads on female bodies or vice versa if that's your thing! (eww). Eye color, hairstyles, color, body shape, etc can all be changed at anytime with the use of salon passes or star gems. When you first start out, salon passes may be few and far between, ,but don't worry, overtime you'll collect quite a few from just playing the game and receiving campaign items from Sega. N-color change passes allow you to change the colors of clothing, which you will also collect and stack up over time for free.

End Game - So once you finish the story there isn't a whole lot to do other than daily tasks, hang with friends, create fashion, try new weapons, classes, build up your weapons and armor, collect titles, collect animations such as dances and poses and idles... yeah.. there's a lot to still do in the game lulz. You can run triggers, leciel, nameless city, etc as well if you need dungeon type content to do. But generally for me I do my daily tasks, work on my outfits, and chat/hangout and/or shop the marketplace for new clothes/hair/accessories/animations. End game in PSO2NGS can be as chill as you like, or as grindy as you like. You just need to understand your options. Most of the time just doing your daily tasks and alliance tasks is enough to keep you busy for a bit as well as to earn you gold and free scratch tickets. Sega introduces new Limited Time Quests as well that offer special rewards mostly every week. And since I have been playing, there has always been some kind of festival with special tasks to do until the last couple weeks where one just ended. 

TLDR - Give this game a try if you like anime style games, fashion, farming, and chatting. PSO2NGS has a lot to offer just about everyone. And if you get bored with NGS, you can always go and play PSO2.. the original version of the game. It's not bad despite being old. Bottom line is, you're not going to know if you like this game or not until you give it a try. And if you feel lost, feel free to ask the community for help. Most people are very nice and helpful, and there is also a healthy YouTube community to help you improve and learn the game. But don't feel pressured to grind this game, take you time and just enjoy it for what it is.

this game is filled with style options, and everything can be had for free! yes, there are ac scratch tickets that require real money to use, but most of the items end up in the game's marketplace for free.. of course some items are priced for ridiculous amounts of gold.. so you'll need to farm a lot of gold to go the free route. i absolutely love the style in this game tho. you can, if you choose, just spend all your time playing dress up if you like.. forget the monsters, i want to focus on fashion today! n.n pso2ngs also offers a lookbook system that allows you to save your outfits and share them with the community. the fashion scene is pretty big in this game, and for good reason! customize-ability of characters - you have a bunch of options here as well. you can spend hours in the salon changing just about ever aspect of your character. no 2 pso2ngs characters are alike, unless it's on purpose lulz. there is no standard avatar or anything like that. you can generally choose from a few different body types and head shapes, and then you can customize them with sliders graphs to your heart's content. you could even put male heads on female bodies or vice versa if that's your thing! eww . eye color, hairstyles, color, body shape, etc can all be changed at anytime with the use of salon passes or star gems. when you first start out, salon passes may be few and far between, ,but don't worry, overtime you'll collect quite a few from just playing the game and receiving campaign items from sega. n-color change passes allow you to change the colors of clothing, which you will also collect and stack up over time for free. end game - so once you finish the story there isn't a whole lot to do other than daily tasks, hang with friends, create fashion, try new weapons, classes, build up your weapons and armor, collect titles, collect animations such as dances and poses and idles... yeah.. there's a lot to still do in the game lulz. you can run triggers, leciel, nameless city, etc as well if you need dungeon type content to do. but generally for me i do my daily tasks, work on my outfits, and chat hangout and or shop the marketplace for new clothes hair accessories animations. end game in pso2ngs can be as chill as you like, or as grindy as you like. you just need to understand your options. most of the time just doing your daily tasks and alliance tasks is enough to keep you busy for a bit as well as to earn you gold and free scratch tickets. sega introduces new limited time quests as well that offer special rewards mostly every week. and since i have been playing, there has always been some kind of festival with special tasks to do until the last couple weeks where one just ended. tldr - give this game a try if you like anime style games, fashion, farming, and chatting. pso2ngs has a lot to offer just about everyone. and if you get bored with ngs, you can always go and play pso2.. the original version of the game. it's not bad despite being old. bottom line is, you're not going to know if you like this game or not until you give it a try. and if you feel lost, feel free to ask the community for help. most people are very nice and helpful, and there is also a healthy youtube community to help you improve and learn the game. but don't feel pressured to grind this game, take you time and just enjoy it for what it is.

review_text:
I wanted to like this a lot more than I did.

The art style is adorable. Seeing various characters wandering around town always brought a smile to my face. Aging, disease, death, and a bit of randomness in the economic structure made for an interesting combination. There are so many things that set up for an interesting scenario.

However... the game largely feels empty. There isn't much point to generations. Rushing to marry a random NPC and have kids is primarily a function to increase how much watering you can do in your farm. On one hand, it's very nice that there is a reason to tackle that challenge. On the other, relationships of both platonic and romantic nature are just kind of /there/ and not really needed.

It's not really a social simulator. Due to the nature of the generations, especially with fast aging, more and more characters from a pool will appear and dialogue is taken based on what "type" of character it is. An example that comes to my mind is Animal Crossing. An odd gimmick arises as well because of the generational and dying aspect, and that is male pregnancy. Anyone regardless of their physical sex is able to produce a child in order to ensure there will always be more NPCs appearing in the town.

There's a lot of good ideas here and the foundation exists, but ultimately the emptiness of the game makes it hard to invest in. A pretty package with not much inside.

A fun little game that can be cleared in a day or less. The combat feels nice and continuing is not too hard, but checkpoints don't restore health which means continuing is painful sometimes. 

One criticism I will level at the game is that if you want the best ending you have to actively refrain from opening chests that grant some very useful equipment, which means spending the majority of the game underpowered. While this is an appropriate level of challenge for the "golden ending", it takes the form of a side quest with no indication that this side quest is crucial to attaining said golden ending. Worse is that the reward is very mediocre gameplay-wise by the time you get it, so people who don't look up guides/don't care about the story will feel disappointed by this. 

Combat balancing is rather...iffy. As mentioned earlier, if you follow the side quest then you'll probably spend the majority of the game running away from enemies as there are no experience, gold can't get you good equipment (which is where most of the gameplay benefits come from). On the other hand, if you ignore said quest and open every chest you find, you will soon discover some very broken combo like infinite mana regen which makes most bosses a cakewalk. This can be achieved before fighting the third story boss. But if you're into min-maxing strats then this is an obvious buy.

review_text:
The game is certainly enjoyable and so right off the bat, I will recommend it, but this has certain caveats.

First, I'll go through the pro's:
- The storyline is enjoyable.  Cheesy, but enjoyable
- The combat is fun.
- The graphics are nice and just about what you would expect.  They are not amazing by any stretch, but they more than suit for a JARPG (not sure if that's a real genre, but eh...)
- The music, whilst repetitive, suits the game/world.

Now for the cons:
- Complete lack of control over your characters progression.  This is following a specific story and whilst that's fine, it would've been nice to rebuild Haseo in some manner of your own choosing.
- The grind...  Now, for me, this wasn't too bad.  I enjoyed the combat enough that I didn't mind grinding it out, but if that kind of thing bores you, you're in for a rough time.
- No real replayability as it's pretty much a linear path through the game.  My played time is currently at 86 hours and I believe my first play through took around 76 of those.
- Would be nice to view emails etc without having to leave the game-proper.  It happens often enough that it can get annoying having to log out and back in again.

So like I say, it's an enjoyable game and I don't believe I could bring myself to not recommend a game I spent close to a hundred hours playing, but it won't be for everyone.

I would also say that the voice actor to Haseo (at least for dub) is different than in .Hack//Roots (although it might be worth watching this before playing the game as this is a continuation from the show) and also the final volume went from very smooth cut scenes to really choppy and badly edited ones.  Otherwise it does do something to close off the story a bit more.

review_text:
STO is that game that you can't put down and before you know it you're out of time and out of money.

But seriously, if you love Trek and know what you're doing gameplay-wise, it's easy and fun to get into. The gameplay leans more into the combat then most Trekkies would prefer, but I'll take what I can get; besides, it's not like it's called an RPG for nothing. In addition, the story writing is really well done and the celebrity voice cast (and most of the non-celebrity voice cast) show that Cryptic may be trying to make a quick buck, but at least they care enough to give a quality product at the same time. If money is an issue, exercise restraint and either grind the later difficulties, or just don't play. The game is more enjoyable if you lay down a little money for a ship you like and did research on, plus it makes the harder episodes much easier (and enjoyable). Besides. it's a f2p game, what did you expect, a free ride to the end? It's a long road, getting from here to there, and Cryptic needs to stay a float, so be thankful STO is still going with good consistent writing (except for the STD and Klingon House storylines, those were absolutely atrocious; only play those if you have a friend to play them through with, it makes them bearable and comedic).

All in all, give it a try, just remember it's free to play, and over a decade old; graphics updates can only hide so much. However, with the new high-detailed ship model updates and continued well written episodes, the best time to start was yesterday, the nest best time is right now!

review_text:
Rise to Ruins has been a delightful surprise in the Early Access scene, offering a refreshing mix of strategy and survival elements. From the moment I started building my first village, I was hooked by the game's ability to balance resource management with the thrill of tower defense.

The game presents a world where corruption spreads, and monsters threaten your villagers, adding a layer of tension to the otherwise peaceful task of building and expanding. The attention to detail in the pixel artstyle is commendable, and the music sets a perfect tone for the atmosphere of the game.

One of the standout features is the villagers themselves, who have distinct needs and behaviors, making the management aspect deeply engaging. The introduction of a lifespan for villagers adds a new layer of strategy, as you must balance their immediate needs with the long-term health of your community.

The tower defense component is challenging and rewarding, with the game cleverly ramping up the difficulty as you progress. The ability to share resources and villagers between multiple villages on the overworld map is a welcome addition that adds to the game's complexity and depth.

While the game is still in Early Access, the developer has shown a commitment to updating and improving the game, which is promising for its future. Rise to Ruins is a gem that offers a lot of bang for your buck, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone looking for a game that combines strategy, management, and a touch of retro charm.

review_text:
To the moon was actually created as a PHD project as a tool to screen for psychopaths i.e. those that lack empathy, so if you’re not a fan of this game, congratulations psycho, you should be worried.

Tears. So many tears playing this.
I revisit this game every year, and every year I seem to cry a bit more. It was more than a game to me, by the end of it I really felt like I was there experiencing what the characters were experiencing.

I'm in my mid 30s, and two grueling battles with cancer have left me severely pessimistic about the future. I have been fortunate for now, but at any moment I know it could come back and I’m not sure I would be long for this world if I have to fight like that for a third time. So this game hit so close to home. I think about how I would feel again. How I'd love to relive my life, the happy moments, even the sad. My first love, getting to know my dad again after he quit drinking, holding my brother's daughter the first time as a baby. Even just roleplaying through it again would be so soothing.

God no matter how many times I play this game, that bittersweet ending will always get to me. To the Moon is my second, maybe third favorite game of all time. I am a different, better person for having played it. You will never forget this in your life after you finish it.

To the moon is a point & click/interactive visual novel in which you play as two scientists, who visit a dying man. Your task is to fulfill his last wish: to go to the moon. But to do this, you need to find out what made him want this. You essentially experience his life backwards from a third person perspective. The game play isn't challenging at all, as it's fully a story-driven game. The plot and the music are the main attractions that'll stay with you for years after you finish the game. The sequels are good, too, albeit IMO not quite as good as the original.

You explore places to find various clues or items that help you learn more about the story, and talk to or watch interactions between characters. There are also recurring puzzle mini games, though those are not meant to be the main focus— they mainly just give you breaks from the story to think about what has happened and try to piece together answers. Additionally, the games can also derail into other “joke” mini games (like trying to do a turn-based-rpg fight against a squirrel, or something equally silly). There is only one instance of ‘silly mini-games’ in the series in which your success or failure substantially influences the direction of the story; even for that one, failing it doesn’t give you a ‘bad ending’.

As for the writing, one of the game's main themes is asperger syndrome/high-functioning autism and how it affects personal relationships. That's a pretty unique premise for a video game and it does a great job conveying the emotions involves. A lot of western media just portrays AS as being an emotionless robot which is a wildly ignorant and outdated take. This game might not get it perfect, but it does a way better job than most of the representation out there. When people are praising games like Beyond Eyes for representation, the bar is pretty low.

One thing that stuck with me years after playing To The Moon was how bittersweet its ending was. It didn't sugarcoat how unambiguously sad were the lives that some of the cast got to experience. This game was not about the moment-by-moment, action-packed gameplay, but rather a slow, methodical journey showing how someone's past affects their state of mind. The main take away for me was about the incredible value that love injects into our lives. It was a game that surprised the player by having a compelling story rise above a standard RPGMaker elements; the simple graphics and twee dialog.

I think what made it work is how silly the game was in the majority of the story. Stuff like the main characters Dr. Rosalene using random vegetables as curse words and Dr. Watts shouting random pop-culture references from Dragon Ball Z and Hulk to hype himself up. Genuinely made me laugh a good amount despite the feels. It's the opposite of brilliant banter, but its very idiocy hit home for me. Because most people devolve approximately to this level of stupidity when they're letting their guard down with a friend. It's human nature to be stupid when you're trying to recover emotional energy: smartness takes a lot of effort. If you keep trying to find the smartest thing you could do when you're chilling out, then your "chilling out" isn't going to be very restful.

To The Moon is a bit like the Shoebox Project in this manner: it's cringeworthy in its stupidity, but adorable in how close it is to real communication between actual humans. Leave brilliant banter for pirate adventures and other works of deliberately unrealistic human interaction. This is slice-of-life. It has different literary standards. The game came out in 2011 anyhow, when that kind of random speech was at peak popularity in nerd subcultures. People may feel a certain way about the writing and the jokes, and I get that. Some of the humour didn’t age well. However, when the story hits a beat, it hit HARD for me. I remember going through dialogue between Rosalene and Watts during one of the big story beats, and just hitting this realization that explained the title of the game and reframed the whole story. Threw me for a loop.

If you’re looking for gameplay, this isn’t it. However, if you want an incredible story, then you found the first in a perfect series. It’s one of those games where you have to take the entire package into consideration when reviewing it. If you look at all the individual aspects of the game, it's kind of average/okay. But where it really shines is with its emotional impact. I highly recommend To the Moon. The story hit me really hard, and I hope I can get some more people to experience it.

10/10

This is my honest review about this game. Its not Helldivers 2 at first, but as you learn the ropes you start to realise that this is another game just like it, but just not as polished by a long shot. its the same game type as helldivers 2 basically but more older. 

i find its the same type of game like Planetside 2 as well with regards to the look., that game is 12 years old.  
If you can put up with this, Johnny Rico looks like a pirate not a marine, the bugs themselves can be a bit chaotic in their swarms, especially in your early game, the base building part can be a bit messy, but its fun to play and watch what others are doing with it.. The tutorial starts off not as well as it should. The map is good to ignore.. There are problems with this game but i took the risk to buy it to see if it was as as as others have said. Im enjoying it cause its the same game type as helldivers.

Ive played five hours straight and I can tell you you need it to appreciate the game. First off on a big score..the field of view setting in this game needs to go right up to get the bugs and screen mess out of your face. At first if you dont put this setting on highest you'll see screen mess all around you. 

I think the developers have limited the fov compared to other games on purpose, the highest setting is like 60% in other games.  As i said this game is not polished and it needs tweaking in the settings to be able to enjoy it.

 Im finding with a rtx 4070 that i am having fun on high settings with shadows medium, dlss on ultra performance v sync on, and field of view right up to 130%. This is working for me to get a game that is simillar in experience to helldivers 2. low settings on this game are a no no as it creates pixilated graphics.  You will have to sort the settings for yourself on your computer to be able to enjoy it like helldivers 2. But ive given ideas on what to change in the settings.  At first when i loaded it up it was screen mess and chaos and disorder but i tweaked it to sort it to play it as it was intedned but its taken a while to do that.

The bugs themselves, are swarming massively as they do in the movies at times and it can get quite messy and out of control, like really out of control in a maddennig way and you get blown up for some reason every so often - who dunnit players?.. bugs? .

review_text:
If I had to quickly summaries this game, I'd present it as "Far Cry meets Hitman."

Set in a semi-open world, you have five locations in wich you must eliminate a primary target with some secondaries objectives.

In my opinion the game's best strength is its level design, allowing you to choose how to kill your targets. You can snipe them from afar, get close up and stealthily execute them, or go in guns blazing and keep on shooting until the whole map is dead.
The environment is also another strong point, very detailed all while looking really good, and running without any issues.

For the gameplay, you start each mission with 3 weapons (sniper, Assault Rifle and pistol) and a number of gadgets that can be increased via skill points. Unfortunately, guns are rather lacking of personality and I ended up running the one's with the bests stats.
But even then I found shooting to still be satisfying, even if it doesn't hold a candle to games like COD 2019 or Insurgency.

Sound wise, the guns and general effects are good but the music is more of an "ambiance", not an OST that I would ever listen to outside of the game.
And then there's the voice acting. It's ok all around, but there are a few characters that are so over the top, so bad, it's actually good (in a Z movie kinda way)!

There are, however, a couple of negatives: AI and clipping.
Enemies are dumb, no matter the difficulty. They will run around like headless chickens while you pick them off one-by-one, will crouch on the wrong side of cover, etc.
Clipping is mostly an issue when trying to stealth. I have been stuck in front of a branch or by a crack on the ground right next to an enemy a few times too many, resulting in my swift death or alerting the whole level. Very frustrating.

Oh, and there's also a "story" that is completely forgettable and no more than a back drop for the missions.


All around, a good sniping power fantasy with great level design and visuals, somewhat hindered by poor AI and clipping issues.
Solid 7.5/10

review_text:
Good example of a very fun game with a thousand flaws.

The characters and bosses are all very stylish and the whole thing is a joy to look at.  The plot is predictable and not very memorable but it stands fine without it.  Exploring is a lot of fun due to the wild assortment of weapons, items, and accessories you can find.  You'll never feel like the game is wasting your time, because often what you'll discover is extremely useful for what is up ahead.  The huge assortment of practical collectibles and boss rewards gives a real sense of wonder and adds a lot of variety.

The downside to this is that it leads to a lot of menuing.  When you have a hundred weapons and accessories with specific uses, you'll feel obligated to swap them constantly to be gaining full advantage.  There is no restriction on this, meaning you can literally hit an enemy with a DPS setup and then swap to a defensive one during an attack phase.  It slows the gameplay to a crawl.

Additionally, there is a real problem with the combat in this game, in that weapon speed is far too overpowered.  The increased action delay on using a heavy weapon leaves you wide open, often getting your attacks interrupted completely since enemies tend to attack quickly.  Due to your very low health pool and relatively limited consumables, this is disastrous.  On top of this, faster weapons are better dps anyway, and you can often just stagger enemies and use your shield and counter, rather than trying to secure a larger opening.  It often feels like the optimal strategy is to force a boss into a corner and dagger them to death while spamming food.  The spell to slow projectiles also completely breaks half the bosses.

I should mention that upon completing the game, you unlock a game mode that removes weapons entirely and gives you a Castlevania 3 (or more recently, Curse of the Moon) setup with well-defined characters you swap between.  This actually removes the issue of having to menu weapons, and since the combat didn't make good use of the weapon selection anyway,  the game just feels much smoother.  Menuing accessories and food is still a problem, but it's better.  I wish that the game had been built with this as the main mode instead.

Despite all of this, the game is just fun.  

A thorough playthrough probably runs 10 hours or so, but boss mode was fun enough for me to sink in another several.
