review_text:
Once more evidence that we need a "meh" option rather than just recommend/dont.

GTTOD is fun, it has it's own visual style that should age well and it has decent gameplay loop but.. for 20 bucks there isn't much. Before I rant a bit, I'll just say game good but there's a lot of fixable gripes right now. 

So now for bullet list of those gripes.

There's only a handful of levels and this is apparently the update before 1.0, even if he did add another "act" of levels, the game would be incredibly short and still not worth 20 bucks.

There's only 2 real bosses and they're both melee focused with some ranged attacks, in a game where you're effectively a ninja monkey on 12 experimental enhancer drugs and that's without the upgrades. Yeah dev didn't think boss design that well.

Movement feels great as if you can speed and soar into the air, but the design of the levels seems to want to keep me to the ground. Yeah there are wall run spots everywhere but nothing screams verticality, anything that has a whimper of it fails to keep it consistent and the enemy ai..

The AI is simplistic completely. They just walk at you and do X attack. Some (IMP) try to do a unique position spot so they can spam ranged at you but a majority just walk at you even when they're range based. 

In addition the maps have MANY zones where the player can just be safe, regen shields and even throw grenades/c4 down at the enemy to wipe them. If the player wants to cheese the game it's incredibly easy to, even the bosses aren't immune to this.

The challenge area, abyss or whatever, is completely pointless beyond farming. There is no way to escape it that at least I could find, it's endless dropping that is completely disconnected from the main game's setup so.. why does it exist? It's not actually challenging, you're just dropped into a arena and kill a bunch of guys to get a reward. Since you can't return there's no reason to go into it on a normal run, its purely just to farm and for a rogue game that's... bad imo. The main game should facilitate said farm, not some side area. If anything it just further tells me that this Rogue-like aspect of it was tacked on.

There are many small tiny issues concerning sound design and animation, for instance many inspect animations do not have sounds yet and/or are very VERY basic animations while others have a full visual flare to them. Also inspect animation sounds and camera movement does not stop if you swap off weapon, funny.

The dev, for whatever insane reason that just contributes to the idea that he's just cobbling together ideas, added a fishing minigame. No wonder this game's taking so long to finish.

The game lets you acquire "card packs" from the get go at random, these are supposed to give cards that will, for one time, change your starting equipment. This mechanic is fine and I like the idea. What I don't like is the only way to access this is to level up your character about 3? 4? whole bars in the upgrade tree, which takes awhile since you dont have the challenge area to farm as it's also locked, just to get the guy who lets you use these cards to open. This "shop" should be open either from the get go or when the player finishes the first level up bar of the upgrade system. Not several.

I want to say I like this game, but all these minor gripes add up and the fact that they're touting a 20 dollar front and from what I can tell it was previously 15 bucks for even less content? Is horrible. This game is $10 MAX at current state and unless their fabled 1.0 update adds another 2-3 acts, it should never be above $15 after release.

And the funny thing is, I didn't even pay for it, my friend got me it as a gift, I still feel like it was overpriced. When 1.0 drops I'll check it out and redo the review, for now this is what I have to say : Get it on discount, and I mean a GOOD discount. UNLESS 

IMPORTANT Edit : As one small thing, despite my gripes with the CURRENT pricetag for the CURRENT content. The dev could use the money, if you feel the game deserves the money regardless, fuckit pay full price. After actually checking their discord and talking with the dev myself they seem like they actually do want to keep making the game better and better and I hope they can achieve that.

Lucius makes an erstwhile attempt to play upon the "son of the devil" trope, but in the end, makes the idea of being born with demonic powers seem... pretty boring, to be honest. It also seems rather trite that your father merely wants you to kill pretty much everyone in the house where you're being raised, rather than doing anything interesting with said powers. Worst Satan ever.

It's a shame Lucius fell short, really. There are some great death sequences in there, and some interesting storylines sprinkled in for a few characters, but most of those fail to deliver or are left dangling in the long run. A glorified puzzle game, Lucius mostly just has you running around the house to collect item combinations to finish setting up a death, like a series of vaguely evil Rube Goldberg machines. You're given a handful of powers, but they don't come into play particularly often, leaving one wondering why they're even there in the first place. As for your victims, it seemed kind of odd that some of the characters seemed to deserve their fates while others were complete innocents, which was confusing. I mean, if you're the devil's son, wouldn't it make more sense for almost all of your victims to be innocents? Or for them all to have filthy souls just begging for harvest? The blend of the two felt like a case of indecision more than anything else.

The chore completion aspect adds another layer of tedium as well. By completing different tasks given to you by the manor's various adult inhabitants, you can pass yourself off as a "good" boy and obtain a series of gifts to make your life easier. Of the three, I felt the Tricycle was the most useful in how it increased your movement speed (and looked kind of ridiculous, animation-wise), but it was the last of three I obtained, leaving only a few chapters in which I could even use it. I feel the "good boy" status could have been better used as a way of lowering suspicion rather than just a method of procuring handouts.

Between the tedium of each chapter and what feels like a lot of wasted potential, I can't really recommend Lucius. I finished it, but it was more a matter of just headbutting my way through more than anything else. Meh.

TL:DR - Good game play, too many bugs, no good way to look for people to play with. Game's been out for two years so it feels neglected.

The game play itself is pretty good. It's not too dark or hard to reload weapons, there are different maps that have very different layouts and some different game modes so there's a variety of things to try out.

The reason I wouldn't recommend this game is that this game has been out for two years but it feels like it still isn't fully developed yet. There are TONS of bugs, many will cause you to lose the last minutes or hours of your life because you lose any rewards you've earned when certain bugs hit you. Also, their party system is still almost non existent so good luck looking for a group to play with. I often load up the the game, check for any parties looking another player and then leave feeling like no one is playing.
Their party system is really bad. The majority of the game is you going on runs to collect rewards and work towards improving your customized weapons. However, the runs must be run with 4 people and the game will fill out the party with computer controlled characters if your party is missing people. The problem with this is that computer controlled characters are very weak and won't work well in the higher difficulty. The game has no way to actually see who's looking for a party or has a party looking for more players. 
Here's how the party system works, you chose your play mode, level and your difficulty and you tell the game you're ready. If someone else did this before you with the same difficulty, then you'll join their party. If there's no one else, then you create an empty party and you can wait or continue with computer controlled characters. Because there's so many difficulties, levels, and play modes, you end up creating a party over and over in each possible combination that you want to play. You can see people in the "lobby" and invite them to join but what often happens is that the person invited is not a fit for the run you want to do; for example, I was running a very high level run in a very hard mode and two of the people in the party were very inexperienced and under equipped. This actually happens often and the other players usually carry the team. 
Finally, the game feels neglected. Bugs are around for months if not years and features like a good party system seem like a pipe dream. This game has been out for two years now but it feels like a 3-6 month old game. This game feels like it has a lot of potential until you realize it's a two+ year old game, then it feels neglected.

Here's an example of a bug that should have been fixed immediately: In Sep 2022, they released a update that caused one of the guns to become extremely over powered. As of Jan 2023, the weapon is still exploited by almost everyone. This over powered gun makes the purpose of the runs obsolete; why bother trying to find improvements for other weapons when this one gun makes every other gun look like a cap gun?

review_text:
The game mechanics are pretty decent for a Left 4 Dead style VR shooter, and the optimization is pretty decent. The shooting feels nice and aiming is purposefully a little sluggish to help you stabilize shots (it's hard to explain, but it's almost like trying to aim underwater a little bit. It isn't tedious and actually helps against the jitter often seen in these VR shooters. This is a big positive). It's also one of the few games where when I throw an item, it actually goes where I intended it to go, another common issue in VR games. Returning from launch, a couple of things have changed since launch. a handful of guns were added, the grind eased up a little bit (it's still an extremely grindy and luck-dependant game, just not as much anymore), manual reloading has been improved but is still finicky and forces you to often crash your VERY expensive controllers together every so often, and horde mode was added along with one new mission and mutations to old missions that change daily.

There are still many issues, however. The AI bots are still completely worthless, won't pick up items, can't aim, and will actively protect zombies by constantly blocking your shots. Remember to mute NPC voices in your setting to protect your sanity against the AI constantly complaining their face is blocking your bullets. Because of this, you'll be subject to the games community, which is a hit or miss. There are some people who will help you along the way you'll have a great time, but most of the time people will hotmic shitty music, be on the phone, complain, pester, whine, scream, bicker, refuse to communicate, run off on their own to die, try to command your every action, and/or will not speak English. This isn't much of a fault of the game developers but god damn does it ruin the experience. Gun stats and upgrades are often extremely vague and true values hidden in patch notes, which isn't very helpful when you're trying to modify your guns to suit your needs and it's extremely frustrating when the game refuses to give you upgrades for your favorite gun, while you've managed to unlock everything for a gun you never want to use. The content in the game also gets old very quickly, and the devs seem to have a very slow pace adding new ones.

Overall, this game, even after all of the updates in the last couple of months, is STILL not even close to being worth 40 bucks. If you're someone who's fortunate enough to have 3 other friends who often play VR games and are also willing to play this game, I can see this game being an absolute blast. Unfortunately, if you're like me who's only got one friend like that, and have to choose between the horrible AI or horrible people, this game is a hard pass.

review_text:
Murders, slaughter, looting, a plague that decimates the entire town, corpses, mass graves, war, deception, dead babies, hangings—this is all present in Pathologic 2, and even more horrifying stuff! 

The rules of this world are brutal and complex, punishing the player for even the slightest moment of negligence. Money, inflation, thirst and the search for food will be a constant problem. Should you break into a house and steal a piece of bread, risking the life of a household member or your own? Should you trade your so important tools with children for a boiled egg, just so you could survive for little while? Planning your route to avoid bandits and infected areas of the town will add pressure to save as many people from the plague as possible, with time running out. If hunger overwhelms you, or you get killed by a bandit or plague, the game punishes you for your death, complicating the rest of your playthrough without the option to reload without consequences (the penalty remains for all previous saves) or taking something unessential for your progress, but important for you (like the ability to hug someone). 

Chance to lose the ability to hug someone, and a feeling of dread after learning that you can't do that anymore, is the power of Pathologic 2, because it makes you care for its characters.

Beneath all this nightmare, lies an innocence and warmth that can only exist in a child's mind, or some kind of children's game. A polyhedron defying gravity, inhabited solely by children; a mountain-sized bull named Bos Turokh; Characters that look like villains but are actually gentle and good; worm-people; time travel, prophet rats, ghosts...

This conflict between the rational and irrational horror, and the world of childhood, warmth, and the possibility of change and growth, makes the world of Pathologic 2 so convincing and real! Its brutality in gameplay is justified by the tenderness it shows towards its characters. As a haruspax, a surgeon, you, the player, genuinely want to save these people from the plague. You want to save them all. At first, you don't even know why, because the game draws you into its magic so quickly. It compels you to believe in it.

No matter how hard you fight, or what choice you make when it comes to that (and in the end, a tough choice awaits you), you can’t save everyone. And the game teaches you that. And it hurts.

Don't bother. This game is extremely underdevelopped for a Dwarf Fortress: Fortress Mode tower defense with some god game features. This is just a hodge podge of underdevelopped features sprinkled from lots of different game genres, with underdevelopped AI. It is also apparently at the end of its lifecycle, as the single developper has multiple times explained away incredibly slow development for the making of another game.

Development may have started again, and it might be good one day, but I don't thnk so as the problem is with its game design rather than the features. Go play Rimworld with mods or Dwarf Fortress with a tileset and Dwarf Therapist instead. This game doesn't deserve your time at all, there is no complexity to sink your teeth into here, only frustration at a wierd mix between no useful micromanagement, and having to micromanage the individual ways you interact with the game so you don't fuck yourself over because of it's incredibly dumb AI. The game is made to be played in one way, and one way alone.

It's trying to be everything at one.... to be played in one way.

Edit after some extra playtime: Yep, still the same problems, no update for a year and a half now. I give up.
Edit after dev restarted: It's still the same. There's a few new features but it doesn't seem like the dev will be fixing any of the very core problems with this.
Mid 2023 update: It's a dead half-finished game. No update for over a year. I expected this. I will be avoiding the dev in the future.

review_text:
This is not going to be an entirely negative review, but if you've heard the hype about this game, depending on what you're looking for, you may or may not be disappointed.

Pros:

Good music
Touching story (did get a little emotional towards the end)
Good sense of humour
Decent dollar per hour value if you buy it on sale, but at full price I cannot recommend a buy

Cons:

Gameplay not overly interesting or challenging - find some things in the environment and then do a flip puzzle to advance to the next story sequence, only really switches it up a bit at the end.
Somewhat goofy, and often simply written dialogue
I found myself needing to use the keyboard/mouse in some situations - can't be played entirely with a controller in my experience

Overall, I found myself just wanting the game to hurry up and be over.  It was a unique experience, but it didn't make me want to play the sequel, and I may not finish the two free minisodes.

review_text:
I've been a big fan of Hakuouki since the PSP version came out and I was really looking forward to playing it with all the promised new content. But as much as I love it, I can't recommend this version for multiple reasons.

First: This is not the whole game; it is roughly two thirds of the story and the part that was called the 'common route' in the original game. And it ends when any romance option you may have achieved with your decisions just starts to bloom. Since Edo Blossoms is out already, you can continue on the spot, but you are forced to buy a second game to get the whole story.

Second: It is not a romantic story. As mentioned above, this game covers the ‘common route’ and that means you only get a glimpse of budding romance right before it ends. As it is set in a time when Japan renewed itself in a bloody civil war, there are many dark aspects you will discover. And as if the times weren’t grim enough then, the game adds even more dark stuff to that, so if you are unlucky with your decisions, you can have a very dark, very depressing experience. Also, the game wants to tell the story of the Shinsengumi and their fight in those stormy times, so prepare for a long history lesson. I loved it, but I’m a history geek and quite in love with the past of Japan. I just wanted to warn you in case this is not your cup of tea.

Third: The translation. Oh God, the translation… I know that not everyone knows Japanese and would (or would want to) notice this, but I’m already at the point where it really hurts reading the subtitles. And my Japanese isn’t all that good, so I’m sure there is even more than what I've spotted so far. It’s not only that the men ‘sound’ so much more aggressive and ill-willed in the text and that it often doesn’t fit with how they talk in Japanese. I understand that this may be due to localizing the game for a Western audience. But there are translation mistakes even in really short, easy sentences where the meaning is completely garbled and even some instances where it felt like they had given up on translating altogether and just invented some stuff that seemed fitting for the scene. And even the English sentences often have grammar mistakes that forced me to interpret more than read. I expect more from a VN of this caliber, especially for this price.

And last: Neither the developer nor the publisher seems to have any interest in their game here on Steam apart from how much money it makes them. There are some issues with the performance of the game that are still unaddressed. I didn’t have any issues except for the small bug that the characters don’t say my heroine’s name when using the default ‘Chizuru’. But even that is still open, no response from anyone working on the game as far as I could see in the discussions.

So, even though I love Hakuouki, I can sadly only tell you this: If you are one of the few people who own a PSP, try to find the original game. The translation of that was not perfect either, maybe it wasn’t even good, but sadly it was still better than what we get here. And I still prefer the art of the original game, especially with regard to the uniforms. It was gorgeous. To be fair the art in this new version of the game is one of the few good points it has. It still looks beautiful. But that is not enough, so I have to give this a thumbs down. I’m so sad right now…

review_text:
In general, there are two completely different main characters in the Story.
We start playing for the first one and then for the second one.
The world of sorrow is a world of absolute inequality. There is a higher race -
these are those beings who look like "Engineers" from "aliens", they are born
in special capsules similar to tiaras, in the Genesis Tower.
There is also an average race - these are servants. Both of our heroes belong to this particular race.
And there is also a lower race - these are Moldmen, they are essentially biological raw materials.
Homunculi, classified as an inferior race, also stand apart.
So, our first hero was initially infected with a parasitic infection.
And he was in a hurry to turn on the power in the Genesis Tower in order to awaken the Engineers who were dozing
in their tiaras. He needed this for two reasons: first
, that only Engineers could cure him of a parasitic infection,
and second, that he was still a devoted servant and wanted to restore
his masters to their former greatness.
He made his way to the Bioreactor in the Genesis Tower with great difficulty, but
unfortunately the Bioreactor was damaged during the attempt.

review_text:
The best part of BioShock series so far, simply a masterpiece. Sure, the gameplay's solid, smooth, fun, and plasmids system are quite innovative, but that's not what makes "Bioshock" a masterpiece; it's the story. You get a chance to see that a world without morals are doomed to fail, even so beautiful, like Rapture.
Dont be lazy to pick up all the audio, or you will miss the most intersting parts of the plot.
>A man plays Bioshock, a slave plays League of Legends.
>In the thick of of bleak and obtuse FPS games, flooded all stocks and minds, Bioshock felt like a blessing from above. Ken Levine made his brightest shot into the eternity. Bioshock is a Magnum Opus. A real deal stuff. A resurrection of System Shock principles with the isogenic battle system (mixture of guns, guts, wits and magic), with modern, looking-better-than-Half-Life-2-graphics, and deep, dark, sound and comprehensive story. Again mankind was looking for salvation, but drowned itself by ever-growing sins like greed, powerlust, and false infallibility.

A miraculous experience of witnessing the end of time and humanity. A travel to mad scientist inner space. A nice reason to forget about sleep, in my book.

Mark is 8.5/10: the narrative falls down a little in the very end, and there are some other distracting little things on the way through Rapture, that keeps me from praising Bioshock as "the-best-my-eyes-ever-seen!" title. But it is still a brilliant of game design, totally worth of your time.

review_text:
Tl;dr this game is a losing simulator. You will unavoidably lose. There is literally no way to win. This isn't a "gid gud" scenario, you will lose every time, by design.

I refrained from writing a review for this game because I didn't want to hinder its progress, just in case the dev wanted to change the direction of the game. It's very sad that I have to say no, but I will explain underneath the reasons why.

The game is really cool until you realize what the gameplay cycle is. I haven't played it in a while but I saw some comments and it seems it's still the same.

The game isn't difficult. It's impossible by design. I don't mind difficult games. But the whole formula of this game is so that you lose. Let me explain this:

1. The monsters never stop levelling up. Your buildings however have a max level. Therefore there will be a time (and it's not gonna take long) where the monsters overlevel your buildings (and keep on levelling up!). It doesn't even matter how many towers you build, after some time they will be so far ahead that you do 0 damage to them.

2. The corruption spreads, the more you play until it covers the entire map. The more it spreads, the more enemies get spawned. So that means you gotta fight it back right? No. If you fight it back, the game becomes more difficult. So you fight it back to make the game easier, but the game becomes harder instead. But even if you don't fight it back, you're in the way remember? Therefore once it reaches your city, then you are unavoidably fighting it back by simply existing lol. Therefore the game becomes even harder.

3. There is one way to win a map. To do nothing but head to the corruption immediately. When you remove it from the last tile, it won't spawn any monsters. This is more of an exploit than a design though, and if you do that it becomes clear why the dev didn't want you to win. Because that's it. Once you are able to play the game freely, there's nothing to it. Everything is geared towards protecting yourself from the monsters, and defending. So once you do that, the game has nothing else to offer. But read my previous points: the formula of the game is to make you lose. So there's no point in even defending then.

4. You can move your people nomadically to other tiles on the world map. Therefore you might assume that the point is defending and gather resources, move elsewhere, gather more resources, move elsewhere etc, until you're tough enough to start actually fighting the corruption. No. That would make the game cool actually. But that's not its point. Because remember, no matter how many resources you have, the enemies do not have a max level, therefore will always overpower you. Even if we imagined you have infinite resources, your towers at some point will do no damage.

5. TD element. The game initially had this, and it was great. Basically you were supposed to build a maze of towers. That's why there are also slow towers and stuff like that. The enemies would not attack walls unless they had no way of reaching your town. But after some update, the monsters would start attacking the walls anyway, therefore negating this completely. So in the end, you're stuck with towers that's counter-productive to build. Why have a slow tower, if you could build another elemental/arrow/ballista tower? There's no point.

6. God powers. Initially, they matter. But after a while, they are so weak that you are stuck with casting stuff like regenerating resources - mainly food. Also, charm, if I remember, you can take any enemy under your command. So to win, reach the corruption fast, then when a high level fire elemental is spawned, charm it. Do that until you remove the last tile. 

7. Upgrading God powers: So you can upgrade certain stuff by mainly doing stuff in the game. These are the "goals", and it can increase your max levels and stuff. Wonderful huh? Therefore, you can at some point overpower the enemies, right? No. We already talked about how enemies' levels are infinite. By finishing a goal, you will, like, upgarde the level of something by 1. Golems if I remember. One level doesn't mean much. The enemies by then will probably be 10 levels ahead already, if you're lucky.

8. The dev doesn't care about these problems. It's been posted time and time again that the game has no purpose, as it's designed so that you lose. Everyone says this. I went to the comments just now to see if anything changed, and I found a comment from 1 hour ago that says the game is unfair etc.

Look, I don't want an easy game, by no means. I'm happy with a challenge, even if I lose, because then I know more stuff so I can replay and be better. But this isn't a challenge. This is a losing simulator. Actually, what will happen is that you will replay and replay, and at some point you will realize my previous points and give up, because there is no way to win the game.

And just as you're thinking the dev is gonna take notice and do this game justice, they release it from Early Access without "fixing" anything. And I use quotes because I don't think the dev sees these as problems, I really think the dev wanted the game to be impossible. But I don't know why, this game could be cool. Please remember, and I'll say this again and again, your skill doesn't matter. This isn't a "git gud" scenario. You will lose every time because that's how the game is designed.

So anyway, yeah, my advice is to steer clear of this game unless for some reason you really want to lose.

In conclusion, the game isn't horrific.. but it is highly disappointing and not worth it's pricetag

review_text:
SPOILERS IN REVIEW


This game has a lot going for it. Up until the final act it's an incredibly enjoyable well-paced experience. The amount of Batman villains you interact with is impressive in itself. The penguin, Mr.Freeze, Two-Face, the Joker, Harley Quinn, Hugo Strange, Ras al Ghul, The Mad Hatter, Deadshot, The Riddler, Bane, Zsasz, Solomon Grundy, Calendar Man, Clayface. Looking at that sheer amount of villains, all more or less in great form, it's downright impressive the scope of the game. However, as you go on the game starts to show its cracks. 


You tie things up very hastily and with a weird end with Mr.Freeze and the third act begins. Suddenly a well paced story throws all the plot points out the window and you have no new interactions with main villains just sitting in buildings across the map. The mastermind Strange's plan to threaten Batman and take over from the inside and coordinate such an amazing end is here... and his plan is to drop bombs on convicts. That's seriously it. That's protocol 10, that's the entire buildup. Entire story threads are abandoned, Jokers blood in hospitals, Strange knowing Bruce's identity, why Titan is even in this game, why Harley is even in this game, the gang war between Two-Face, Penguin and the Joker. All of these are just left hanging, making you wonder why they were even introduced. 



Now you're at "The AAA End" fighting Hugo Strange, you punch him once and he's beaten, then Ras al Ghul comes in and immediately kills Strange and then dies as an immortal person, then Talia dies by Joker. Two seconds later Joker is clayface and then you kill Clayface and then next second Joker dies, and with his dead love on the ground Batman carries out Jokers body, never saying a single word about any of the events of the last 3 hours. The entire end sequence is probably about 5 minutes total in runtime. No comments about any of the events at the end of the game. Then the game ends, cut to black screen. Really? That's what everything was leading up to. 

Oh, but you have the GOTY edition so you're immediately Catwoman fighting Two-Face in maybe the worst section in the game which cannot end fast enough with 2 words spoken by Two-Face. Now you're Batman again and you're back in the city for some reason still without ANY comment on the events of the game resolving (not really). It's very hard to see why anyone would find satisfaction out of beating this game


There's a LOT to love in City, but all that love, provided you're doing the side content as it comes up instead of the main story first, is all in the first 2/3 of the game. Almost none of that is waiting for you in the ending act. The last act of the game is so rushed and breakneck-paced and wraps up with such a sloppy and fast resolution it makes the rest of the game look bad. I'd be surprised, if I counted, if they spent more than 20 seconds on the Joker dying, I'd be even more surprised if they spent more than ACTUALLY 3 seconds on Batman having the love of his life die in front of him. There's not a single line about any of this, there's nothing in the main game saying or acknowledging or commenting on any of the entire back end of the game where it does so for the rest. 


It really seems like they got to the end of the game and had to slap it together, it's so bad at the end that I got whiplash hearing about the spotless record this game holds with people with how poor and completely half-baked the entire ending of this game is and how all the care given  to the world in City before the ending is completely gone. Despite the bombings, and Joker's death and Strange's death and Ras Al Ghul and Talia Al Ghul's death and Protocol 10 and the city in ruins none of the villains care in their respective places, there are no new developments. Instead they all leave off at this weird intersection where you lock most of them away and they have nothing else to say. It feels so hollow, where the game is leading in the middle act to the beginning of the end is so interesting and they throw all that out at the end. 


And the women in this game, I cannot believe I hadn't heard someone mention it before. Every. Single. Woman has maxed out sliders, every single woman is overtly sexualised even if they don't get a name. Harley Quinn is a damsel, Catwoman a few times is a damsel, Talia is a damsel. The amount of times the word 'bitch' is thrown out in the few times women are centered in this story is pretty shocking. Really am wondering what Rocksteady was doing reducing some of the most iconic women characters to footnotes to objectify and put in the background, only pulling them forward to call them a bitch. I mean hell, Bruce is literally trying to let THOUSANDS DIE because he loves Talia so much and yet she dies practically off-screen, she is killed and they spend maybe 2 seconds and a short quip about it. The game also ignores that you leave her body and walk out with the Joker's over hers. WHAT was Rocksteady thinking with that end. 


You have all these pieces, you have all these thematic ties and interesting ways you can tell the devs read the comics and had all the little details in the world and yet it says nothing with the themes. It does nothing with them, there is 0 exploration of any of the central themes of batman in an entire story about Batman. The writing is so shoddy the further you go, and Bruce is actually just a brick. There's nothing you're going to get, you're lucky to get a single line unless it's about the Joker. 


Poison Ivy is in the game, has her own whole section of the map but Batman can't even get in. Killer Croc is in the game but you speak to him once if you know where to find the secret area. 


All the characters that are given mainline-level attention like Freeze and the Penguin are abandoned and left in weird states by the time you go to beat the game. It feels like so much of the game is SUPPOSED to wrap up but does not. The wrap up you do get is so sloppy it's hard to see what Rocksteady was even trying to do here. It's not super surprising, Asylum's end is universally derided for being a mess, I'm just very confused to not hear the same consensus on the slapped-together ending for this game too. They just can't seem to figure out how to end a game. They know how to set it up and dig deep and go into such detail you'll probably never even notice but when it comes to big storyline resolution they throw their hands up. The ending has less attention paid to it than the side missions, it's so disappointing



Honestly, having a perspective on this game now, separate from the hype and over-praise of this game at the time, I'd recommend stopping before re-entering the steel mill for the last time. I felt the last act was so jarring in its rushed and flimsy storytelling and gameplay that you'd be much more likely to love this game having stopped before the end begins. It's kind of insane to hear 0 criticisms of this game with an entire ending act like THAT. If this is what is hailed as a "perfect" video game story the medium has a LONG way to go. This would be endlessly ridiculed online if not in the form of the game, I cannot stress how sloppy the ending is. Up until that point though? Fantastic game, it's probably an 8.5 before you re-enter the Steel Mill for the final time. By the time I finished and beat that Two-Face boss? It's sitting at about a 6. Game is a mess the second you try and beat it, really leaves a sour taste after such amazing setup. I'd really love to recommend this game, but on sheer principle I cannot. 



The whiplash alone that someone would get playing this game hearing it is perfect and seeing all the massive flaws beating the game is enough to say that you should know this game has a LOT of flaws. It does some things incredibly well, but it is far from perfect, especially the writing and plot. Worth playing, but I'd avoid the ending and just look up plot for it instead, seriously it's that bad

review_text:
I really liked this game from the start. The mechanics are easy to pick up, the gunplay is extra smooth, and the gothic atmosphere is sick. Plus I love the floaty Halo-esque double jump. I've missed that. 

However, when I unlocked Gnosis, I realized I adore this game. New abilities and weapons become available with the caveat of ranked up difficulty? Yeah, I'll take that trade off. The map I thought I mastered just became a brand new level with more hordes of enemies and randomly spawning mini-bosses. With Gnosis unlocked, Witchfire's gameplay loop becomes seriously gratifying and addicting.

I'm not even 10 hours in and I've easily gotten my money's worth. Please keep going devs. You're seriously crushing it. Best FPS I've played in a long, long time. 

P.S. I explained this game to my friend and he said, "so it's Catholic Dark Souls with guns?" What a sick description.

review_text:
[h2]สิ่งที่ไม่ชอบ[/h2]
- การขายของในเกม
- ระบบ Battle Pass, Daily/Weekly Quest ถึงแม้จะไม่เสียเงิน แต่มันทำให้ความรู้สึกที่เล่นเหมือนเกมมือถือฟรีทั่วไป วันไหนไม่เข้ามาเล่นมาทำ quest ให้ครบวันนั้นจะรู้สึกขาดทุนหรือเสียผลประโยชน์ เหมือนเป็นการบังคับเล่นทุกวันกรายๆ แทนที่จะอยากเล่นเมื่อไหร่ก็เล่นได้แบบเกมอื่นๆ (ที่ไม่ใช่เกมมือถือ)
- Character Customization ไม่มีอะไรเลย แค่ตีมอน ดรอปของดีขึ้นระดับสูงขึ้นมาใส่เรื่อยๆวนไปทั้งเกม ดูน่าเบื่อไปหน่อย
- ด่านน้อย Content น้อย คือน้อยมากจริงๆจนเหมือนเกมยังไม่เสร็จ
- Mode CO-OP ซึ่งจริงๆควรต้องร่วมมือกัน แต่เกมออกแบบมาลักษณะนี้ แทนที่จะร่วมมือกันกลับเป็นการแย่ง MVP กัน แย่ง Damage อันดับ 1 กัน เพื่อนตายไม่ค่อยมีใครสนใจจะชุบ เพราะกลัวเสียโอกาสทำ Damage ไม่แน่ใจว่าเป็นเพราะการแจ้งเตือนการตายมันมองเห็นยาก หรือเพราะต้องการแย่งทำ Damage กันจริงๆ (ส่วนนี้ควรเอาอย่าง Granblue Fantasy Relink ไม่มีครั้งไหนที่เพื่อนตายแล้วจะไม่ถูกชุบ ทุกคนรีบแย่งกันชุบด้วยซ้ำ เพราะการตายมันส่งผลต่อเกจการตายโดยรวมของ party)

review_text:
This is an update on my review of GTTOD. My review was previously a negative one, and unfortunately, it's going to stay this way even after playing the update. I will also be talking about the developer's response to my negative review of the previous update.

I've been playing GTTOD since 2019, and I really, really had high hopes for the game. GTTOD used to be an endless shooter in a neon synthwave environment, and I believed that all the game needed was more content, because the gameplay and aesthetics were spot on. However, the developer decided that he hated the game, and wanted to completely rework the whole thing, and turn it into a completely different game. The biggest change is switching from a doom-style endless shooter to some Risk of Rain Roguelike FPS game. This new update is around the 3rd or 4th complete overhaul for GTTOD, where he completely changed the mechanics and alienating a lot of his older playerbase in the process.

Before getting into my issues with the game, I want to talk about the good things first. The movement is much better than it was before, in fact, it is the only thing keeping me from uninstalling the game. The animations are decent and the game looks better graphically than it did in previous updates. The new music is also good.

Now, for the stuff I personally dislike, I think with every update to this game, it loses more and more of what I enjoyed about the game in the previous version. Again, I'm not telling the developer what he can and cannot do, I'm just speaking from my own personal feelings towards the game.

In the previous update, the one thing that was keeping me entertained with this game is the Endless Mode, and although I complained about the Crevice map being completely broken and the game forcing me to play through some horribly designed parkour sequence every time I wanted to play a round of Endless Mode, it was still fun to be able to kill hordes of enemies, parkouring in a small arena, while grinding money to upgrade guns. For me, it was the closest the game's ever been since in rekindling what I really enjoyed about the old 2019 version.

With this new update, instead of improving Endless Mode and fixing the unplayable level, he decided to just completely remove Endless Mode entirely. In fact, now there's only one game mode in the game. Players who wanted something closer to the 2019 version would now have no choice but to play the main roguelike mode, which I also have some problems with.

The game tries really hard to be a roguelike, which is fine, but I think it is poorly executed. The game doesn't know what it wants to be. The movement is super fast, and the compass points RIGHT TOWARDS the exit door, which seems to encourage players to just disregard everything and run right towards the exit (and for the first few levels, there is no consequence for ignoring everything). This makes every level super fast to beat. The is no real incentive to doing anything else, the game barely teaches you what the mechanics are, you are just left to figure things out for yourself, which contradicts how the game encourages you to just ignore everything and get to the exit as fast as possible.

In previous versions, there is a really obvious screen effect for when you are at low health, which tells you CLEARLY that you are about to die. However, with this update, all you get is a beeping sound effect with no other clear indications on screen other than your health bar, and since enemies can kill you super quickly, it can lead to unfair deaths where you didn't notice that you're at low health, and enemies just killing you in a few seconds. 

To add insult to injury, every time you die, you have to sit through a really long death animation, which is unskippable. You will then be teleported to some weird area where you can upgrade yourself, but most of the time, you won't have enough currency to upgrade anything, but the game still forces you to sit through it. Once you're done with that, you'll have to watch ANOTHER long and unskippable cutscene of the player getting up and wiping water off his helmet before the game will let you play again. This is really irritating because of how frequent you may die, and how long it takes for you to get back into the action. This wouldn't be so bad if the animations are skippable, but they're not. Imagine if ULTRAKILL forced you to watch 30 seconds of animations before letting you respawn...

The developer of this game responded to my negative review in the past, where he reassured me that he's working on addressing the issues I had with the game, and told me that the mechanics he's working on will allow those who didn't like the roguelike direction GTTOD is going towards to enjoy the game more. He mentioned something called "The Cinder Core", which he said was a level that is comprised of mini arenas. This level is nowhere to be found, maybe it's in the update under a different name, but I cannot find it. I did find some portal that will lead to a dungeon, but you'll need shards or something to unlock it, and the game doesn't tell you what those dungeons are. Andrew also talked about adding a Prologue which will better explain the mechanics, this is also not present in the update, and if it is, it sure does a terrible job at teaching players anything. Andrew also talked about adding Quick Play, which is also something completely not present in this update. 

Basically, none of the things the developer said he would be adding in his response to my review are actually here. Instead of trying to add features to the game that players who liked the old versions would enjoy and polishing up what he made in the past, he removed and remade more and more things that further alienates those players. I am noticing a trend here.

I really enjoyed GTTOD back in the day, and I believed that it has a lot of potential. But all these unnecessary overhauls just really put a sour taste in my mouth, further drifting away from what made the old versions so fun to play. I am willing to bet that Andrew is going to completely overhaul everything again in a few months. 

Andrew constantly made the game more and more convoluted, complicating things and removing what made the old versions so much fun. I know I'm in the minority, and I am aware that a lot of people enjoy how GTTOD became a roguelike game, and good for them. But I personally don't see the game being what I originally hoped it was going to be anymore. It looks like it's time to let go.

What the hell did they do to the ghost warrior franchise?

GW 1-3 was solid. 3 is actually one of my favorite games. I enjoy them more than the sniper elite games. They did it better... until they decided to reinvent the wheel with the contracts series.


WTF is this bull shnit. Mask now pings everything everywhere in a shade of orange/piss random geometric lines for no apparent reason. Looking for a ledge to climb? NOPE.

 Speaking of over stimulation, map is not any better. A terrible migraine inducing layout with waypoints missing/blurred/colored the same and indistinguishable from one another. Some bert kreisher level genius decided "hurr durr game name contracts = make map look like contractor blueprints"   - I'm sorry but are you STUPID ?!  Who hired these clowns to ruin what could have easily outdone the janky sniper elite franchise that became close quarters call of duty crap. Instead, they aped it, and somehow also made it worse.

 TERRIBLE backwards ass game why would you take the ghost warrior series and ruin everything about it? 

SGW3 drones were fun and you could scout out your missions allowing you to go about in numerous ways. 
Contracts- "here's a drone. just kidding. you will never be allowed to use it." anti drone towers every 20 ft. no way to disable drone towers. STUPID DESIGN

GW3- You could easily get to your inventory to change ammo or weapons on the fly. And you could bring a silencer on any mission.
Contracts-  You get a clunky non responsive wheel of turdslop, you don't get a full choice of inventory or weapons, and you are forced to play the way they want you to play- stupidly.


I also tried at least a dozen times to like this. For one, the difficulty is not just ridiculously high, it is not realistic or fair at all. Enemies will mail you shots of AK-47 right to your cranium no matter how hidden or far away you are because apparently they are all super soldier robots with xray eyes and heat seeking bullets. Stealth? F you, buddy! 

I came back to this when I found WeMod finally updated their mods to work. So excited I tell my buddy hey Contracts is playable now! And although now the game is at least somewhat playable, after 2 contracts I found myself so frustrated I never want to play it again.

I'm more dissapointed than anything. Because they did this, it bombed- Then instead of going back to what worked in 3, they just did the same thing that bombed, and added slightly more long distance sniping. I don't think i'm gonna hold my breath for a Sniper Ghost Warrior 4...

Just take your time with this game and read the guides about how to solve the puzzles.

review_text: This game was completely and unfairly criticized when it was released. The dev team asked for more time and was forced to release before it was ironed out but let me tell you that this game is an excellent horror title that was made with great ambition and love. Any performance issues it was known to have are completely fixed and is optimized very well in its current state. If you never played this game and listened to all the haters, do yourself a favor and experience this game. If you have played it before and was dissatisfied at launch and never picked it up again, do yourself a favor and take another crack at it. You owe it to yourself to experience this fantastic story and create your own opinion after its refinement. The combat is fluid and super satisfying, the graphics and atmosphere are completely unparalleled with breathtaking visuals and attention to detail. All the characters are well written and full of personality. The gore, tension and kill animations are up there with dead space. This was directed by the same man who made Dead Space and Callisto Protocol while being a completely different game is a true spiritual successor to it, and I don't care what anyone says. This game is highly underappreciated for all the care that went into it and I truly don't understand why this game got as much hate that it got because its far more deserving than that. Seriously, try this game and ignore what you've heard because I bet you would be surprised how amazing this game is. Do expect a linear and heavily melee combat focused experience with some gun play combos, but don't be fooled because it was made with that intention and it does it very well with great pacing and flow. I love this game and it deserves more positive feedback because for the things it was criticized for such as performance issues no longer applies. Many people hopped on the band wagon saying its boring and has bad combat but I honestly don't understand what they are talking about because this is a bloody great time. Also for a first play through do NOT play hardcore mode. I did this and beat it but it was so much more fun and balanced on normal. I recommend doing hardcore on a second or third play through, please trust me on this. Have a good time because this is an excellent game. If you did enjoy it, please leave a positive review for it because I seriously want a sequel someday if possible and your feedback matters.

I just may be the only person in the history of the universe to not love Bioshock.  I had hoped to play though Bioshock 1 and 2 before moving on to the oft praised (and contemporary) Bioshock: Infinite. No dice. 

I really couldn't get into this game though it is not totaly without merit.

Pros: 
-through my several hours of play i was able to see the beginings of a interesting plot
-interesting concept to be able to customize your playstyle via the plasmid system
-the game is dripping with atmosphere, though this is only a plus if you enjoy being immersed in said atmosphere (I did not)

Cons:
-I only encountered a handful of types of enemies all of whom annoyingly and quite incessantly spout less than imaginative nonsense making me want to kill myself rather than them
-the gameplay was repetitive - room after not-so-different room of the same few enemies (I'm reminded of Dead Space which I also did not enjoy)
-God forbid that you feel the need fully use the game's hack mechanic, unless you really enjoy the simple yet horrifyingly tedius mini-game employed to hack items

review_text:
Easily one of the most fun farming/cozy games I've played in YEARS. I am an avid Stardew/SoS/Harvest Moon player, and this game is really like if Stardew & Animal Crossings's cousin had a baby with Oregon Trail. It's been so hard to close it and step away, I just want to keep playing and progressing. I would really recommend adjusting the settings AFTER you've played with them normal first, to get a feel for how the game was made to run. I am not ashamed to say I turned off the fishing game - I found it pretty tedious and annoying, and fish is one of the easiest ways to make quick money in this game. I love the flexibility provided as far as controls and even customization for your character once you're IN the game (although I do wish there was a bit more pre-game customization for your character), and honestly one of the only things I'm missing is the ability to name my animals. Some of the point-and-click style controls can feel a bit clunky at first, but once you get used to it it's not bad at all. Best bits of advice I can give - GET INOCULATED and don't interact with strangers from out of town until you do! (Or have your legacy ready to go) Also, wood is a GREAT way to make money early game, but it will mean having to patiently wait and gather two bits of wood per tree (kinda like Animal Crossing) every in-game day to build up the wood for farm buildings - I instead opted to save my wood and fish like a madman in every spare moment of my day, and I sold EVERYTHING the first year that I didn't need to eat to survive and had a chicken coop & barn before fall of my first year. Definitely, there's a lot of flexibility to how you'd like to run your homestead as well. I cannot wait to move on to my next generation and have them raise a family as well. Cannot stress enough - one of the best Cozy games I've played in a very long time. Props to the two person Dev team, you guys are amazing!!! I can't wait for future updates! :3

TLDR: Amazing game, lots of flexibility in how you'd like to approach it & play, totally worth the money if you love Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, and/or Animal Crossing style games and would like a sort of Oregon Trail danger to it.

review_text:
What even to write? I found myself thinking back about the time I spent on this game alone, my account here on Steam says I have roughly 2.6k hours, but I've played this game on the JP servers starting 2016, then moved to global on the XBOX and finally on PC in the last couple of years, so collectively I have around 8k hours or so.

I can confidently say that, despite all it's flaws (That will eventually come up as you run out of story and things to do except endless grinding) this is a really enjoyable experience overall, and really one of the only few games like this that allow you full freedom to customize your character however you like, and that is one of the best things this game has to offer.

Otherwise, the game is populated enough where you can play without any issues, but for completely F2P players, it is a slight challenge to buy fashion items off the market, as a decent hairstyle can go for up to 20m+ in-game currency, so usually a single item is enough to drain all your savings. But instead if you're the kind of person that has plenty of money to toss at SEGA, you won't have any issues looking fashionable. Although it is probably better not to play this game around your family, as a good chunk of the players likes to use that freedom of the character creation to make pretty NSFW stuff, hahaha.

In conclusion, I've met some of the most wonderful people here over the years that have changed my life for the better, that I wouldn't have found otherwise if I didn't play NGS, so give it a shot and see if you can come out of it with something nice.

TL:DR: Instance based "MMO" with decent gameplay, can go back to the 2012 version of it if you download the data for it, lots of story and good characters to entertain you enough, for free.

- Sub-quests can be a chore.
- Finding players for a sub-quest is a pain, especially in Vol. 1

Volume 1-3:
Gameplay: 9/10
Storyline: 8/10
Performance: 10/10

Volume 4:
Gameplay: 6/10
Storyline: 4/10
Performance: 7/10

Overall, I would recommend purchasing this game, even if you have already played the original volumes before. The storyline is still very enjoyable and the gameplay keeps the game interesting.

review_text:
The aesthetics are brilliant. The new player experience as of Webgrave, is seamless. I was incredibly surprised to hear that the new playable map, as well as the tutorial area, were very recent additions - it all flows extremely well.

The gameplay is basically like the open world locations of Destiny 2, but with a lot of those Events, to use destiny terminology. Now, this sounds boring. But why isn't it?

Because the gunplay is as good as in Destiny, and more importantly, the game emphasizes secret hunting (both for progression, and for unlocking trinkets for your rosary), and has pretty captivating ARPG and rougelike-like elements, so you always have new weapons, demonic weapons, spells, heavy spells, rings, etc to grind towards.

And yes, you grind through the same few levels.But whenever your character levels up, all enemy encounters are drastically changed. Even without levelling up, each time you re-enter a map, it is randomly re-filled with secrets, loot, enemies, and even new things to experience, all paced really well. You might feel like exploring off into some interesting corner of the map, only to find another bead for your rosary. Nice collectible hunting. (Did i mention that the rosary is apparently also a recent addition? I can hardly believe it, as it fits so well.)

Each map has an excellent boss-fight at it's end (apart from the first map, though i suspect there might be a boss in an area that i'm unable to explore yet - as the game gives you reasons to return to older maps once you reach certain levels of Gnosis.)

The combat is pretty great, and it can actually get incredibly difficult. This is the first shooter game in a long time where my deaths have felt genuienly avoidable, and yet i died either way. Ya gotta keep track of the enemies circling around you, ya gotta dodge, ya gotta jump, ya gotta duck behind cover to avoid ranged fire, ya gotta learn the enemies' attack patterns so you don't get flattened while trying to shotgun them in the face (Really, it's almost as if this is *gasp* the Dark Souls of first person shooters?)... so yeah. Relatively simple gameplay, but well done. And excellent aesthetics. I always appreciate some semi-victorian semi-medieval witchcraft-themed games. And this one even has some architecture to rival Bioshock Infinite's, though with a slightly more muted colour palette. But *man* is that castle location awesome!

I've never played a game this offensively and egregiously shoddy, and this is coming from someone who's bought every Call of Duty game since 2007.

review_text:
I do not recommend buying this game at full price - I got it for 2 dollars though, and if that is still the price when you see it, then by all means, drop two bucks. That being said, this game is a mess.

I like the idea - I REALLY like the idea - but the execution is mediocre at best. Run around a mansion as a 7 year old and murder everyone in various ways. Sounds like a blast! I didn't even care that it was all scripted, and that there was little to no creativity allowed. What I cared about was the wacky bugs and confusing as hell missions. I had to look at the wiki in order to figure out what to do in the last half of the game, and I regularly play the Sherlock Holmes games, so I'm no stranger to adventure/puzzle games. But there is very little guiding your way. An intial mark on the map shows you your target, but after that, nothing. No markers showing important objects or following your target or anything. You can get a couple "gifts" that give you hints, but unfortunately my game bugged out and failed to register my "chores" so I couldn't get past the Ouiji board (which only hints at an important item to obtain, not what to do). Need to kill one of the maids? Clearly the thing to do is...break the washing machine by dropping an iron into it, thus making her...take a shower? Of course! Need to kill the driver? Well break that washing machine with the iron again to lure out the mechanic (because to hell with washing clothes!), then...find a mix tape so he can turn around and listen to it, allowing you to get some paint thinner and a rag to knock him out with? Masterful! There are also plenty of zero purpose items in the game. Books and bottles can be picked up, but serve no purpose. You can't even throw them to distract NPCs away from locations. Light switches can be flicked on and off, leading one to believe that there is a "stealth" aspect of the game Nope...in the one section where you can do it, darkness has no meaning - mom will find you whether you are standing in pitch black or right under the light bulb. There is a section of stealth gameplay later in the game where darkness actually matters...but you take out the power to the mansion, thus rendering the switches useless anyway!

The powers are cool, but you rarely get to use them. Telekenesis is your go to, followed by mind control. You can mind control a few of the people in the mansion, but unless they have some scripted interaction in that particular "chapter", you can't do anything with them. Later in the game, you get some offensive spells...but unless you choose the "Action" ending (oh yes, that is a thing), you will use the fireball spell twice and the combustion spell - your last spell, btw - once. Yep, one time. The only truly useful spell that doesn't require a scripted event is memory erase, where if you are caught doing something, you can make them forget (but only 6 times a chapter). 

And don't even get me started on the bugs. I have witnessed: an NPC walking into a closed door, effectively locking it for me. A chore not registering as complete (taking out the garbage), thus failing to allow me to continue that line of "side quests". Dropping that iron into the washer didn't work a few times. Dropping a hair dryer into a tub didn't work because it got stuck behind it, and was out of "range" of telekenesis. Entries in my journal not registering, leaving me with zero clues on how to continue. And many more minor annoyances (glitching through walls, glitching through each other, falling through the floor once, getting stuck in the courtyard on a very small "hill"). The voice sync is awful, the voice acting is...not terrible, but not good either. If what they do with their faces could be called "expressions" or "emotions" then those are awful too. Many of these could of probably been fixed, but clearly the developer did not see a reason to. 

Overall, the game is a mess, but it is certainly worth the two dollars I paid for it. I love the idea, and I would like to see more from the developer (although I'm told the sequel to this is even worse), but please polish it up, give a bit more creativity, and let us use our damn spells! If there isn't a sale on, avoid this one. If there is, anywhere from 1 to 5 bucks...go ahead and give it a whirl.

review_text:
No I do not recommend this game.

 This may sound corny over a video game, but it does pain me to leave this review.
After 8898 hours in I finally have begun what feels like an Alcoholics Anonymous program for myself.

 A short about myself: I consider myself a long time fan of Phantasy Star games and Sega. I grew up with Sega Genesis and the original games are still my most memorable JRPG experiences. I still own PSO on two systems, one I bought specifically just for the one version that was upgraded on GameCube.

 Phantasy Star Online 2 New Genesis is not in the right hands. It feels like either the game director Kimura and team has lost passion for this game OR Sega has extremely underfunded and understaffed them since the Global release and launch of NGS. I played this game every single day since 2020 and can count on one hand how many days I missed logging in to do the run of the mill dailies (these are literally the core gameplay focus).

 Hopping on the treadmill of completing dailies and spending real money for AC is a serious self abuse if it's in hopes for this game to ever become popular or have more to do in it. They call it a live service game but the only live service is more AC scratch tickets every week to suck $ out of players who fall prey to it.

 It would be justified to spend $ on a game to support the developers if they actually had passion about the game and showed it through the addition of meaningful and decently paced "content" updates. More meaningful and impactful story. More places to go and see that have actual detailed thought out design instead of rehashed VR geometric areas that look like they are built with children's toy blocks.

 The worst part about all of this is the game has five star combat, five star creative space, and five star character customization. But please believe me, it stops there, if the team spent half as much time as they spent on new AC scratch and SG scratch ticket items then this game could possibly have an acceptable pace of new story and places to see and go, characters to meet and build upon, new enemies etc... but this game is the definition of stagnation. If only they could do this then it could be a decent game, but it is sadly in my strongest opinion, in the wrong hands. 

 Too many years and times I have stuck up for Sega and the development team basically lying to myself and others drunk on the thought of it getting better and backed even worse by investing $ into it in hopes that it could get better.

 Phantasy Star 2 NGS has turned the game series into a platform to advertise other games and vtubers and has even done it semi poorly. It's nothing but a long drawn out recycled cash grab of endless AC scratch tickets with 1/10th the development focus on the game's own identity. There is no meaningful loot system, no dungeons with detailed environments, I do not mind the open world but they should have by now built upon it with some "dungeon crawling" and quests etc that the original PSO was built upon.

 If you made it to the end, then thank you for your time and allowing me to vent what should have been said at least a year and a half ago.

review_text:
Lucius is a third person game where you take control of a young boy called Lucius. Satan himself visits his bedroom and commands him to become a serial killer. This game reminded me a lot of the movie the omen.

[b]pros[/b]
+ graphics are nothing special, but get the work done
+ every killing gets you a short cutscene
+ big map
+ the victims don't feel like random redshirts with no names
+ great in-between cutscenes

[b]cons[/b]
- very linear. there is always only one way to do things
- game is very unclear what you have to do. I often used guides since I didn't bother
- there isn't really an ending
- clunky controls
- best thing about this game are the cutscenes. the gameplay is pretty annoying you put up with to see the short videos.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
This game has huge potential, but since there is always only one way to finish each chapter the game falls short. It's much easier to read guides than to waste your time by searching random little objects on the huge map. The cutscenes are worth experiencing the game. But since the gameplay is so irritating, you could honestly just watch a walkthrough on youtube. If you are still interested in the game, get it on a sale.

Replay value: very low (too linear, gameplay is not fun, great cutscenes)
Rating: 6/10 (not bad per se, but you won't miss anything if you don't play it)
Recommendation: No

review_text:
So, after playing this game to completion I can say that it isn't great. Maybe I was spoiled by the Dead Space remake, but since this game takes so much inspiration from Dead Space it's almost impossible to not compare them to each other almost every way. 

PROS:
-Excellent Graphics
-Good performance. At the time of this review it runs smoothly. I know on release things were rough but that seems to be completely fixed now.
-Great story that stays interesting and is well paced throughout the game (personally I'm also a big fan of audio logs)

CONS:
-DLC, Yikes DLC for actual ending of story
-Horror. You will not be horrored. This game commits the cardinal horror survival sin of just being frustrating. I did not find myself being scared except for maybe once or twice near the beginning when things are still mysterious, but after an hour in I found myself just getting annoyed at enemies popping up or grabbing me. (Fuck the grabs where you spam E seriously)
-Survival. You will not survival. Some things you will learn by dying... why? You should not be dying to learn things this isn't a souls-like. (For ex. tooltip to shoot robots in head but you will be INSTANTLY killed if you do, you actually have to hit them multiple times before they go down)
-Time. I knocked this game out in 8 hours. That includes exploring every side route, which are annoying too since there's rarely indication of which way is optional and there's tons of drops where you can't backtrack. And it seems like I spent over a half hour crawling through vents just holding w.
-Combat. The dodging is pretty stupid easy since there's not timing window, I had fun in a couple boss fights but the fodder is just annoying to fight especially when you pump the same amount of shells into the same enemy type and one dies right away and the other is a fresh zombie boi. 


Yeah so overall I'd just say skip this one and replay Dead Space or Resident Evil. Maayyyybe buy if it's on a huge sale, but definitely don't buy the DLC that's just feeding greed.

review_text:
What's there to say that hasn't been said yet? I think Act 2 of Hiveswap is phenomenal. It takes the game in a different direction, whereas Act 1 has mostly focused on locations, items and descriptions, Act 2 knocks it out of the park by focusing on what we all really wanted from the game. Trolls. And lots of them!

I think it's by no means an exaggeration when I say that what Act 2 puts into form is something every Homestuck fan has been wanting to see from day 1. More Trolls, more interactions. The train is a fantastic setting as well, allowing the player a highspeed hemospectrum tour that openly displays what has been canonically known for a long time, the way trolls interact with each other according to their social hierarchy dictated by blood.

And do not get me started on the music. While Act 1 had catchy tunes, Act 2 really knocked it out of the park with some absolute bangers (Quadrant Confusion) and some actually terrifying jams (Down with the Clown).

Overall, this is what we've been waiting for. All those years in the making, what Act 1 failed to deliver was realized in Act 2 and I'm very happy for it. It bodes well for future acts and it has me genuinely excited to see what's bound to come in the next 4 years.

review_text:
The Callisto Protocol is a lot like Dead Space! Or is it... Follow Jacob Lee, a new inmate locked up in Black Iron Prison, where he bears witness to an outbreak of zombie-like creatures that wreak havoc on the prison. Get up close and personal with some brutal melee action to dismember and destroy the foes in your path as you try to find out just what the hell is going on.

Similar to Dead Space, you play Callisto Protocol in a third-person perspective walking around a dark and creepy environment. Similar to Dead Space, you'll occasionally be assaulted by three to five creatures of nefarious origin and tasked with dismembering them as swiftly as possible. Similar to Dead Space, you can also yeet and pull shit around with a tele-kinetic gravity arm tool thing. Similar to Dead Space, you can keep track of your health via a segmented bar on your back that you can refill with syringe item pickups, and similar to Dead Space you can find said pickups by stomping on an enemy's corpse. Similar to Dead Space, there's also a mysterious cult-like origin to the zombie beings that assail you. And yet with all these similarities to Dead Space, with all these moments where you go "I feel like I've played this game already", Callisto Protocol still manages to separate itself to a decent degree. The primary thing being that Callisto Protocol is incredibly melee-based, with a focus on counter-attacks and dodging and weaving through the swings of the enemy. The big benefit of this is that you really get to fully immerse yourself in the violence, gore, and horror of the action going on around you. And while I love Dead Space, this variation of a classic formula is still really fun to mess around with.

There are some downsides to The Callisto Protocol. For one, the combat can get a little repetitive after a while, as once you figure out the optimal block-dodge-strike sequences the game feels a tad "figured-out". To make up for this the game introduces a lot of new enemies and variants, most of whom feel exciting to encounter (we do not talk about Two-Head holy fuck what a boring enemy). The story definitely leaves a lot to be desired. Ironically, Dead Space actually has a really solid story at least for the first two games, whereas Callisto Protocol is about 9 hours of your protagonist going "what the hell is going on???????" followed by a final chapter of exposition dump and a god-awful ending. One of your primary antagonists has so much beef with you and for frankly no reason considering you've interacted for all of twenty minutes together. The DLC actually wraps up the main game's ending really well for the most part and offers a much better resolution in terms of gameplay and story, but considering this is locked behind a DLC paywall this feels really scummy. The gore is pretty solid, but the blood effects could be better for the type of the game it is and the advertised gazillions of ways your character can die don't really feel that amazing. If anything, you might see a grand total of like, 8 different animations in the whole story, as half the time an animation won't even play and your character will just flop over dead. Finally, the environmental layout feels really cheesy and slapped together. While it's graphically well-developed, it's also filled to the brim with cheap jumpscares and shimmy sequences (you will crawl through so many vents). Also what the hell kinda prison is this, why are there just random walls of spikes and sawblade machines of gore and destruction (besides to give the player some environmental tools to kill enemies with). 

And yet, with all that being said, I gotta say:

The Callisto Protocol's kinda fun.

Does it feel at times like a pretty inferior product to the game it so frequently emulates? Does it get redundant? Does it feel less horror-focused and more cheesy gore action movie at times? Yes to all these things. But if you can get it on a steep discount, say $20 or less, I'd say it's pretty worth it. Just set your expectations low, and go in just expecting to wail on some zombies for a few hours and experience some brain candy popcorn fun.

There is a lot of good in this game. I just wish it could go like Terraria and evolve as a game with patches and updates. It could really become a game of the highest quality with a little more love put into it.

Update:
The devs continue to ban and delete any posts that are negative. 
I used an Alt account to point out that they started using ai generated content without putting the warning on the page like they are supposed to do. When people asked why using ai content was an issue I stated it wasn't about the content it's about the fact that these devs constantly have to be reminded how to do things right. I proceeded to list a few things they needed reminded of and they deleted the entire thread and perma banned the account for "disrespectful posts". (Never mind that the guidelines that Valve gives devs is to give a warning for first infraction and a temp ban for the second; never lead with a perma ban)

These devs are giant man-children with egos large enough to blot out the sun.

Avoid this trash and especially it's devs at all costs.
[hr][/hr]
If you would have asked me a year ago if I recommended this game, I would have said absolutely, and if we were friends at the time I might have even tried to buy you a copy.

I was a fool, and had foolish hopes.

Today I learned that back in an August Q&A (about 2 months ago at time of writing) the devs said that it was too hard to separate ADS sensitivity from Hipfire sensitivity and that that feature would not come until after their 1.0 release. I was astonished by this because I have seen the exact options in the old UE4 ini files before the upgraded to UE5; they were just never activated and defined.

So I did what any nerd would do when they don't believe something and I looked into how to do it. 

At first I found a video tutorial on how to set X & Y sensitivity individually, which was something they didn't know how to do for a long time and had only 1 slider for both sensitivities. This took about 3 minutes for me to find and learn how to do, and I've never developed a game in my life (though I do have a lot of experience tweaking UE ini files).

I then refined my search and found exactly how to define input mapping contexts in UE5 and can give you a link directly to the developer guide provided by Epic.

[b]I learned how to do all of this in about 10 minutes[/b], with some minor help from Copilot, and absolutely no developer experience. [b]These 'devs' have been unable to figure out how to do this for over a year and a half.[/b]

In 8 days this game will be releasing on consoles and none of the players will be able to set different sensitivity for their hipfire versus their ADS. As someone who plays EVERYTHING (even StarCraft) with a controller, I can tell you this will make some weapons absolutely unusable and many of these would be new players are going to be turned away.

This is a game that relies heavily on an active community or it becomes unplayable. You can't finish the main co-op mode with less than an 11-12 person team. The devs knew this and that's why they rushed to put out the console version as the PC playerbase has been dwindling over the last year and a half. 

Oh did I forget to mention they are rushing out the console version ahead of their original plan?
Yea that's a thing; presumably because they need players to keep the game alive.

They also said they aren't going to allow controller controls to be customizable, at least not right away. This is not a hard thing either and a handful of us have been customizing the controls via ini edits for over a year, since they experimented several times with different controller schemes and some of them were pretty bad; and yet they can't figure out hwo to make a menu to do that, but are about to put out the full release in 8 days.

[b]If you've only skimmed this review to this point[/b] you might be thinking "this is mostly controller stuff and doesn't affect me because I'm going to use Keyboard and Mouse" but there's heavy, heavy signs of incompetence here, and rushing out 1.0 in 8 days is looking like it's going to be a disaster. Because again, these devs can't even figure out how to separate ADS from hipfire after 1.5 years, and I can teach you how to do it in less than half an hour.

And mind you, in 8 days the price is going to go up too.

I could go on longer about other poor decisions they've made (like jumping from UE4 to UE5 before they tested thoroughly) and are projected to make, but this has a character limit, and at the end of the day I simply do not recommend the game. I really, truly, wish I could because I loved this game at one point, but I respect you more than the devs have respected their fans.
