It's just good. Period.

Decently paced with clear progression, immersive atmosphere, fun gunplay, great enemy variety and adequate difficulty ramping.

Some people say it needs to be harder, some say it needs to be easier - which makes it just perfect in my book.

Play at your own pace, however you want to play. No microtransactions, battlepasses or BS exploitative practices. Simple, good gameplay with a fair price.

If you're on the fence about buying this game or not - don't be. Support these devs, they deserve success.

P.S. Thank you to The Astronauts for such a wonderful project. As a long-time fan of DOOM, Painkiller, Serious Sam and Wolfenstein this managed to scratch my nostalgia itch for days gone while making me appreciate the modern gameplay  design innovations, both of which are blended seamlessly.

说实在的，自从上来大学以来许久没有玩过这样的作品了，也许久没有体验过这部作品给我带来的感受了。这真的是一部很扣人心弦的作品，从始至终的节奏把控的都特别好，倒叙的方式也是让我感觉眼前一亮，从老年一个不知所以的愿望逐渐推回最心底的记忆，逐渐了解到这场爱情故事的根本，这样的叙事设计真的很不错。

------剧透警告------

[spoiler]非常美且遗憾的一部作品，美在那John和River之间纯粹的爱情和追逐梦想约定的毅力及勇气，遗憾在于，尽管John的记忆里达到了那个愿望，但是River至终却只知道John对她的第一记忆不是他们相遇许下约定的那个晚上，而是被记忆模糊之后的“学校相遇”，可能这就是River在那次谈话之后病情逐渐恶化的原因吧……但是对于John来说，这真的是最完美的结局了。到最后结局之前其实我一直都以为是不完美的，为了达成John的意愿去月球而放弃了他与River的相遇，但是结局真的太出乎我预料了，我真的没想到River也为了追寻同样的一个小小约定而有如此大的毅力和勇气成为了宇航员。当我看到John和River在航天局相遇…当熟悉的钢琴旋律再次响起，那首《For River》的曲名变成《To the Moon》的时候…我真的没办法控制住情绪的波动。是啊，To the Moon，其实这一切的动力就是For River啊。[/spoiler]

Great game! Seriously, I love it, the shooting feels amazing, the movement is smooth, the weapons are cool, and the controls are easy to handle.

I only have one big problem: the Arcana upgrades.
It’s honestly really frustrating that most of the Arcanas are situational and often end up being useless. 
Not because of the stats themselves, but because of the skills.

For example: I’m in a run and I get four upgrades in a row for lightning magic, more damage against shocked enemies, more crits, extra charges, and so on. Awesome perks!
The problem? I don’t have lightning magic.
And this happens all the time. I constantly get upgrades for things I can’t use.

That makes it super frustrating since you can’t change your magic during a run.
On top of that, I rarely use magic anyway, because the gunplay is just too good and the magic feels kinda boring.
I even tried playing without any magic equipped at all, but unfortunately, I still kept getting tons of magic upgrades.

I really hope this gets changed or at least that we get an option to block certain categories from showing up.

review_text:
Right now, I don't recommend it.

Most of the current features in the game feel like they are only HALF of the feature. Sandbox mode feels empty, Custom Mode is not so custom.
So many things missing.

Weird design decisions that either make no sense or are working hard against the player.

I don't mind the difficulties or that no matter what you do, you effectively are just creating a village to have it destroyed in the end. That is the premise of the game after all. The name of the game even says as much.

I'm just annoyed and pissed at the half arsed design of the game overall.

Love the graphics, no can't fault it here.

Here is a few things that could improve this game - And by their lack, made me uninstall this game for good:

* Custom mode and sandbox SHOULD BE MERGED!!!
Have a checkbox in custom mode that enables Sandbox features... Simple...
As is right now, Sandbox feels more like a tacked on half idea with little thought put into it.
Waste of time game mode more like.

* Custom mode lacks more fine control.
Again, half a feature, half an idea. Just tossed out to say "Hey, see, we ARE making content for the game..."
Yeah, but it feels more like half an idea and half the effort.

* Villager AI is a joke: "Let me just go and chop down this wood while 5 zombies are destroying my towncenter" Like wot m8?
You got an axe, you even have a shield/armor, go slap a few skulls along with the 14 other villages and WORK TOGETHER...

* Editor does not have even basic help menu.
For the map maker, there isn't a small menu that gives hints as to what would cause the corruption to spawn, or offer other hints.
does not even have controls shown.
Again, tacked on idea, but only half of it.

There are more tiny things to talk about but those were the ones that made me really grit my teeth... these things ruined my fun.

I'll be back in 1 year to see how much have changed in this game, but considering the speed at which a patch or content release is done, i doubt much will have been done... Oh well...

review_text:
Here is the deal. As someone who started playing PSO2 on the original Japanese servers back in 2014, I can't help but feel disappointed with NGS. The charm of PSO2 was in its randomly generated stages and central hub. PSO2 captured the essence of being on a home ship and embarking with your team on missions. Emergancy missions were awesome as the matchmaking allowed for a full team of 12 players. The game offered numerous quality-of-life features that benefited free-to-play players, and the vibrant economy thrived due to accessible trading and item exchanges. 

Sadly, NGS's shift to an open-world format and alterations to the PSO2 formula appear to be Sega's strategy to increase monetization, pushing players to spend more. Each update feels like a regression, especially with the current power system acting as a barrier to boss encounters, the most enjoyable activity in PSO2. The open-world design and player distribution sometimes result in vast empty areas, particularly outside the main hubs, having the game feel like your playing solo. The removal of friend bots sucks. It always felt like you were playing with your friends even if they where offline. With the current average of 1,557 players on Steam, it seems PSO2 has days have long since peaked.

My first recommendation is to play thru a single character route in this game, and then immediately play thru the ending for that character in Edo Blossoms. The two games go hand in hand (and have been considered a single game on other platforms). I prefer Edo Blossoms by far because the stories are unique to each character, whereas Kyoto Winds has a lot of parts that overlap so there is a fair amount of repetition. I think if you were to attempt to play all the routes & endings in Kyoto Winds back to back you'd quickly grow bored, at least for me. 

As for the game being "action-y" and historical, and not really your typical otome, I have to say yeah that's true - but by no means should that discourage you from playing it if you're looking for a good love story! The romance in Kyoto Winds builds slowly, and starts out with little things and acts of friendship as the characters get to know each other. Its not over the top, and I feel like it's wonderfully done. Once you have the foundation laid, play Edo Blossoms over and over for those heart wrenching, passionate moments. ;)

review_text:
The concept is brilliant! Sadly the pace of the gameplay is too erratic to hold my interest. 

Long periods of point-and-click style play happen between tasks/murders which vary in difficulty, seemingly at random. Generally in games keystage challenges become exponentially more difficult, but in my (short) exploration of this one it seems  one task can be virtually impossible to complete followed by a task which is ludicrously simple. 

It is challenging, in some instances overly so; actions expected of the player can be very obscure with no hints, once you've finally figured out what you have to do it can then be a feat of superhuman dexterity to complete your mission... creaing a  serious anticlimax. It is frustrating and slightly tedious in alternating intervals. This is not helped by the fact the game mechanics appear to struggle with a controller, there are a great many graphics glitches, odd bouts of lag, and reloading from a checkpoint takes a very long time. 

Perhaps the game is just older and I am being unfair. It is also possible that I'm just not suited to this type of puzzle solving as, to be candid, this game very quickly felt like a chore rather than a joy which is a pity because, as I said, the concept is awesome.

review_text:
It amuses me how many people are complaining that a schoolgirl can't swing a broadsword faster than a battle-hardened orc.

That aside, here are some things you need to know:

-- This ain't your daddy's Metroidvania. It's tough as nails and will torture you if you're expecting a mash-happy slash-fest.

-- Combat is clunky and messy, and it's by design. It's supposed to be punishing and brutal, and it's entirely fine if you avoid it. 

-- Even if you avoid combat, you're still gonna die a lot. Poison, bleeding, freezing, and being set on fire will kill you faster and more often than an axe to the noggin will.

-- Recovery items are sparse. If you do find any, this game is a hoarder's worst nightmare, as most fights you get into in the early game will force you to use something. Don't think you can rely on checkpoints to get your HP/MP back either! 

-- Money is hard to get at first (I often got it by selling items). There are lots of items, spells, and weapons to buy but you won't be able to afford many of them at first. Recovery items are a luxury. If you want them, you must sacrifice things to be able to buy them. 

-- The game really makes you think about what items you're equipping. You won't have an all-purpose build. You need to think about what enemies you're going up against and plan accordingly.

-- Graphically, this is one of the most gorgeous games you'll ever play. Truly enchanting pixel art.

-- If I had a complaint, it'd be that I'd like to be able to refresh checkpoints with updated equipment. Checkpoints only become usable again after every third one you activate, and if I die at a boss with the wrong equipment loadout I have to keep remembering to switch to something else each time I die.

edit: I was asked about time to completion. There's a good bit of content in this game. It'll take you probably 8-10 hours on your first playthrough, and then you unlock three (yes, three) new gameplay modes, each with a different way to play the game.

review_text:
(Mild Spoilers) This game is terrible. Not only are the controls clunky, the characters obnoxious, and the gameplay tedious at times, but it's also grossly ableist. It's made very clear that River is autistic, but the game never even uses the word "autism" and makes it seem like it's a bad word. They keep referring to it as "her condition" and going on and on about how hard it is for her husband, John, to tolerate her. Mind you, these two are supposed to be in love. He explicitly refuses to learn about her "condition" when given the opportunity, and also makes it clear that he only started going out with her because she was "weird" and "unique" and he didn't want to be "boring" so he uses her to make himself appear more interesting.

I found out after playing that the creator has donated to Autism Speaks in the past. It seems he has since learned about the criticisms against Autism Speaks and no longer supports them. I think it's great that he acknowledged his mistake in supporting them, but he still has a lot to learn about autism. It's clear that he did not reach out to the autistic community during the development of this game.

It's very problematic, and honestly even if it wasn't, it's still a terrible story. It tries to be funny, then romantic, then heartbreaking, then creepy, round and round again, failing at each. By the end of the game, I hated all but a few side characters and River. I felt little more than annoyance during my playthrough. The ending was so unsatisfying, and there were a few loose threads that are never acknowledged (perhaps in a sequel but I'm not sticking around to find out).

I did enjoy the soundtrack and the visuals, and I liked the idea of going through someone's memories in reverse order. The main premise sounded really interesting and could have been done very well. I typically love games that involve facing the reality of death and questions of morality. This one, however, was a miss. I would not recommend this game to anyone.

review_text: It was a mistake to chief the DMT cart while playing this. I finally broke through while a humanoid creature was crawling out of an incubation pod. I wasn't prepared in the slightest for what I experienced. I can't put into words the 10 to 15 minutes that proceeded the break through, but when I got a grip I saw that the creature that was just birthed in front of me had died. For about a half second I felt so hopeless and sorry for the creature, before I realized I was staring at a screen. If I was a lesser man I would say something along the lines of "I felt like I lived that things life." But I'm not a reddit shaman and I don't attend burning man in a diaper and a binky. Regardless of my experience, this is a game you play more for it's art style than it's actual game play. It's still a fantastic game though, and I find immense entertainment in imagining how the world of this game came to be, and what it might have all looked like in it's prime. I often find myself simply staring at the walls in this game to take in the detail. Very few rooms, objects, and items in this game lack any detail or prove themselves boring to look at. I imagine the game play and story line to be a similar experience to living in small towns in South Asia; crawling over unidentifiable piles of flesh in a frail pathetic body only to be occasionally met with an ancient monolithic structure who's purpose the world forgot long ago. This game masters an atmosphere of persistent fear and dread of what's to come, and every enemy you encounter reminds you of how weak you are. It reminds you of a primal dread that's forgotten in this modern world, and makes you feel like a monkey that's lost it's tribe in the wild. To put it simply, you feel like a small animal being hunted. The puzzles aren't really that challenging, but the overall experience makes up for a lack of interesting game play and puzzles. I highly recommend all who appreciate this sort of genre of surreal art that artists like Zdzislaw Beksinski and H.R. Giger have brought to this world to pick this game up. My only regret with this game is that I didn't pick it up sooner.

review_text:
[b]Needs more appreciation[/b]
Visually truly uncanny, but for most players the good ends here. The complaints usually involve: bad puzzle and level design, confusing combat, and the game being too short.

Puzzles indeed are not trivial - they ask you to stop and think or at least load a lot of level into your memory. Enemies however are often just obstructions, meaning you mostly have to run past or away from the enemies, not shoot ‘em. As a result, combat is best avoided in the vast majority of instances altogether. There’s a boss fight that involves gunplay, but it is really easy as it is not the focus of the experience, however it works as a survival puzzle as well and guns are perfectly suited for that fight.

So... what was that game genre where you progress slowly, fight annoyingly hard to kill enemies with imperfect combat abilities and need to [b]survive[/b] with limited ammo, health, and sparse checkpoints (all things found in Scorn!)... ah yeah, "survival horror", by the book.

If you go with the flow, the whole package starts to get into your head. Scorn is designed for you to get lost in [spoiler]and ultimately lose[/spoiler]. When you spend at least half of the time wandering and thinking what to do next, its brief length makes sense - it knows when to wrap things up. Did I mention that the environments are truly alien and alienating and that the story is actually fitting that tone of overall decay.

review_text:
Admittedly I don't believe there's anything that I can say here that hasn't already been repeated hundreds of times.

But as much as it pains me I cannot keep up with NGS anymore, initially I hated the game since I first tried it being a longtime player of base starting years ago on JP. While I wasn't keen on NGS I eventually warmed up to it and it became a somewhat fun time killer when Slayer released but I was never able to sit down and play the game for extended periods of time like other titles such as Final Fantasy XIV.

Every time I thought SEGA was taking a step forward into something better they have continued to take four steps back and it's grating, once you're caught up in levels and the story what's left? NGS EQs (Emergency Quests) are half baked and hardly replayable when compared to what the original PSO2 had to offer. Gone are a lot of the amazing set pieces that made quests like the Yamato battleship, Megatsu and even the Luminmech dogfights in space in exchange for uninspired "Falz" fight after another. DQs (Duel Quests) are an absolute joke asking the player to build entirely new armors and weapons just to meet DPS checks since the fights aren't scaled properly to 1-player, so you're telling me that even if I go out of my way to max out my build you're just releasing content that'll make me use a different set? Then you have the LQs (Limited Quests) which in my experience tend to just be "Fight this boss, then fight this one. Done.".

All this to say that SEGA has consistently done the bare-minimum required to keep this early access bullshit live using whales for AC scratches to fund it. To top it off they're now forcing their dwindling player base towards a far more invasive anti-cheat with the removal of nProtectGameGuard in favor of Wellbia.

There's more I could say but for the sake of saving you redundancy all you need to do is sift through the abundance of negative reviews and you'll see a lot of longtime players who share my sentiments. 

Fuck you SEGA, fuck you for killing one of my favorite games in favor of an experimental alpha test that you've dragged us through. I'm done.

review_text: Considering its age and history as one of the first truly successful modern indie games, World of Goo has aged brilliantly. Its characteristic physics puzzler gameplay remains intuitive and easy to pick up while offering variety, complexity, and real challenge throughout the course of the game, especially if you aim for the OCD flags. Still, the game’s most outstanding quality, and what led me to remember and return to it over 15 years after I first experienced it on the Wii, is its distinctive, eerie atmosphere. This is cultivated through its vivid art, excellent music, and witty narrative and worldbuilding methods, which coalesce to create a dark yet lighthearted, amusing yet pointed experience that is truly unique and only comparable to its recent sequel and 2D Boy/Tomorrow Corporation’s other games. No matter what games you enjoy, or even if you haven't played a game before, I would easily recommend World of Goo to anyone. Just like its eponymous googly-eyed black blobs, it will stick with you forever!

review_text:
Writing this after 2 hours of actual play time cause playing this game after completing the 3rd one is legitimately depressing. My first hour of playing the campaign of Just Cause 3 consisted of a brief exposition dump about characters you're made to care about like Dimah and Mario along with some exploring and capturing of the early outposts which was generally really fun. My first hour of Just Cause 4 was was being introduced to 'Bad Corporate Guy #1' and 'Bad General Woman #1' along with 'Rebel Woman with Vendetta against Bad General Woman'. After the least memorable intro to a game I've ever had the displeasure to sit through, I was immediately put off by the tether mods that i found to be more of an annoyance than anything, the next 10 minutes was "wow a tornado!", and then i spent the last 30 minutes of my first hour searching the wind outpost for breakers that would've taken 5 minutes had they been directly marked (like they would've been in the last game). I genuinely remember more of my first hour of the 3rd game than this one and I just started playing this 4 hours ago. I would 100% refund this game if i didn't go AFK and put myself over the 2 hour mark, which says a lot considering i got the game at a 90% discount, I'd honestly rather have my $10 back than subject myself to playing and finishing this game but it's in my library now so its gonna get finished, will edit review when done.
Edit: the mission based regions instead of the destructible outposts really doomed this game from the start. Progressing by blowing up outposts is something nobody wanted changed from the last game. The concept of front lines is cool but the execution just wasn't there. The fact that there are actual battles on the front line would be cool if these battles weren't just static battlefields, the line doesn't move to either side as you kill enemies they just endlessly spawn on one side of these big fields on the border of predetermined provinces. If they would've had outpost based progression like JC3 and implemented the frontline mechanic with an actual moving front that you could manually interact with instead of taking preset regions, this would be a better and more successful game than JC3. Also idk what happened between JC3 and 4 but Rico just seems so much more bitter in this game. His mood and tone in both games really mirrors my experience with either of the games, in JC3 Rico was making jokes and seemed to be having fun as I was enjoying the experience, in this game it just feels like he's doing this cause he has to, as opposed to doing it 'Just Cause'
TLDR: Play the 3rd game this is too repetitive, if i had a dollar every time they asked me to flip a breaker or hack a console id have enough money to buy the Just Cause IP and make a better game myself

review_text:
This is another time where I wish the "Informative" option was available for regular reviews instead of only being there for curators. But I am gonna complain, so I guess this is a negative review.

It just doesn't give me what I bought the game for. I wanted fun combos like Tony Hawk Pro Skater and fun platforming like Jet Set Radio Future. I got neither. The combos hinge entirely on you accumulating boost meter to do the boost moves which are the only way to get points, rather than hinging on how long you can keep a combo going, with as many moves as possible. 

The scoring system was pure bullshit, by the way. It only increases its multiplier if you touch a billboard or you *lean into a curve on a rail*. So not how many *tricks* you can do. Or how varied the chain is. No, your multiplier is entirely driven by doing every single corner in the level to acquire a multiplier because you start spamming boost dash moves to reach the achievement requirement.

The platforming is also not there because they've made the levels humongous and barren, leading to you having to basically manual your way to every rail because the longest unbroken chain of rails in the game you can do is maybe 4 short ones in the first level. The best levels was the Pyramid, and that's only because it's  small enough that there's actually skips and techs you can do in it with loads of ramps to jump around on. There are very few times where you need to manual on that level.

Also why the hell are there so many inward-facing billboard chains? Like that's supposed to be a forbidden tech in the original games but in this one, apparently, dashing backwards into the poster that was facing away from the one you just jumped off is just how the game is actually meant to be. In fact, why were posters so rare in general? There were so many spots that could have been improved by having posters to jump between.

You also have the graffiti system from Jet Set Radio except they forgot the reason why it worked in Jet Set Radio was because it's an extremely slow game where enemies will actually try to stop you from tagging stuff. In this game, you go fast as fuck boosting everywhere to the point where the most dangerous police enemy is the turrets that stop you from just leaving. And when you go fast as fuck, that tagging just breaks the flow. You should have had it be only for L-XL graffitis so you can place those ones that you have to stop for in meaningful spots, instead of having us pause in mid air just to do circles on the joystick.

I don't understand the point of the heat system being in the game. Like it genuinely is just a minor nuisance the entire time. It would have been much more impactful to have properly designed police battles throughout the game instead of randomly deciding "You have to fight police snipers now but one of them is wearing a white helmet actually". And speaking of the police:

Where the hell is the voice acting for cutscenes? I've had Tryce exposition dump me the entire layout and plot of every zone I go to, but he's just not doing the Professor K narration. He just *subtitles* as if he was doing a Professor K voice. This is relevant  to the previous section because the police assaults are just missing the aesthetics of HQ TO ALL SQUADS. Like I don't even notice the police is on me until the turret cutscene plays. You got the heat system from GTA. Did you miss the part where GTA has police radio chatter when the chase starts? Or would that have ruined that little late game joke where the character says he can't listen to police radio chatter?

Also, the police fights are just worthless. Like it is just not fun to run back and forth boost dashing to knock them down. The Golden Rhinos had to be boost dashed because they were late game enemies, I do not want to boost dash a basic police officer 3 times to get them down. Also for the next game you can just remove the attack buttons, no one is doing that, that's garbage. Just make enemies with a clear "stun" condition that lets you tag them. You did it with the robot enemies and they're fun to fight.

They put mumble rap in the soundtrack. I don't think they know why any more than we do. I think they saw rap was on the Jet Set Radio Future soundtrack and wanted to emulate that but they forgot one very important component: Aisle 7 was the song for Rokkaku-dai Heights. It perfectly fit the vibe of skating down in the slums during late afternoon. Rocking the Mic was the song for the sewers. It perfectly fit the vibes of hopping half pipes and random power cables in the sewer system. There is not a level where mumble rap fits. Or rap in general. None of them have *that vibe*. So, soundtrack fails a vibe check on some of the songs. But at least *your* Birthday Cake was not atrocious.

The graffiti markers were very buggy the entire time and I don't know why they got rid of the hovering arrow/circle system that was in the Jet Set Radio games because it made it easy to tell from the side that you have to tag this wall. And also since it's a physical object it's much less prone to shader bugs.

The character designs are questionable. You start the game as *some guy* then you get the robot head which is sick, but then, you turn back into *some guy*. Like imagine the most generic looking hipster you can. The kind that wears a beanie. That is your main character when he doesn't have his robot head on. Now imagine a youtuber that grooms children. That is what the main character looked like before having the robot head. Then you meet *some guy in a winter coat* and *some girl* in a winter coat and you fight *some girls in a winter coat*, because apparently winter coats are just peak design. There's also alot of overdesigning going on. Like Solace has the whole crash test dummy aesthetic and the happy merchant face... And then also angel wings, for some reason. Rave looks really cool, until you turn her around and you see her goofy ass  helmet htat has no reason to be there. Rise straight up wears a bathing suit underneath a winter coat, what is it with these winter coats? Mesh is a random bald kid in an oversized t-shirt wearing a VR headset who screams LESSGOOOOOO and LESKETTIT, which you would be extremely familiar with if you watch twitch, and he's one of the more coherent designs.

Oh, right speaking of Twitch, there's alot of zoomer lingo that does not age well in this game. One of the character says "yaaaas". That hasn't been a thing in like 5 years. Another of the characters also says "fam". *Also* hasn't been a thing in a few years.

Overall, it really just seems like everything they tried to do differently was done differently for the sake of being different, without understanding why it was done that way in the original games they got the ideas from.

Anyways, I recommend it if you're looking for "An indie game in the same genre as Jet Set Radio", but I absolutely cannot recommend it if you're looking for a spiritual successor to jet set radio. The vibes failed, the funk is not present.

review_text:
On release, there was a major error that prevented people from playing it for the first day and a bit (depending on timezone). However, since then patches have been fairly speedy and solved all major problems.

In terms of story, if you've played previous Hakuouki games, this ends around the halfway point (just a bit after leaving Kyoto, when the major twist happens to most of the ROs). This is because they added 5 new routes (Sanan, Shinpachi, and two new entirely characters including Sakamoto Ryoma), in addition to adding several new scenes to both the common and individual routes. Personally, Sanan's route is one of my new favourites, up there right alongside Shinpachi and Harada, although I won't spoil it since I was fairly surprised by the direction his route took, given his roles in other people's routes in the other games.

Personally, I liked this game, both in its own right and as adding additional content to the series which had otherwise been (as far as I'm aware) fairly static in terms of the main game other than porting it to other platforms. It's a little disappointing that we can't play Edo Blossoms yet, but only because I can't wait to see how the new routes are resolved and what other new content is added to the original routes. Would totally recommend, especially with the story pack (although the stories are very short and only cover 4 routes, so I'd buy them if they go on sale again) since it adds some lovely additional stuff roughly around halfway through this game (although you have to play them in the menus so I'd recommend finishing the relevant route first before playing it).

I really love how the enemy and friends of kirito interacts with each other. Such a treat i hope there will be many characters to come.

Gameplay wise its a good action rpg not on level as GBFR tho, still clunky on some ways especially the camera. But its still good.
Coop overall is fun they implement a system where we must level up to unlock our skill, i havent been grinding much, its pretty much still alive, i can find matches without waiting, i play on Asia server its not that laggy, iam playing from SEA.
For characters, there is 21 free character from the enemy and friends of kirito, they all have unique move set.

Overall the game is not worth the price if you're just buying it for the gameplay, but if youre a SAO fan that watches all of the anime and movies you will love the story and characters.

I hope they cook something for the next big update. i had hope for this game.

No update and the game got boring real fast i only play when there is exp up event. This is a live service game but as of this updated review there is still no new updates after 2 months, i cant recommend this game.

I have the 400 day unlock from previous plays and was a player at launch the game changed a lot for better and worse but there's a lot of worse.

 On the plus side stories have continued to evolve, more voice overs from original cast members that were recorded just for STO also improve the game a lot.

 The minus is the game is extremely expensive and very little has been done to update the engine graphics for 10 years and while not extensively buggy it does have enough to give the presence of a unfinished product.

 When I say the game is expensive it's very expensive: 
*The lockboxes are a dollar each and have terrible odds
*The latest ships range from $30 to $200(for the pack of stuff you don't want)
*Ships have consoles that are powerful which you probably want
*The older ships run a range from $12-$25
*You need to buy a service to have more than 2 million of the in-game currency
*Retrain tokens cost money
*There's a post 65 level and it costs money.
*You can level up your ship, this costs money.
*There's a second hidden store called the "Lobi store" you buy lobi with keys so lobi cost money
*For some reason there's something called "Mudd Market" part of the store which is supposed to have "frequent sales" but I have yet to see one so what it is actually is an excuse to mark up the price on random items(As much as $400!!) and claim it's "because these items aren't on sale".
*Finally, to top it all off, there is a way to earn store currency in game THEORETICALLY. The system is like a stock exchange(for some reason) where you need to sell your in game currency to other players for the store currency except nobody wants to trade the store currency for the in-game currency so it doesn't work.

review_text:
This is one of those times I really wish Steam had a "mixed" review option. The good stuff is genuinely really good, but a recommendation doesn't feel right considering the problems and the current price ($40, or $20 on sale).

Good stuff: 

+ Visuals/Aesthetic
+ Soundtrack
+ Skateboarding/Biking/Skating - Feels really good, but the negative section below makes this point a little bit moot. 
+ Level design (sans collectibles)

Not so good stuff:

-Difficulty - The game is absurdly easy and you will beat the AI's score by a wide margin every time, which gets boring very quickly.

-Collectibles (incl. graffiti) - To progress in the game, you have to paint graffiti throughout levels. You have to find enough of the predetermined spots to write over to get the attention of that area's crew. Probably a third of my playtime was spent trying to figure out where these damn things are so I could progress to the next boss, rather than actually enjoying the skateboarding/etc aspect of the game. I don't mind if optional collectibles are frustrating to find, but graffiti being the only thing you need to progress kind of sucks.

I really wish progression would've been based on skill instead. Get a certain multiplier, or combo duration, or total score to continue, because the skateboarding/etc aspect of the game is actually very fun but there is no reason to go for high scores unless you're aiming for achievements.

-Police - As you paint graffiti throughout an area, police will arrive and shoot at you. They aren't difficult, but they are very annoying at higher heat levels. You can fight them but the hand-to-hand combat (that exists for some reason) is incredibly boring and slow. If police were removed from the game entirely, it would be an overall improvement.

-Tricks - You can press one of three buttons to do a simple trick. You can combine any of the three with left trigger to do the same trick but get more points. There aren't any interesting combos, there's no real depth, you just press buttons to get points. It's not like points really matter much anyway because you will win every time by just button mashing.

-Health - You are essentially immortal, but you do have a health bar that regens very quickly if you do take damage. Aside from the final boss, the only time I ever actually ran out of health and died was when my character got stuck in place (only happened once, not a recurring bug) and police shot me until I died. This feels like a completely useless mechanic alongside police in general.

review_text:
Initially the game wouldn't run in full screen (this seems like a rather common issue) until I searched around for some settings to change in the game's options.ini. Ultimately that's more of an inconvenience and not the reason for my negative review, but I just wanted to mention it for others having issues.

Going into this game I was really sold on the premise as I understood it: a graphically simple game that would scare you in part by making it appear as though bad things were happening on your pc outside of the game. Unfortunately in reality the game is pretty standard horror fare. There's creepy music and the scares are almost exclusively just things jumping out at you in-game while you try to solve tedious puzzles. That would be fine except that the visuals are nauseatingly blurry and pixelated and the movement is super janky. The "meta" aspect of the game seems to be relegated to putting some files in a specific game folder on your desktop, having to close and restart the game often (which adds to the tedium) and, at least in one instance, watching a video on youtube. Really not that scary or surprising.

The game is reasonably priced for what it is, I guess, but I don't think it's worth the time to play it.

review_text:
Dead Space for modern audiences.
It's alright, just manage your expectations: this isn't a game for players, it's a product for investors. It ticks the boxes but it doesn't innovate or respect you.

[hr][/hr]
Good bits:

- Lots of accessibility options: dyslexic font, color-coding for game items (enemies, hazards, etc.), subtitles font settings (size, color, background). Although, font settings apply only to subtitles, and not to other text such as item descriptions in the store which are barely readable.

- Interesting combat system: evading and chaining different melee and ranged attacks. But it gets really boring really fast, I started the game at medium difficulty and quickly dropped to low because having to hit each and every enemy a dozen or two times for them to go down is not that fun.

- Skippable cutscenes.

[hr][/hr]
Bad bits, in no particular order:

- Unskippable intro logos. Fortunately the movie files can be deleted or renamed.

- Stupid save system: there are auto-saves at plot checkpoints, and there are manual saves anywhere, except they also save only the checkpoints. And as far as I can tell, any checkpoint is saved only once, so if you stumble into an auto-save but then backtrack to pickup any leftover items - the only way to save that backtracking is to progress further to next checkpoint.

- Can't use GRP (kinesis) to pick up items like ammo and health.

- Enemies don't drop loot if killed with with certain types of environmental hazards like huge fans or other chopping/grinding things.

- Gamepad controls are not editable, and the default scheme is... suboptimal. Some buttons (d-pad) bind to several actions, while others (L3/R3) are completely unused.

- Ranged weapons are boring. There are 5 types, and they basically differ only in clip size and fire rate. Maybe in damage too but that's not noticeable. In general, they all shoot bullets in one way or another and they all have different ammo types so you have to carry every type separately, but they take extra time and attention to swap between them and keep them all reloaded.

- The "alt-fire" mode is pointless because it spends N times more ammo for N times more damage so it's not in fact an upgrade.

- Selling or otherwise handling items in the store requires long-press (which is good) but buying weapon upgrades is instant so if you accidentally click on wrong thing, you will spend a potentially sizable chunk of your cash on an upgrade that you might not have wanted.

- "Blind" enemies are a joke. You can cram a dozen of them into a room, and stealth-kill ALL of them. None of them will aggro as long as you do not exit crouching state and do not move closer to any of them than certain threshold, even though "stealth kill" itself is accompanied by a hefty amount of screaming and panting. However once they do get aggroed, they will chase you to the end of the [strike]Earth[/strike] Callisto even if you run away and try to hide.

- Closer to the end of the game they trick player by putting a puny enemy (a parasite larvae, found throughout the game) into a box that typically contains valuable loot. I guess the intent was to increase the suspense by breaking player's trust in loot containers, except they did it to three containers in a row, which completely defeats the purpose. Already after the 2nd container I couldn't care less if another slimy thing will jump on me or not, and the 3rd one drove the final nail in the coffin of horror and atmosphere.

- Final boss is impressive visually but poorly executed mechanically. He's invulnerable to bullets when he's in his first, weaker, human form. I unloaded all ammo from half the weapons in his face and the scene didn't change. The way to progress is to smack him a couple times with melee weapon. The logic left the room...

- Characters are pathetic. Kudos to the actors, they did their part well, but the writing is utterly flat. Saying farewell to Lucatiel of Mirrah was moving, watching Elias die was not. And they have roughly the same amount of interaction with their respective protagonists!

- For half of its duration, the game takes away your ability to run. Sometimes the plot "requires" that you walk and talk alongside another character, even though there's loot to gather on the other side of the (sometimes pretty big) room. Other times the main character just randomly slows to a walk. I guess it might have something to do with the terrain but if so then it's extremely unintuitive and inconsistent. Dead Space had a distinct sound and walking animation for "sticky" floor, this game does not. A game is supposed to be an interactive media; I, the player, am supposed to be in control of my actions; limiting that at random for no reason is [b]INFURIATING[/b].

[hr][/hr]
Update: spelling.

review_text:
I got this game heavily discounted, and if I hadn't I'd feel like a fool.

I love the concept, controlling a group of characters through Edo period Japan, tactical gameplay, and fantastic art direction is what the game promises, and that seemed like a pretty great time for someone who really loves strategy and tactics games.


In execution though, this game is a slightly broken and frustrating attempt to blend genres. It attempts to be an RTS and a turned based tactics game at the same time, but ends up feeling more like a port of a mobile puzzle combat game centered on stealth.

The issues this game suffers from that are worth mentioning are numerous;

-Terrible default control scheme.
    The default controls are far from intuitive and frustrating
    Alternate control schemes aren't particularly good either, leading into my next point
-Imprecise controls and bad indicators/tool tips really compound the controls issues.
    There is no click to confirm feature
    The game will frequently highlight a target, but your click won't register for that target, leading to bad inputs and 
    frustrating, avoidable deaths
-Pathing is absolutely abhorrent.
    Runs like badly cannibalized pathing from 90's RTS games
    Completely at odds with the games focus on precision and tactics
    No movement preview to alert you to how tragically bad the pathing is
-Shadow Mode is poorly implemented.
    Total lack of any meaningful way to time out actions means you are left to trial and error most of the time
    Suffers from terrible UI layout, bad pathing and imprecise inputs
-Dialogue and character interactions are poorly written and undermine the fantastic presentation of the game
    Awkward delivery doesn't help bland, forgettable dialogue
    Characters feel shallow and cliche


The game hosts a variety of features which, if properly implemented could have made for an interesting and engaging game, but it ends up a mess.

review_text:
I don’t think this is a very good game.

First in order to be a good game you have to, well, be a game. I know it’s a point-and-click title but can they not at least make whatever extra puzzle/gameplay we have a little bit more interesting? The inclusion of these extra bits shows that clearly thought has been put into making things less monotonous than going to A, picking up B, going back to A, rinse and repeat. Yet they can’t go that extra mile to develop these much-needed gameplay bits more?

This first point would hardly be worth complaining about if the story is good. And a good story is more than a good premise, a good twist, or a good ending. Let me rip the band-aid off right now: The story is not well-written: There may be a good story in there somewhere but since it’s told from the focal points of two puerile scientists and written by someone with the sensibility of a Tik-tok-roaming Gen Z edgelord, whatever gravitas the story could’ve achieved is instead constantly sucked out by out-of-place jokes and awkward soppy dialogue transitions where characters would suddenly bring up topics out of the blue just to push the story forward and desperately make you feel something. I’m not saying every game needs to have subtle or edgy writing, only that if your goal is to create a heartfelt story, the last thing you want is to take the attempt so seriously that you lose sight of how it looks “from the outside”. The fact that this game’s writing is so totally inconsistent makes me wonder if it could really benefit from an editor’s input.

I can’t say I had a good time with this. The soundtrack can be lovely but mostly just sounds as cliche as a lot of the tricks the game pulls to elicit a reaction from the player.

2371, to some that is a crazy amount of hours, to others it is not even half of theirs. Would i recommend this game? Yes but No, it's not a hard No but i wouldn't recommend to a new player for the sole reason you need to sink a silly amount of numbers into the game to learn the basics but also to actually enjoy the amount of perks you need to buy nearly every character just to be in for a chance of competing against good players. Now the review, this is a killer mains perspective so you survivor mains move along you will just disagree with everything boohoo killer main yes yes.

So I've played, streamed and put so much time into this game that it was the sole game i played for years now, patch after patch, perk addition after perk addition, toxic message after toxic message later I've learned what a pile of poop this game really is, beneath all the bugs, imbalances and overall mess of a game this is, is the most toxic community only second to League of Legends I've ever come across!! Had a decent game with 8 hooks, 2 hooks on 3 people and 1 dead, nah trash should get good while watching 3 lots of tea bags at the exit gate because you played "fair", so you change it up, get 2 survivors out earlier and avoiding the good looper BANG!!! TUNNELLER, UNFAIR, REPORTED, CAMPER, PLAYING LIKE A TOXIC PERSON!!!, You can't win.

Now let's move onto the devs. I am sick and tired of seeing the immense hand holding to one side it's unreal, look at patch 9.3.0 that is soon to come out (PTB.... we will see), it's honestly a disgrace that survivors are getting countless base kit additions, x-ray, shield, speed, stealth etc.... oh but don't worry the killer gets some extra speed after hooking, but he will lose it as soon as they see a survivor... but don't worry we will throw in an extra 200bp for each hook!!! Talk about the 2nd child treatment oh my gosh. The fact they don't even play test their own game (Jim Beam is an obvious fact that they don't) is laughable. This game is digging it's own grave and i'm tired of thinking team killer will have an easy time. The last survey i closed, i didn't even finish because it's insulting that the options for why you uninstalling or not enjoying the game features 2 anti fun killer options basically asking Survivor mains why they are not enjoying... what about why i'm not enjoying? Why is there no "Gens are too fast" "Too many Endurance perks" "Base kit is too oppressive" "Why can i only kick a gen 8 times but Survs can heal infinite times and reset" or any other killers are not having fun options but nope they only care about the favourite child. 

Before anyone wonders... yes i play Survivor, i have around 1K of my play time survivor as well and boy can you feel the game is designed around them just by the game play. So, to most i would never recommend this game but apart of me still holds stupid hope that they will think about both sides and reward the killer for playing how "They are supposed too" you know killers are meant to play a certain way to make sure the survivors are having fun too. The more i type all this out the more i realise i am just no longer enjoying the game and for the first time in years i actually am close to calling it daylight.

Hope this didn't feel too much like a crying rant as yes it does look like it but i guess it's just come this far and that is how i am viewing the game! The game at its core is fantastic but has too many issues. Until the devs actually decide to think about the other team I'm going to give it a rest for a while. Surv queues are going to sky rocket with how many killer mains will end up leaving.

review_text:
Man what a disappointment this was. I played all the way through the first three games and was completely stoked for this one but it is just a huge downgrade and incredibly annoying to play.
--There is way less customization and freedom in how you play than in SGW3. There are few weapons with very limited customization. Most gear and utilities that make the game fun (different types of bullets, drones, etc) are locked behind hours of grind to get currency.
--Assault rifles are so inaccurate they are completely useless. You can't his anything farther than 20m away. 
--AI is frustrating and annoying. If you miss a shot, every enemy on the map (even if alone and hundreds of meters away) is immediately on alert. There's no sounding of an alarm, no calling out over the radio, it's just boom, everyone knows where you are. Same thing for when someone tags your location, every enemy immediately knows exactly where you are. It's infuriating. Between this and the useless assault rifles, you might as well quit and start over if you get detected, because you have virtually no chance of success once you've missed a shot.
--The game flow itself is not fun. They tried to do some sort of session-based mini-open-world thing where you spend a few hours at a time in an open world area and try to complete certain objectives without leaving. If you leave, your progress is basically reset and you start the area over. So it's not really open world, because you can't change loadout whenever you want or make permanent progress, but it's also not really mission based/linear, because you have to complete multiple missions in the same open world in a single session in order to complete objectives and get currency. It's really the worst of both worlds and makes the pacing of the game awkward and annoying. Maybe it's better if you've got 3-4 hours at a time to sit down and play? I don't know, but I did not enjoy the pacing at all.
--There's really no story to speak of. Again, a major downgrade from SGW3

review_text:
Dammit, it was starting so good... I really liked it more than Dead Space (both original and remake). Where Dead Space seemed to build the atmosphere mainly by turning off lights and jump-scaring you with monsters, this one seemed to be doing much more than that.

Firstly, it was using proper cinematics when required to show intense situations, to let you feel "the strain" of it all. The way camera was moving, the way the frame was "dirtied" (this does not necessarily mean actual dirt, it means that a frame is not "perfect" and that can help with immersion). It felt like they are really putting you into the game, at last to an extent.

Secondly, there were just those little things here and there, like little unnecessary movements made by characters, they made it feel just a little bit more "natural". And it was also little details in the environment, too. In Deas Space I always wanted to run, and could not, because I needed flashlight, which works only if you aim. Callisto is much brighter, but I never wanted to run here, because it just felt wrong. Something was telling me, that I need to be cautious, and move slowly, even though logic told me that this is a safe area, and everything is scripted either way.

There was also combat. Yes, it turned out to be somewhat repetitive pretty quickly, but the way you were introduced to it, and the way it felt... Like "heavy", "difficult", "important". You know, like, with fighting scenes in movies: sometimes they have this weight, that you feel even though you are not participating.

My point is, I wanted to play the game further. Yes, the second prisoner (Elias, if I remember correctly) seemed a bit forced as a guide, perhaps, since he is a prisoner, he probably should be that knowledgeable if he is in his cell most of the time. But there is enough doubt regarding him, that maybe there will be an explanation. I really wanted to know what will be next, was really excited...
Until on the 2nd evening I could not load my saves. Half of them. Apparently, in some obscure cases the save files become 200+ megabytes instead of 200+ kilobytes, and that makes them unloadable: the main menu just hangs, at some point changes into black screen, but nothing loads anyway.

But, ok, I cleaned those up, lost maybe 10 minutes of playtime, not that big of a deal. I mean until within next 1 minutes from that save I need to go through a door, but instead of loading the room, I get a black screen. And this bug is (or at least was) present on PS4/PS5 even. And there is no solution for it: for some people restarting the game from the very beginning worked, but for some - nothing worked at all. I've tried multiple things on PC to no avail, and I am not that invested to replay almost 2 hours to find out if that door will open for me or not.

So trying for a refund. Luckily, in total I got just a little bit over 2 hours, and since there is evidence of bugs, there is a chance that I will get my money back.

review_text:
I have seen a lot of praise for the story for To The Moon. This is one time where the praise was due. What I saw of the story was very well done. The problem I had was that most everything else, aside from an awesome soundtrack, was not. Had this been a kinetic visual novel I would have enjoyed it much more. Had it had better thought out puzzles, such as Rakuen, I would have enjoyed it much more. Sadly what I was left with was a quality story that to enjoy I had to wade through input issues; low frame rates; and poor puzzles. The input issues were such that when I clicked on a location for my character to move they sometimes would go there. Other times they would go part way and stop. The same would happen when I clicked on objects to investigate, sometimes they would go right to it and others only a bit and stop. The puzzles mostly consisted of mini games of “preparing” mementos to go further back in Johnny’s memories. To do this you had to clear away white blocks on a picture by pressing buttons that correspond to columns and rows. In doing so you would creat white blocks elsewhere. You had to anticipate where they would form (there is a pattern) and you could them clear them all. I found this pretty annoying. Even the basic puzzles of finding keys had issues at times. I was supposed to read this passage of a book to find a key hidden there but it wasn’t until the third time I read the passage that my character found the key.

	I played To The Moon on Linux. It never crashed on me once. There are no graphics options at all. Alt-Tab doesn’t work. It uses a total of 223MB of disk space. It uses the RPG Maker XP engine. The game allows you to manually save at any time outside of dialogue and has 3 save slots. There is also an auto save feature for those who prefer that. During play my GPU usage was 3-7%; my VRAM usage was 537-594MB; my CPU usage was 0-3%; my RAM usage was 2.6-3GB and my frame rate was a constant 40 FPS. Why it was stuck at 40 I have no idea. 

	I got through 79 minutes of To The Moon before the I came to the conclusion that the story wasn’t worth putting up with the gameplay. I paid $2.52 for the game and would say that is very much a steal for the story but way overpriced for what I put up with for it. Your enjoyment of the game will hinge on whether you value story and whether you have similar pet peaves as me with gameplay.

My Score: 5.5/10

Some cool ideas, overshadowed by some of the worst. There's a revolver that practically shoots satchel charges, a sniper that burns the enemies you view through the scope, a machine pistol that builds up ramping damage-over-time the longer you shoot, the list goes on. 

But for some reason, they tried to make this into yet another souls-clone. There's a way too small stamina bar and you lose stamina if you get hit, which isn't necessarily always the player's fault. Player character is really gimped seemingly only for the purpose of enabling a leveling system. I never felt like my character was getting stronger when leveling up, but only getting closer to the level where he should've been from the start. 

Enemy packs can spawn in ridiculous clusters right in front of player spawn on some maps and at least a couple of times I swear I got hit before even fully loading into the map. 

To some people a lot of these kinds of issues are forgivable, considering the game is in early access, but all I'm saying is that they have a lot of work to do with the full release being planned for early 2026. 


Also I would say that the currently 92% positive rating on Steam is not to be trusted, as only 2.7% of players finished the early access build (as of writing this review), but it's not like this is the first game people rate highly without even finishing it.

review_text:
[h1] Where The Scorn Don't Shine [/h1]

I wanted to like this game, seeing the trailers made me have so many questions about the world of Scorn and how it works. I understand the developers wanted the story to be told through environment, but there is almost zero deviation of said environment as you are stuck in the same building almost the entirety of the game and leaves you with more questions and none answered. The highlights of the game are pretty much all shown in the trailer and there is no exploration aspect when most paths lead to an locked area or dead end, if anything it's a walking sim. While the game isn't intended at all to be a "shooter", I feel like the variety of weapons speak differently especially with the main focus of the last 1/5th of the game primarily being restricted to "shooting", even having to solve puzzles with your weapon despite the game being "not a shooter". Even then all enemies are way too easy to escape that there is almost no point of having any weapons beside the first tool you get, it seems like the developers couldn't decide whether or not to have guns be in the game but eventually were forced to due to the puzzle design and [spoiler] unnecessary end boss fight [/spoiler]. Just when the game starts getting good, it ends just as abrupt as how the game began. The audio is nice and music is great as expected but the graphics aren't exactly anything to write home about as they are on par with games that came out years ago like Doom or Resident Evil remakes. I feel that if Scorn came out when atmospheric survival horror was more popular it would have been an absolute hit, but this game doesn't do anything defining for that genre gamers haven't already seen.

Overall I can't say I recommend this game, it took me 5 hours to 100% and even on sale for 36$ that is just not worth paying 7$ for each hour of this game and I feel bad for those who have waited years for this. It doesn't seem to shine in any of its aspects, it has plenty of gore but nothing that really gives you the "shock factor" or makes you feel in immediate danger, just monsters making noises crawling around you that can easily be heard and therefore avoided. None of the puzzles were really hard, mostly just fetch quests for other items or doing things in a certain order seemingly to make the game feel longer. The atmosphere is GOOD, if you're okay with seeing what you saw in the trailer for 5 hours and the ending ruined anything that happened in the game. To me there are tons more games that do this genre much better, Abe's odyssey series or Amnesia to name a couple are much more engaging in surreal story telling, art style, exploration, horror, and came out decades ago.

3/10

review_text:
Short Review: 
Yes. Get this. The worst that can happen is maybe you don't fall in love right away, there's no real lose here. 10/10 

Longer Review:
PSO2 NGS is one of the coolest games in general and it's even more impressive considering it's an MMO. I have a limited history with the series, starting with PSO2 base before the global launch, playing on the Japanese servers. It wass a long time ago, but I was really addicted to it. It had actually fallen off my radar, though, and I missed the global release, not realizing it was a thing until NGS. I tried it then and it seemed okay, but there wasn't a TON to do then, not as much as before, anyway. That is no longer the case.

My friends and I were looking for something to do after coming off of FFXIV. For us, Eorzea had lost its appeal and we wanted to try to find something, anything, to fill the gap it left. On a whim, I decided to give NGS a shot and after a night of streaming some of it, everyone was on board and we have been daily junkies for this since. There is a lot to talk about here, and I'll try to keep my thoughts organized and brief. 

Story - As anyone who tried FFXIV might relate to, good story isn't all that common in MMOs. NGS doesn't care about that trope and crafts an interesting story that keeps itself grounded and real, produces interesting characters that go through powerful arcs, and even functions to provide lore reasons for gameplay mechanics. It is hard to discuss without spoiling later parts, but as someone who likes to poke fun at things like "well this is obviously because it's a game," I found the answers they eventual reveal to be very satisfying.

The basic plot involves the player character and gives a sense of importance without falling into the pitfalls of a "chosen one" affair that can often give a feeling of disconnect between story and regular MMO life. Progression feels natural, but it also doesn't waste a lot of time. A power player can rush through the whole thing relatively quickly. It's great for those who care about story and not a huge barrier for those who don't. 

Gameplay - NGS has a lot of style and flash in its combat, but it also has the substance to back it up. The controls are solid and movement is fun. It may seem like a lot at first, and it definitely can be, but even if you don't pick up playstyles quickly, the end game content is still accessible.

Combos are done more similarly to an action game rather than a traditional MMORPG, using a variety of moves to pull off complex attacks. Spells and the like can be charged by holding down a button rather than waiting on a timer. Dodging feels great and parrying, while harder to perfect, is extremely potent and fulfilling. Fights are also a lot of fun, with bosses using a set group of attacks in a random order across various phases. The added platforming during really keeps you on your toes!

Music - A+++. It's Sega. This is their thing. The entire soundtrack is so great, even the simple things. 

Graphics - For a game built on top of an older game, NGS is extremely gorgeous. The colors are so vibrant, the landscapes breathtaking. There are particle effects all over and the lighting is divine. That all said, if you don't have the best machine, it still runs great on lower settings while not sacrificing the spirit of the higher end visuals.

Other stuff that I don't know how to categorize - There has been controversy with this game and some people aren't thrilled with Sega, so I want to take a second to talk to those issues. NGS took the place of the original Phantasy Star Online 2 and having experienced some of the best that game had to offer, I completely get it. A lot of what PSO2 was isn't in NGS, but there is still a lot of love and passion and even humility to be felt from the developers. They are working on building something great with little updates coming constantly and larger ones spread out a bit more. Compared to other major games in the MMO field, NGS is getting a ton of attention and care from the people working on it. I don't want to drag other things here, but if you know, you know. If you don't, lucky you, I hope you realize how good you are eating!

There is also the concern of Gacha elements. Yes, you can buy in-game currency to get special random ticket items for fashion. Yes, it's not as straight forward as picking something from a catalogue and ordering it. However, with how the game's economy works, it is not that big of an issue. First, AC (in-game currency) is entirely optional and not needed to play the game in its entirity. You never have to spend a penny here if you don't want to. And that brings me to the second point, which is personal shops. The same items that you can pay to get tickets for can be sold and purchased on shops run by players. A free to play player can grind to buy from another player, and those who pay and don't get what they want can resell and purchase something they do. All games monetize in some way or another, and considering how much here is just given away and how the Gacha has workarounds, this is probably the least predatory monetization I've ever seen in an MMO. 

Oh, yeah, and the housing is absolutely bonkers good. 


Edit notes I forgot to add - 
PSO2 Base is also available to play in near full with this. 

Line Strike was just added and it's a strangely great card game system. Unique, easy to understand, tough to master.

Edit 2: I wanted the game nomination badge thing. This is a labor of love and it probably won't be on the radar for that award, but I think it deserves it. 

Oh also, there's a really funny official comic that comes out weekly and it's great.

review_text:
Title: “.hack//G.U. Last Recode: Sword Art Online’s Cousin That Actually Makes Sense”


---

Hook:
“I came for a nostalgic anime MMORPG experience, stayed because I couldn’t stop yelling ‘WHY IS EVERYONE SO DRAMATIC?!’”


---

Key Features:

1. Story:
An immersive plot where everyone acts like losing in a video game is a world-ending tragedy.
“I’m trapped in a coma because of a game!” Sir, just unplug your router.


2. Combat:
Button-mashing brilliance that makes you feel like a god... until you realize you forgot to block.
Pro tip: Spam skills. Strategy is for losers.


3. Graphics:
They upgraded the visuals, but I’m still haunted by PS2-era cutscene stares.
Faces may look better, but the angst is still pixel-perfect.




---

Personal Experience:
“I spent an hour customizing my character only to remember... you’re stuck with edgy emo-kid Haseo for the entire game. On the bright side, his fashion screams ‘Hot Topic employee of the month.’”


---

Relatable Humor:

“The party AI: brilliant when healing others, but absolutely useless when healing me.”

“When I finally found that one rare item... only to discover it’s worse than the starter gear.”

“The email system in the game is so realistic that I started avoiding them in real life too.”



---

Pro-Con List:
Pros:

Deep story with twists and turns that make Game of Thrones look tame.

Nostalgia overload for anyone who remembers blowing into PS2 memory cards.

You can date your party members, because nothing says ‘romance’ like dungeons and trauma bonding.


Cons:

Haseo’s voice acting is 90% screaming.

Repetitive grinding. The enemies are sick of me farming them, and honestly, so am I.

Too much menu navigation. It’s like playing a PowerPoint presentation, but with swords.



---

Verdict:
“If you’ve ever wanted to experience an anime MMORPG without the actual crippling despair of losing to PvP players, this is for you. Just be ready to emotionally commit to shouting, ‘HASEO, NO!’ at least 20 times.”

Rating: 9/10. Would log in to The World again.

In my opinion, give the game a pass. Especially at this price.

review_text:
This game is honestly a mess and a nightmare to play.

Same missions over and over (destroy the generators, flip the switch, hack the terminal, raise the transmitter, and then the dreaded defend said transmitter). Rinse, repeat ad infinitum.

Horrible UI and controls in general.

Driving makes you go mad, and with the amount of driving in this game, good luck. The camera angle sucks, and no way to change it. While driving you will get stuck on every little piece of debris on the road and will constantly spin out of control, and crash.

Terrible missions that are borderline impossible. Defend X mission objective - good luck without some of the DLC with overpowered weapons and vehicles. Waves of enemy tanks spawning from nowhere that will blow your defense object to hell before you even know where the missile came from.

HORRID performance. The game will stutter at times, will go from 160 fps to 20, will microstutter, and some of the "fixes" are hilarious. One common fix is to unplug your ethernet cable to fix stuttering. Even blocking all online components of this game doesn't fix the stuttering / lag, but does help a tad.

The frontlines part of the game aren't bad, just badly implemented. Just Cause 2 and 3 had it down where you just blow ♥♥♥♥ up, in this one, it doesn't matter. You don't "create Chaos" like in the previous installments, instead you fly into a base, flip some breakers, kill endless waves of enemies, die from a single sniper/rocket shot from nowhere, reload the save, and try again.

review_text:
*SPOILER FREE* 

If there was a 'mixed' recommendation button I could have selected for this game, I'd have picked it.

Conceptually Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts is very simple: A "realistic" sniping mechanic, a bunch of ducks in a row, and many a high vantage point from which to snipe them to your heart's content. Additionally there's a nice array of gadgets and secondary weapons to play with and upgrade, some of which are very entertaining (turrets, sidearm laser sights, gas mines, and a recon drone to name a few). Charmingly enough, there's also a bona fide RPG layer which adds some much-needed complexity and replayability to what could otherwise end up being a repetitive shooting gallery.

All that being said, the game has some serious, incredibly frustrating flaws. You've probably seen many comments criticizing the janky autosave functionality. These critiques are justified. You'll undoubtedly lose (cumulative) hours of progress since any time you trigger an alert (which is often) the game doesn't autosave unless you exfiltrate, leave the area, or kill literally every opponent in the vicinity.

I'm not seeing as many complaints about the maps, which are admittedly beautifully rendered, but they need be said as well. Objective markers are occasionally unclear, locking onto objective areas on the map seems inconsistent, and there are collision bugs semi-frequently. I had to reload ~3 saves since my character got stuck in a cliff or in a pile of crates. Fall damage killed me many times, and mantling from water to surface is very unreliable. In the frigid waters of Siberia this can result in very unfair deaths, as the game has no way to designate where you can safely clamber out. You guess wrong, you die.

Lack of communication with the player is one of the game's biggest faults, and this is especially apparent when purchasing new weapons. There's no way to preview what attachments or modifications a weapon can undergo, so you'll have to spend money to buy it first. I definitely wasted ~$800,000 on rifles that I didn't know could not be outfitted with my favorite ammunition, bipeds, or scopes.

As an added side note, the enemy's accuracy, even on standard difficulty, definitely breaks immersion. On maps with fewer options for vantage points, this obsoletes any of the game's louder sniper rifles. You'll get spotted after a single shot, and torn apart by enemy automatic rifles even though they're 200+ meters away.

All in all, as a sniper simulator the game excels, and it looks good while doing it. Stray from the formula and you'll likely encounter some resistance. It looks more polished than it actually is, but that doesn't mean it doesn't flow nicely from one encounter to the next. Expect some frustrating moments, but if you're on the fence about buying a cool sniper game that'll occupy your time for 15+ hours, go for it if it's on discount.

Fucking embarassing. 

And when you change the video options, it changes the size of the window somehow in the background? 

This is not acceptable in 2019 when the game entered early access in 2014.

Combine that with terrible tutorials and tips and you have a HORRIBLE experience for new players.

I have played a lot of these passion project games with tight communities, and this one is the epitome of the dev getting lost in stupid late game details, without investing time on BASIC SHIT like making the main menu work and writing a campaign / tutorial for new players.

No wonder this game is lying in obscurity despite it's high review rating.

Don't support lazy devs that leave their games in EA without fixing obvious and basic issues.

review_text:
This game was a disappointment for me. 
Sure the graphics and music are awesome and tailored to the atmosphere of the story you're watching. Because it's not exactly a game, even if it has some elements of gameplay in it. It's indeed more like a story, as you go in the memories of a dying man.
The deeper I went in the game, the more unease I felt about the story, and there wasn't a satisfactory resolution at the end.
What's more, remember how I said it isn't a game but a narrative ? Well, there is still some gameplay, which makes it tedious and boring, as you get to move around to find random stuff to unlock the following "chapter" of the memories, not to mention the little puzzles scattered here and there (why the hell are they present anyway ?) who break completely the flow of the narrative.

Well, in a nutshell :
+ The music, visuals and global atmosphere are top notch
+/- The scientists humor, which may be here to lighten the atmosphere. There were a couple good jokes, but once again, it's not suited to the story
- The gameplay is not suited to this kind of game
- The story itself, and especially its ending (no spoil here)

And just for the record, I played Rakuen, which I felt was an amazing ride of emotions, and came here as some people made the parralel with this game, so I was perfectly aware of what kind of game I was to find. Hence the disappointment.

One of the best stealth experiences that initially reminded me of the Commandos games with the enemy view-cones, movement patterns, reaction and alert systems, but this game stands on its own. I'm a trial-and-error player and I found the gameplay is addictive. I spent a lot of time (over 2 hours per level) solving tactical puzzles and not once was I frustrated or felt like giving up because the combinations in which to approach solutions with the characters is up to the player's imagination.

I'm not the type of gamer who generally finishes all his games, but this game got me hooked right till the very end and I highly recommend Shadow Tactics even if you are new to this genre.

p.s. That kuma is amazing!

I'm eagerly waiting for the Mimimi's next game "Shadow Gambit" - The demo was amazing!
