review_text:
TRASH GAME - Read why here.
I'm going to request a refund for this, but I'll probably not get one because I'm over the 2 hour limit. This game had me excited - then concerned - then frustrated - and now, apathy. I've gone through all the stages. Keep in mind, I went directly from Arizona Sunshine 2 to this, so there are some parallels - and some VERY big differences. I'll walk you through this below.

Excited: I've got a i9 9900ks with a 4090 Trinity OC running Steam VR with my Quest 3. This game looks beautiful, I'm hot off Arizona Sunshine 2, having a blast. I jump into this game and it's a little different right off the bat, but I'm enjoying FPS VR titles, so I think nothing of it. At this point, the game is a solid A+.

Concerned: I go to the central hub ("The Line") and get into my first mission. As I'm starting, some random joins. Knowing it's my first, I had gone with Survivor difficulty, and thought I was going with 4 AI. My first map experience was some random dude trash talking me through the whole map, getting frustrated with me that I was still learning and trying to play (on the easiest difficulty, with 2 other AI to round out our 4 person team), and I was REALLY irritated that this was a 4 player REQUIRED game. This was my first huge red flag and I should have immediately stopped there, but knowing I could play through the game with AI, I decided to just push through it. Upon mission completion, I got my harvest ("money") and unlocked a new gun, basically a desert eagle. Neat! Back at the hub, I went and noticed there were other guns available - but I didn't know how to get them. I would soon realize I only unlock guns through completing mission levels, and mods (things to make the guns better) are only unlocked by a "gacha" system. Furthermore, the tier of these mods is locked behind difficulty levels. IE, if I chose to play on survivor difficulty for the entirety of the game, I would only get low-tier mods. This reminds me of the concept, "I need a job to get the experience, but I need experience to get the job". Still, the first level was a learning curve for me (despite my FPS VR familiarity) but it wasn't terrible and I knew with time it'd be a cakewalk. Cool. Red flags observed, but let's carry on.

Frustrated: I go through a few different levels of the game with increasing number of snowies ("zombies") as I continue to carry on with AI. I have learned to QUICKLY press the "start mission" button in order to avoid randoms joining my game and ruining my experience. (Online mode appears to be REQUIRED, I cannot turn it off, this is a point of annoyance for me.) I work my way through enough levels to unlock a few guns, and eventually I end up at some kind of "midpoint" campaign level where I have to fight a boss. First time, he wrecks me - and I realize this is just one long level, with no checkpoints (at checkpoints you buy health and such) but the arena is pretty big, so just bad luck, I'll try again. The second time I do the map I actually kill the boss - three times. Yes, in what is a gigantic annoying PITA twist of events the Devs picked the "Kill boss 3 times" mechanic as a "midpoint". I was pretty disappointed, especially after my hands were cramping from such a long fight. (Your mileage may vary.) Also at this point, it feels like the AI are becoming less and less effective. They don't kill as much as they (seemed) to before and I feel like I'm doing more and more of the work. I don't mind that, but when my hands start to cramp up because I'm white knuckling the controllers, it turns from a stressful experience into a frustrating one. Anyway, that wasn't really the straw that broke the camels back - I had beaten that boss fight and moved on to the next map. I play the next map, they say "There aren't as many snowies in this area" and I think great, a breather. Well, let me tell you, they fking lied. The most snowies I've seen yet were on that map, and we get all the way to the end (a kinda cool looking movie theater) and the culmination fight begins. First off, the reload box was behind an object - you had to be at a specific point in the arena in order to hit it. Second, an eater spawned, no issue. A juggernaut spawned, took him down. Then an eater, juggernaut, gunner, AND crusher (the boss type I JUST KILLED) all spawn, as well as a million snowies, on survivor difficulty, with me and three AI. Two of the AI go down, I'm clearing the room, it's JUST the crusher left, he somehow gets me despite being half the arena away from him, and I watch as he runs over to the remaining AI and the AI just STANDS THERE and lets him kill him. Oh yeah! Did I mention that if you get hit by the boss, EVEN ONCE, you're done? On survivor difficulty, the easiest difficulty in the game? What a literal joke.

Apathy: So I've gone through all my stages of frustration. I'll put in for a refund request which will probably get denied because this kind of game commits the largest cardinal sin: It sucks you in with a few hours of easy gameplay so you CANT refund it, then it ramps up the difficulty. I don't want to play with other players. I RESENT this Dev for making me have to do that. I RESENT the Dev for half-assing the AI. I RESENT being hoodwinked. I have nothing but resentment and apathy left.

Do not buy this game. Let it freeze to death and teach the Devs a lesson. Nobody playing a game on EZMODE like this, should have this kind of experience. Could have been great, but this is just trash. Shame on predatory Devs.

review_text:
Witchfire Webgrave Update

The game is now in a great place, even from what the devs are saying (for Q1 2026 1.0 and how the game now is almost mostly about more content) and Steam/Reddit agrees the game feels excellent to play and very polished. I said it before, but if you miss Destiny being Destiny - here's a witch-themed Destiny that replicates that signature of Destiny-Bungie-Halo like gun and movement feel. It's excellent, also because it's not just trying to be Slavic-Witcher-like Destiny, but also just having strong progression and game loop. It's just fun, the enemies are fun, the guns and upgrades are fun. Not to sound like a broken record, but it's all just fun. There's a nice mix of moods too, from more Slavic-Nordic elements to some Inquisition-style Spanish influence and a lot of western vibes straight from Hunt: Showdown.

There are not many games I would recommend in early access (like No Rest for The Wicked) because they feel too amazing to play (and have almost no bugs), but this is one of them. Early 2026 is not far off, but if you get in now - you have almost the final version. After 60h (20h of this new update), I'm level 81, so more-or-less late-mid/early-late game.

The roguelite.
The random run roguelite element is well integrated into the game design, allowing you to further customise your build per run. As with many great roguelites (like Hades), you can upgrade your character and gain access to more control over the random skills by choosing tier prefs (a bit like gods' trinkets in Hades for getting more types of certain boons). You can pick between beefing up your guns (like dash reload or bullet refunds on crits, etc.), your magic, or your life. It makes for a fun random skill system that can make each run different even when using the same core gear.

The extraction.
I feel that this is where many people hesitate, as extraction shooters are usually a bit more hardcore. While Witchfire is an extraction shooter, it is also a single-player game. Most extraction shooters feel more intense as you know other players are out there and may wait for you at the extraction. With Witchfire, that's not the case. The game has systems to keep tension high (like extraction portals guarded by enemies or calamities that work as a timer for you to not grind one map too long) - it's never as stressful as in a multiplayer game and works great within the lore of the world for you to get in, fight the evil witch's minions, and make your way out.

Some tips if you start:
- Level up your guns, they can have game-changing mechanics, so even if you don't love the gun on level 1 - by level 3/3 it may be amazing and super fun to use.
- Mix status elementals, the game allows you to mix more elementals than just obvious ones like Fire and Ice. All elementals mix - so a decay and lightning can produce more lightning, or a fire with lightning can produce a more rapid burn. Don't be afraid to mix - you don't need to (you can) just focus on one elemental.
- Experiment with your gear - one ring or a totem can change the way you play. One of my favorite rings is one that freezes enemies when they melee you and you dash - makes (all enemies, but especially) elites much easier as all enemies in this game have a melee attack and it can be a pressure off if you can freeze a stronger enemy to strike back or just reposition. They melee - you dash - they freeze - you crit-hit. It's poetry. Or how about electric shocks every time you dash after hitting an enemy?

With the Webgrave update - Witchfire is one of the best FPS games on the market, it's fun - has very satisfying combat and gunplay and just works. Oh yeah - it's also great on Steam Deck - had to add that hahah.

review_text:
I've wanted to play this game for a long time after having discovered the world of otome and hearing people saying so many good stuff about this game. Man, Otomate NEVER DISAPPOINTS. This one proves it once more. 

Hakuoki: Kyoto Winds is the first part of the story, based on the history of the Shinsengumi in the 1800s. There are 12 routes in total, with one big common route and two route chapters. The only thing that I can complain about is the repetitiveness of going through the main route a million times to get those small changes throughout the chapters and that final route chapter for each character. Also the main character Chizuru is really naive, makes stupid decisions, brings people in danger, can't defend herself at all and never listens to what they're saying to her. She drove me mad most of the time, but I guess that's mostly because of her sheltered life and age. Part of her charm I guess? Other than that, this game is def one of the best in its genre! 

This part really sets you up for the next part called 'Edo Blossoms'. So make sure to play Kyoto Winds FIRST, before going into Edo Blossoms. Voice acting was phenomenal (as always), character development was on point (as always, there is just no character that you can possibly hate) and it really tells the story of the Shinsengumi, which is such a treat to me. (more or less with some fantasy elements included etc) I only knew bits and pieces of their history thanks to the movie 'The Last Samurai', but I'm very glad I got to play this game and find out more about this wonderful (tragic) piece of history of Japan's last samurai. So it's not only a great game, but also very educational, as it gives you some free history lessons.

I haven't finished the second part yet, but be warned this is one big, heartwrenching, sad, depressing story. Bittersweet is maybe a better word for it. Just like the real history of the Shinsengumi. 

Otomate and Idea Factory really deserve all the love in the world for their quality games. There's just no developer who's better than them imo. Especially when it comes to the Otome genre. They are at the top of their game. They know how to make quality games with top voice acting, great storylines, great characters + development, great art,...  and I'm so glad more and more people find their way to the otome genre. It does deserve all the love it gets and I'm hoping more games will be localised in the future. It's not just 'a romance visual novel/dating simulation for girls'. It has become so much more than that. It's even an insult now to be called that! It's not 'just for girls' anymore, but for everyone who likes a game with a good storyline, great art and great voice acting. 

Hakuoki is hands down one of my favourite otome games so far (and I haven't even finished it yet). And I can say it's def not a 'fluffy romance VN'. This is a game about war, the consequences of war, principles, faith and fighting for what is right. That mixed with romance and friendship makes this game one of its best. A DEFINITE RECOMMEND!!

review_text:
To the Moon is a game about two scientists who can create false memories, and use this to fulfil the dying wish of those on their deathbeds. In order to understand why their client, John, wishes to go to the moon, they must work backwards from his memories, which leads to the story unfolding as they delve deeper into his past. This is certainly an interesting premise, and a unique way of telling a story about the regrets one might have at the end of their life. 

The actual gameplay part of this game is extremely minimal, with the majority being pointing and clicking or solving simple puzzles. 
The rudimentary tile flipping puzzles needed for each memento was particularly egregious, as they felt extremely out of place with the story and seemed to only serve to waste time. In fact I grew to dread the repetitive nature of collecting 5 memory orbs and solving the tiles as I knew it was coming. My least favourite part about this game ended up being the gameplay, which is disappointing to say the least. 

The artwork is good, with detailed sprites that effectively convey the complex emotions the game seeks to display, but the rudimentary tools used to create the game unfortunately make it feel dated, such as in the control scheme, which is clunky to say the least. There is also no option to change settings such as controls or resolution. While I understand that these constraints are the result of the game engine, they must nevertheless be pointed out. 

The ultimate question though is: why was this story told through the medium of video games? What choices do the player ultimately have? What separates one player’s experience from another’s? I could have watched a playthrough of this game instead of playing it myself and got the exact same experience. 

While I acknowledge and appreciate the game’s ambition, it's frustrating seeing it fall short of excellence in just about every category. While the story is good, it is not good enough to justify suffering through it’s lackluster gameplay, and for that reason I have chosen not to recommend this game.

review_text:
Oof, Lost Ruins is a Game alright.
But in my opinion not a good one.
This Game is kind of a Metroidvania Light with (badly implemented) Souls and "Survival" Elements and it just isn't fun, actually it is a frustrating mess.
I can forgive that a little bit because after seeing the Credits, I think only 2 people really worked on it (disregarding the Localization Teams here) but if a Game is bad, it's bad.

So the first thing you will notice is the extremely annoying sound the "Character Talk Box" makes. This is the first impression. Then you will notice good Pixel Art. It is just that, good, not the best ever but it kinda has it's own chunky style.

The next thing I personally noticed was extremely annoying. I played with a Gamepad, but when I switched to my Keyboard (for opening the Steam Overlay or for going to Desktop) the displayed controls in Game would switch constantly (!) between Gamepad and Keyboard and the only solution is to restart the Game and also: NEVER touch your Keyboard while playing.
Second thing I disliked (I at first thought the Game was buggy) was when an Achievement Notification would pop up but basically it only tells you, that you have fulfilled one step to get the full Achievement. Found it kind of annoying and also useless.

The Music was also kind of meh. More bad than good. More annoying than hooking me. (You see where this is going? There is so much ANNOYING stuff here and that's not all, the worst things I will tell you about next.)

I think this Game does not know what it wants to be, this is a perfect example of an identity crisis. 

- The Game has Souls Elements with slow and "deliberate" combat but it just feels clunky as hell. The Controls don't feel good. Then there are the enemies. Oh boy is this one frustrating Game. Normal enemies can be a pain to kill. I played most of the Game with a Zweihänder (yes, you write it like that) and the enemies are just unfair. The Zweihänder is VERY slow and in the time you attack, most enemies still have longer reach than you and can SPAM their attacks like CRAZY without ever stopping. Of course you are free to use other Weapons/Ranged Weapons/Spells, but everything feels kind of bad here.
Then there are the bosses which are laughably easy. Every Boss has 2-3 Phases (Normal Phase, Big B**b Phase and sometimes a "funny" Phase were you can just kill them easily) and most of them have only 3-4 Attack Patterns which are extremely easy to counter. Also they take a ton of Damage and are down real quick.

- Then there is the Metroidvania Element but the Game fails here as well. There is no real progression (apart from getting a LITTLE more health or getting new Items for new "Builds") here. No Double Jumps, no Dashes, no nothing. The Level Design is also extremely BORING and lazy. There are almost NO secrets to find and no branching paths and backtracking is also rarely if not ever needed. Basically you start on the left side, then go right aaaaall the way, then go up after a boss, go left aaaall the way, go up, go right and so on. This is the basic design here with VERY few variations (sometimes you go down also...).
Platforming when it happens: Also bad. Either you are in a very small space and bump your head or you are outside and jump on a few platforms, it's not really needed here but also not very well implemented.

I read some of the positive and some of the negative reviews on here and I actually agree with most of the negative reviews. 
Another thing: Savepoints and Checkpoints don't restore your health/mana, you have to consume items for that or just play like I did with a ton of regen-Gear.

Storywise it's stupid. So is the dialogue. Just wow, what is that even? Can't and don't want to describe this.
(And what's with all the big b**bs on the bosses?)

Well, my first playthrough took 5.9 hours, only got 12/40 Achievements. In good Games/Metroidvanias/Soulslikes I would want to jump back in to get more Achievements and to see a different ending. Not here. I am just glad it is over. Especially because for some Achievements you have to torture yourself through the whole Game again, grind/farm a lot and/or play different Game Modes.
I literally have 0 interest in that.

So yeah, if you are a REALLY REALLY big fan of Metroidvanias/Souls-Adjacent Games and you need to play everything, MAYBE you will get a kick out of this, for everyone else who just wants a good Game: Stay Away!

 Countrary to the usual metroidvania, you don't scale in power into stupid levels (like Symphony/Ritual of the Night) and every enemy is still a threat from begining to end; also, your character stands still with each attack and you can't do the usual trick where you jump and attack so you can still move (attacking locks you in place) so you have to be careful and measure your distance and hits... kinda like a souls game.

 Give it a try, it's quite worth it.

review_text:
Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon is a fantastic blast from the past, paying homage to 80s action movies and video games with its retro-futuristic setting, over-the-top action, and cheesy one-liners. The game is a standalone expansion to Far Cry 3, offering a shorter but more focused and absurd experience that doesn't take itself too seriously.

The gameplay is fast-paced and satisfying, with a variety of weapons and abilities to choose from that make you feel like a badass cyber-soldier. The neon-soaked visuals and synthwave soundtrack add to the overall nostalgic feel of the game, transporting players back to a time when action movies were king. Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon is a must-play for fans of the 80s and anyone looking for a fun and unique shooter experience.

However, it is a shame that Ubisoft forces players to use their clunky game launcher to access a game they purchased on Steam. This unnecessary step adds an extra layer of inconvenience and frustration to an otherwise enjoyable experience. It would be much better if players could simply launch the game through Steam, like most other games, without having to deal with Ubisoft's cumbersome launcher. Hopefully, Ubisoft will reconsider this decision in the future and make the player experience more seamless and user-friendly.

review_text:
First thing’s first: To The Moon is not a game. I hesitate to call it a “story,” and it certainly isn’t a work of art. Reading the “Overwhelmingly Positive” reviews makes me feel like I’m out of the loop on some elaborate prank to make me feel insane.

Most obvious from the store page; the graphics. They’re RPG maker graphics. Nothing special, but aside from some… questionably drawn scenes, it’s basic pixel art. That being said, the utilization of said pixel art is dull. Everything is bland with drab colors and samey design, which is a huge problem because of…

…the “gameplay,” if you can call it that. Drag your playable character around with awkward, clunky movement controls and click on every random object in a dull room until you find the one insignificant thing the developer decided you HAVE to interact with to progress. While a handful are signposted okay with visual cues that guide you toward them, the vast majority are just senselessly chosen and placed to pad out the already painfully slow pacing of the “game.” In addition to this, there are randomly scattered puzzles, many completely unrelated to the plot and with poorly designed arbitrary solutions (For example, there's a random Animorphs trivia question that doesn't even have the correct answer).

But, let’s be real, none of that matters, right? To The Moon is about the AMAZING story that sets a NEW STANDARD for what games should be, right? Wrong. Wrong in a million ways. There is hardly a story here to tell, despite what the reviews will tell you. The first three quarters of the game is a mindless slog with zero substance and the least likable or interesting characters you will have ever seen. You have the two “witty” scientists who serve only to undercut any even slightly serious tones the game comes close to building. The main character (the old man in the bed, not the playable characters) has zero discernible personality. The main character’s wife, aka the OTHER main character is a caricature of someone with autism; she’s totally incapable of expressing herself in any way (unless the plot calls for it and she all of a sudden does a complete 180), and her whole personality is just being a rude smartass because she has autism; a complete spit in the face to anyone who actually has ASD.

The game is a disjointed collection of the main character’s memories, as he has asked the player to enter his mind and implant fake memories of being an astronaut because he wants to go to the moon. About three hours in, the developer must have realized he’s done absolutely nothing productive with the story, because out of nowhere the final quarter of the game turns sharply into an ending almost completely disconnected from everything else. The last hour of the game is another, faster-paced series of random events, but this time with poorly written and repetitive emotional music playing over it. The game is so desperate to claw an emotional response out of its audience that it’s honestly laughable, and does not earn a single one of its attempted emotional moments, though I assume the general melancholic tone of much of the game is what drives people into thinking it’s deep when it’s really not doing or saying anything at all. 

Overall, the game is just a mess, and has virtually zero redeeming qualities. I cannot recommend it for anyone to be honest, and especially today there are dozens to hundreds of well-written, beautifully crafted masterpieces that respect your time, money, and brain much more than this garbage ever could.

Update: it appears i do not need to wait for all the dlc to release as this game is pretty dead due to mismanagement(what a shocker for sao games right?)

TL;DR: a game that once had potential, mismanaged and starved to death, do not buy as you will not find matches. buy one of the others such as Fatal Bullet or Hollow Realization

This game had alot of potential aside from the jank combat system and rather stiff movements, it was at release what we wanted for a while though the roguelite element probably not.

Instead of releasing more content they released serial codes thinking that's what players wanted and implemented a system that requires a certain amount of players to start a match instead of just filling with bots(the bots are bad.. you'd be better off just playing solo if it let you unironically, another shocker).

Original review beyond this point.

Edit: I will be redoing this review once all the dlc drops to judge the final product, as it stands currently fatal bullet is still better but my statement below still stands, this is "probably" the best one if they handle it properly
TL:DR: If a fan of grinding, buy now
If grinding can become tedious for you, wait for sale or skip, this game is 100% grind

This is probably the best sao game we got so far, but it is not without its flaws or issues as a long term sao game player you may already know most of them as the formula is similar.

I'll begin with the good points
-The battle pass is free and gives you tickets to buy outfits in the shop instead of spending more money(I am unsure if ones in the future will be paid, considering sao game track record, I wouldn't put it past them especially considering how dimps handled the fatal bullet dlc)
-The gameplay loop isn't to repetitive or tiring to do, the structure allows it to be entertaining similarly to base pso2 or psu
-Each character plays in a different way be it a minor alteration or larger alteration, if your bored of one you can swap to another and have a mostly different experience
-(potentially good/grey area)The gear is ran off of an affix system, for gear hunters this allows you to hunt for the best gear possible, these affixes will impact your gameplay noticeably or minorly depending on affix build

Neutral: this game is like a roguelite from mission to mission in multiplayer, only your gear carries over

With the good out of the way, there isn't very many actual bad points I can personally make note of so most will seem minor
-The story makes absolutely no sense, if you are familiar with sao you are probably used to this as it is a stable basically(I personally don't mind this considering it is a multiplayer pve game, I would just rather the story make sense or be enjoyable considering it's somewhat forced on you)
-The gear drop rate for legendary items is quite low, for gear hunters like myself finding the best affix combo can be annoying especially with low drop rates and when something does drop it has a potential to have entirely useless affixes(similar to how anthem was at launch, for those not familiar with it an example would be a light element weapon dropping with water damage increase or such)
-This game has a habit of dropping inputs if you use a controller so you may often find yourself just standing there for a moment when you try to combo or use abilities

Overall, despite the issues I would recommend to give it a try depending if you need a game to waste time on, if you have played phantasy star(not new genesis) or previous sao games, you will likely enjoy the gameplay loop provided. There is also a hidden game in the artbook/soundtrack called "Kirito The Hero"

review_text:
To describe this game in one word, frustrating. It tries to do a lot of things, and for some it may accomplish them well, but for me personally it's just too annoying and overly punishing to be enjoyable. Its not a rogue-lite, its not a souls-like, its not a doom clone, and its not tarkov, but it tries its hardest to be all of these and more. Player guns feel like anemic nerf guns, while enemies are given near-hit-scan, tracking projectiles and melee aoes the size of the average family sedan. Maps are too small to justify having minimally-randomized tarkov style raids. Dying and losing everything feels awful when loot is already so underwhelming, the only thing that drives me to look for it is the potential of working towards a new weapon that might not feel like trash strapped together in the vague shape of a gun. Traps are needlessly frustrating. Stamina is needlessly frustrating. "Combat Focus" is obtuse and needlessly frustrating. Leveling up is a chore and player stats start off so laughably low, it makes me wonder why the enigmatic Witch hasn't conquered all of humanity yet. 

I come back to this game with each patch, hoping it has found its place, and shines like I want it to, but its just too unfun, convoluted, and annoying to deserve its price tag or its spot on my hard drive. Looking forward to seeing if the next update makes things any better.

review_text:
Rise to Ruins is a fun mix of tower defence, god game, and village/colony sim. The basic premise is you are a God overseeing your villagers and helping them survive against the ever encroaching threat of the corruption. 

The corruption is the main antagonist, it slowly consumes everything that your influence doesn't reach and sends waves of monsters to destroy your villagers every night. It can't be beaten, it can only be contained and the more constrained it feels, the harder it fights back. (well it can be beaten, but it requires extensive knowledge of the game or cheese that defeats the whole point of playing on anything but peaceful mode)

The main gameplay loop is fun and will eat up more of your time than you expect. You build your village, establish industries to support it and develop defences to protect it. The learning curve can seem steep at times and you will most likely fail many times over before you've gotten a solid grasp on the mechanics, but it is a fun and rewarding experience. 

There is a roguelite progression system that helps with the learning curve and keeps things from getting stale to quickly. You are rewarded xp after every session, success or failure. You can use this xp to open perk chests that give you ever increasing bonuses to almost every aspect of the game. Sometimes you may open one and think "Cool down reduction on a spell I don't use, meh". Other times you will get something that makes you rethink your entire approach in order to make use of it. You also aren't locked to your first region, you can send migrants and supplies to neighbouring regions which you can use to establish a new village and there is enough variety in the different maps to keep it from feeling "samey". Plus, you can always return to an older region/village at anytime without losing progress anywhere else (which can allow for some interesting interaction between your settlements)

The difficulty is fully configurable and you can alter pretty much any part of the game's difficulty/mechanics to suit your tastes or create unique challenges (Extreme length winters present more challenges than you would think).

The biggest complaint I have is that there isn't a ton of depth or variety, once you've found a strategy that works you won't find yourself forced to change your approach very much, and something that you've safely ignored will most likely stay ignored unless you want to challenge yourself/mix things up.

review_text:
As being one of the only vr games designed around the left 4 dead gameplay style, it an ok game. But trust me, when the next l4d style vr game comes out this game will probably come up very short.

I like the weapons and attachment system, but the fact that the bulk of good attachments like the increased mag is locked behind the hardest difficulties and if you can't or don't like playing with random people its going to be a sh!tshow just to acquire them, that's also not taking into account that you'll get repeat attachments that offer nothing more then more harvest. The guns are fun, but really really unwieldy and a complete pain to try and aim with even when you get the improved sights. I'll also point out the elephant in the room, no melee. Not just weapons, but even a swat them with the gun to knock them back to give you breathing room. With how on top the zombies get, this would be really helpful to be able to do.

The bots are about as competent as they ever are in 4 player co-op, but the devs decided to do one thing to make them laughably crap. They all spawn it with either: starter pistol and mac10 smg, desert eagle (the worst default in my opinion), the pump shotgun (second worst bot loadout), or the ak spoof. They have all these guns in the game and they can't give the bots a more colorful and stronger loadout option? Or at least let the player switch out the loadouts with the guns in the locked room or the ones we have many duplicates of?

The "special" zombies are dups of the same overall idea "What if they are bullet sponges that can instant freeze players?" You got 3 of those. one with a gun, one with armor, one with speed... they spawn way too much, sometimes two at a time all the while the players have the common zombies to deal with. Furthermore the game does lack the concept of "chill" giving the players a moment to breathe with the rather repetative "path blocked, kill the horde, shoot tentacles, move to the next chuck of map and repeat"

Admittedly the world feels kinda like it was built around the fact that when incap, you are frozen. But this game's incap requires the use of the health syringes to revive, which is really a mixed bag, especially with a strict 2 storage spaces in your gloves.

So. I find the game really fun but no better then a 6/10 experience. So why give the game a recommendation? just a general courtesy as I did have fun upon first playing and still find it worthwhile to hop into on a boring day and I want a more interesting zombie game then a wave shooter as seen in pavlov or contractors. But like I said, when a dev releases a rival 4 player coop zombie game to vr, After the Fall will definitely come up short.

Unfortunately, I recently had a falling out with my girlfriend because my motorcycle tire blew out and I couldn’t give her time. She got upset and asked, “Who’s more important, me or the new Sword Art Online game?” She doesn’t understand how long I’ve been waiting for this moment, counting every second! Just help me get that 69 award, and all will be good.

Will we really get to live through the first part of the anime series? I seriously hope so. I’m feeling so many things right now, and I don’t even know what to say, but I will say this: I’m beyond excited!

Fighting with a full team is such an adrenaline rush for me. This is my absolute favorite game—Sword Art Online: Fractured Dream. If you think I’m just another casual fan of the game, world, or anime, go take a look at my profile. I’m completely hooked.

I’m really looking forward to playing this with my girlfriend and friends. At last, I can experience the world in a more immersive way, something I haven’t found in VR yet. I’m really hoping this game develops into VR because that’s my ultimate dream—to experience Sword Art Online for real.

My favorite installment so far has been Sword Art Online: Hollow Realization Deluxe Edition. I’ve spent 2000 hours in that game and never got bored. I really hope Fractured Dream offers the same level of depth, missions, expansive world, and gameplay mechanics. More than anything, I want to see Asuna take center stage in this game. I firmly believe Asuna should be the leading character, not just the one always shouting, "Kirito-kun!"

There will definitely be an update to this review soon, I promise.

I can’t wait to see Asuna in this game. Will she be wearing pink underwear on the bed? I guess we’ll have to wait and find out!

First review update: I’ve had the chance to try the beta, and it’s truly mind-blowing. The combat feels like stepping into another dimension, almost like the anime itself. I’m really impressed by the collaboration happening in the Sword Art Online community. This is just my initial take, so expect more updates in the coming days.

That said, I am a little concerned that the game could lose steam quickly. I hope the community stays active because, as it is now, Fractured Dream relies heavily on online and co-op play. Overall, the game is fantastic. The characters and abilities are incredible in every sense (and the bosses aren’t pushovers, which is a relief). review_text:
Rooftops and Alleys is an amazing game! Easy to learn but hard to master. There are 6 different unique maps (5 when this review was written but 6 when 1.0 releases) with a variety of different obstacles that you can do tricks on. The game teaches you some moves but you also get to experiment learning new moves and combos. Time trials help keep you engaged during while you play and give you a sense of accomplishment when you finally get the gold medal. Time trials also make you want to come back to beat your highscore again and again. Additionally, there are multiplayer features and gamemodes. The current gamemodes are tag and trick battle, they offer unique and fun experiences which are fun with friends or others online (more negatives mentioned later). The main multiplayer feature is a leaderboard on time trials, this keeps you playing just to beat one of your friends so you can prove that your better.

BUT, every game has its flaws. Although each map offers a different experience, after you explore each one, you might find it boring revisiting the old ones (of course it depends what type of person you are). Furthermore, the maps are fairly small, I belive that instead of focusing about size, the maps are focused on specific areas where players can freerun and combine lots of trick together. I personally like fully exploring all the maps and find it fun finding the small details scattered around the map. There is one problem with the multiplayer gamemode, if you don't have friends willing to play the game/buy the game, then it can be hard to get into a multiplayer game because there aren't many other solo people that also want to play multiplayer.

In conclusion, if you are looking for a game with the most realism, just wait for STORROR Parkour Pro to release (in about 6-12 months from when this review is written). Rooftops and Alleys is a great game where you can explore around unique maps doing different tricks. It keeps you coming back to beat time trial and learn combos. The game has realistic aspects but also less realistic things to make the game more fun. KEEP IN MIND, this game is made by a SOLO DEVELOPER, they are doing their best developing the game.

I forgot to mention this earlier, but the game has an AMAZING music soundtrack (the developer was previously a dj). The music gives the game a very unique vibe and overall enhances the experience.

review_text:
Although this game is not a bad game, not at all, I am stunned how it reached such a positive overall rating. Let's start with the criticism:

[olist]
    [*]The story is okay, but it is childish. There are a couple of thing which are not fitting into the carefully built-up atmosphere, totally ruining the experience. Also it has close resemblance to [b][i]Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind[/i][/b] (2004)
    [*]The gameplay is dull. You are doing the same things again and again. And again and again. Walking, looking for objects. Walking, looking for objects. The puzzles are rather an annoyance than any kind of challenge.
    [*]The dialogues are childish. Very childish. Extremely childish.
    [*]The music is okay, but the synthesized musical instruments started to hurt my ears quite soon. The arrangement is not for an orchestra so not using accoustic instruments is just cheap.
    [*]The graphics. Anybody saying they were beautiful is lying. It is not even average. The colours are dull. Take any VGA, point-and-click adventure from 1990s (Sierra, LucasArts) and compare it to this, and you will see what I mean. Don't believe the reviews.
    [*]The game engine. There are no options. You cannot change the volume. You cannot change the resolution, you have to use 640×480 (I wonder how future-proof this is). You can make the game running in a window but the game will not remember this setting the next time you start it. The controls are bad. Sometimes an object-associated action is triggered even when clicking somewhere completely elsewhere.
[/olist]

Okay, I don't want to be so harsh. These are not critical issues. The game is enjoyable, but I don't think it is an outstanding piece of art. Just watch [b][i]Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind[/i][/b] and you get a better experience.

review_text:
Rise to Ruins is a cross between a city builder and tower defense game. You build a city during the day, and at night enemies attack you. You have to build towers and walls to kill the enemies before they enter your base and start wreaking havok.

In the campaign, the world map is divided into regions. You pick one region as your starting region, and build your first city there. To conquer that region, you need to survive there a year. Then you can send people and resources to other regions to begin again there. The catch: The game stage progresses for all regions at the same rate, so when you start that next region, you will almost immediately be assaulted by top-level troops. If you haven't sent enough people and supplies to get defenses built by the end of the day, you're screwed. But, you are limited on how much you can send to a region in one day, so the longer you take to send things, the more difficult the game gets. You can unlock bonuses to help you combat the difficulty, but the slow rate that the game runs at essentially guarantees that you would have to spend the next 30 years playing to win the game. Not really my idea of fun.

Besides this, my other biggest complaint is the garbage collection. As your people work, they generate garbage which has to be collected and stored or burned. This is a pain in the rear. Who in the world thought it was a good idea to introduce garbage collection (including Wall-E bots) in a medieval fantasy city builder? No thanks. 

Before the garbage collection mechanics were added, I would have given this game a thumbs-up for single-scenario play, just to see how long you could survive, ignoring the campaign altogether. Now, I have to give it a thumbs down overall.

But I must say, once you understand you are not Doom guy or some bad ass Call of Duty guy, you learn to accept, appreciate and get good on how to fight and avoid fights. Play this game more like a classic Resident Evil game and you will enjoy it. I reccomend it to those who like classic Resident Evil Games and the classic Alone in the Dark.

A generally competent game that just makes some really out there decisions in the later half of the game.

Everything Kiryu and Saejima touch is golden generally no complaints an actually good story out of both of them. And then Haruka's part of the story starts. My problem isn't actually Haruka herself but her manager Park who is written to be well...she takes Haruka away from the orphanage and literally threatens to close it down if Haruka doesn't behave the way Park wants her to. Is this absolutely confusing and will never be brought up again? Yes. Does it make Park completely irredeemable in my eyes? Yes. Does the game continue to try and paint this woman as a sympathetic character who wants any good for this child? You get it, she's awful and I feel like she would have been more engaging a character if she were either just more cruel or never a straight up toxic POS when she's introduced to us. Akiyama returns and continues to be lightning, idk why they skimped on giving us more of Hana but I can't make Sega change a 12 year old game to give me more of beautiful foodie lady who is weirdly their best written female character to this point if we're going by release order. Gameplay wise everyone in the cast to this point is great, even Saejima isn't miserable to play this time, idk what's different he just feels different. Kiryu and Akiyama are the same as in 4 and that's fine because they are great, Haruka has a sadly over done dancing game where you will find yourself dreading hearing those same songs by the end of your time with her. Could have had more songs but maybe they should have just cut her stuff a bit shorter so that we spend less time on her. However she is the best character to town explore because no one attacks her at random so she's safe to just look around and have a good time soaking in the vibes of whatever local she's in at a given time.

Now sadly there is a fifth character and I did not like him, I seem to be in the minority here but this minority is a vocal one and we all hate Shinada, now a lot of people hate him purely for gameplay reasons, that is one but the other for me is his absolutely vulgar character. He comes off to me as one of those guys so desperate for a whiff of pussy he'll drop plans made with you months ago to try and fail at getting a girls number. So you can imagine my dismay at realising I had to play as this loser for a few hours until the plot decided it was time to wrap up, hell he also has fuck all place in the story but still comes to the final showdown despite everyone telling him to fuck off and proceeds to have a fight that had no build up and made no sense. All in all annoying dude and I didn't like his voice actor.

So yeah other than weird ass writing for a good chunk of the story this game whacks, musics good, you get to dress Haruka as Hatsune Miku in the post game and you get to play Taiko No Tatsugin. Pretty good out of good.

review_text:
Edit: It's now been almost a year since I purchased the game and the devs have still not added the vibration support for controllers that was promised. They are now discussing brand new features never talked about before while still failing to add the existing features that have been promised. When I made a discussion about this topic a few months back I was immediately harassed by some other users that ended up causing moderator intervention and instead of just dealing with the harassers they used the opportunity to lock my thread and downplay the concerns. I do not recommend supporting these devs at this point while this is in early access. I would gladly take a refund. 

Original Review: 

I really don't want to leave a negative review, but might be the only way they start paying attention to a feature that the vast majority of modern games support but this one doesn't, basic controller vibrations. There are none and it feels horrible to play because of it. 

I do appreciate that they've made some posts saying they are aware it's being asked for, but they've also shared posts where they claim people enjoy the game so much they don't notice it's missing. Maybe it's because I've been a PC gamer since the original Half-Life release, had my fair share of consoles, and still game regularly to this day that I find such a comment insane. Maybe it's from someone who rarely plays with a controller, but it's not something anyone with any real experience says. 

Vibrations are additional feedback that you get accustomed to. If I do play with MKB then I change how I play because I no longer have that feedback present to tell me stuff. When I play with a controller I can't make that switch. 

In probably 10 years or more, this is the first game I've played with zero vibration feedback. I've seen it mentioned long enough that I chose not to refund the game. At this point, since they just keep mentioning it but not taking it seriously I regret that choice. I wish I had refunded. 

If you play with a controller and have for any period of time, this game will drive you mad. Do not buy, wait for the full release and see if it ever gets the support they claim they are aware of and working on.

review_text:
[h2]Briefly:[/h2]
There's fun to be had as long as you plan on ignoring the achievements, or if you enjoy achievements that require a punishing level of perfectionism to obtain. For me, that isn't the case.

[h2]More fully:[/h2]
The game [i]itself[/i] is good. It's decently creative and has personality, and the puzzles are challenging but solveable. So far so good.

But, if you're someone who bothers with achievements or otherwise cares about them, it becomes quickly frustrating. So, not so good.

Out of 8 achievements:
 - 1 is for passing the game
 - 1 is for doing something unusual on a specific level
 - The other 6 of are finnicky, nitpicky, perfectionist achievements only earned on passing [b]every[/b] level in a chapter with much more restrictive requirements (for which you get an "OCD flag")

It was this third point that soured the game for me. Because I do care about completing a reasonable percentage of achievements for each game I play (50-75% for most, unless I really like the game, then it's 75-100%). Unfortunately, these 6 achievements take a [i][b]disproportionate[/b][/i] amount of time [i]beyond[/i] simply playing the game decently well and passing it—and they make up 3/4 of the achievements obtainable.

It was after I spent hours in the the first chapter getting OCD flags for the first 10 levels (failing over and over on the 10th) that I started to ask myself why I was spending so much time at something I was coming to hate.

review_text:
[h1] Quantity over quality [/h1]
In hindsight I can see why the PS3 Yakuza games are glossed over. They aren't very good. Yakuza 5 has a ton of content arguably the most content in the series. You can race, drive a Taxi, Hunt in the wild, sing and dance as an idol, swing at the batting cages, and this is all ON TOP of the standard Yakuza fare. However, as a result, all of these things are super simple and get repetitive and boring FAST, and they are REQUIRED to get through the story. Don't even get me started on the story, this series somehow manages to have some of the best and WORST stories in video games. 5 is the lowest of the low, yes the sum of its parts is collectively worse than 4's infamous twist. 4 was dumb, but 5 actually makes me mad. Established characters act weird and have motivations that make no sense considering past games. (Part's 1-3 practically pretend Yakuza 3 and 4 don't exist). Haruka and Kiryu would NEVER leave the orphanage and Haruka wouldn't abandon Kiryu in his time of need. The games plot progressively gets worse as you go on. I know people think Shinada's story is bad, and its dumb, VERY dumb but I liked Uno and Takasugi and liked the mystery upwards until the end where it just devolves into nonsense.  I personally found Haruka and Akiyama's plot to be the worst offenders. I don't mind their gameplay but in general their chapter is just boring uninteresting fluff and a giant pace breaker.  Do you care about idol drama? Do you care about an obvious murder mystery? Do you like obnoxious or outright boring characters? That's Part 3 in a nutshell.
There are no fun or likable characters introduced in their section, in fact the game FORCES you to sympathize with an unlikable character when you have absolutely no reason to. [spoiler] Park, upon first impression and even upwards to her final moments is just pushy snob. But because she acts as """mother figure""" to Haruka, by having us shop together do our hair together etc. we have to feel sorry for her failed career despite her bad treatment to her past and present employees/idols but we should like because she likes Haruka. There is no reason to like this character, and the 2nd half of that chapter is finding justice for that same character that the player most likely does not care for. There's a point in the story where 3 adults let an already kidnapped teenage girl walk off on her own because she "has a plan", 
who then proceeds to obviously end up in more trouble. Either Everyone in this game is an idiot, or something was lost in translation. Probably both. There are a considerable amount of plotholes and inconsistencies in this game. Hey our Rival businesses were actually friends this whole time and we planned this debut in advance despite that making NO SENSE in our current circumstances I burst into laughter during the final twist because it was so ridiculous and it was being played straight. [/spoiler] 
This is the longest game in the series and for absolutely no reason but to be drawn out with exposition, terrible characters, repetitive mini games, and with a plot that feels like it doesn't need to exist.

review_text:
The pros. 
The base defense is fun. People sometimes have strong opinions on how to build the bases but most people agree holding ground against the bugs is a fun time. (Flyers from the movie would be cool)

The final run to the drop ship is exactly what i want from a horde shooter and captures that evac from the movies. 

Most players are willing to try and pick you up. Being a medic is very fun with the tools they get and sharing lives usually means most players want you back up in those game modes.

The body mechanic is amazing in concept (and probably a big part of the frame rate issues.) bugs crawling on top of bugs to pour over a wall is awesome to see. Sadly most players wipe them away and it rarely happens. The modifier for strong bodies doesn't fix that issue and usually the frames get very bad because a massive pile away from the base doesn't get cleaned.

I like most of the classes and their tools  are very fun.Scanning is very cool but doesnt compete with the others. Some have repeated weapons (which is a bit a of bummer) only a few of those i don't enjoy using.(the under barrel shotgun needs more punch and less shots)The unique weapons are all very neat.

Its a fun game and im a massive fan of the ip.I like the Map,Bug,and Weapon designs, I wish i saw the tanker bug more but the one time i fought it was awesome.

The cons

Frame rate issues, Even the new update has them. Its getting better and for me the game is stable and playable but i know its a big issue for some.

The map rotation Im not a big fan of the method but with the player base its clear even in my short time playing most have a clear preference in game modes and maps. With so many rotation options im still playing the same things in quick play and playing anything outside the events without quick play hasn't really been possible.

The missions can be very long. Not every game needs to be a quick 15-45 minute dopamine hit but if a mission drags in this game it reeeeeeally drags.

The events and even the game in general really awards bug kills over playing objectives a good solution would be a point modifier to kills near a objectives like the refiners but i also know players will most likely milk that.Mind you its not every game but sometimes the farming gets ridiculous ruins the fun.

Not being able to change classes is huge. Its crazy i havent had it be a problem until the last game i played but if there are not engineers there is no ammo.I dont wanna see a limit on how many classes of each can be picked thats not fun but support in this game is fun most would swap if and when its needed. 

The demo guys needs more boom options

review_text:
Hakuoki is an absolute otome classic, being one of the first and most popular localized otome releases in the west. You could say that this game walked so that many of the amazing English otomes we have nowadays could run. I was intrigued by the game and its story so I did some research and found that most of the characters and the events that take place (aside from the obvious fantasy elements) are real, and the historical accuracy is astounding. As many other reviews have stated as well, Hakuoki: Kyoto Winds is only half of the entire Hakuoki experience. I decided to write this review before playing Edo Blossoms so that my opinions would be based solely off of this first part.

Due to the fact that Kyoto Winds is only the first part the romance is, unfortunately, pretty lacking. I imagine the second part will give a lot more to work with in that department but if you're in it for a steamy love story then there are some pretty slim pickings here. Of course there are still some superb CG artworks depicting cute scenes between the protag and her chosen LI, but these tender moments are few and far between[spoiler] the closest thing you get to a kiss is a peck on the forehead from one of the characters...[/spoiler]. The plot itself is fun for the first playthrough, if at times a bit too heavy with the political talk that can seem to drag on endlessly. The fantasy elements served to keep things interesting, while the interactions between titular characters helped offset the boring politics and bring some life back into the story.

Apparently, the original release had only six love interests, while this one boasts a whopping twelve. That's a heck of a lot of men to romance, so you're bound to find at least one that you like... But, on the flip side, you'll probably also find one or two that you'd rather skip. As a completionist myself, this was not an option, and I strove to get every single CG and every ending for all of the characters. My top three were definitely Hijikata, Chikage, and Sakamoto. Hijikata's felt like the game's intended "main route" and so there was a lot of love put into it, while Chikage actually had the shortest route but his character was one of the most interesting. I liked Sakamoto for the amount of romance in his route that well-exceeded the others just due to the kind of character he is. This otome actually has more of a "linear" gameplay style where all of the routes follow the same exact story, just with individual scenes occurring with your chosen LI, so there is a lot of skipping involved. I found Yamazaki's and Shinpachi's routes to be the biggest slogs to get through as I didn't really like either character but your mileage may vary.

As for the heroine herself... She was okay. I didn't have strong opinions either way, but I do feel like there was squandered potential with her character. Rant: [spoiler]Despite being a pure-blooded demon like Chikage and Amagiri and the others, Chizuru has no supernatural abilities to speak of aside from fast healing. While the others flaunted their superhuman strength, speed, stamina, and agility, Chizuru (and even the other female demon Sen) were lacking these things entirely. The heroine even carries around a blade with her at all times and it is said that she can use it in self defense, yet I can count maybe one time in the entire game where she actually successfully lands a hit on somebody, and even then it's hardly a fatal one. I suspect this has something to do with the way that women are seen in Japanese society, attributing to the fact that none of the female characters seem to be at all useful in a fight here, but I digress. Whatever the reasoning may be, she got talked up a bit too much for how useless she ultimately ended up being.[/spoiler] Aside from these complaints she was very much just the typical otome protagonist: is nice, gullible, wants everybody to be happy, has no talent other than traditionally feminine things like cooking/sewing, etc, and gets protected a lot. A tired trope, to be sure, but luckily not a dealbreaker for me.

The artwork, music, and voice acting were exceptional, as expected. However, there were a few times where some characters or sound effects were WAY too loud and grating to the point where it would cause the mic to get all fuzzy when a man would shout something. Shinpachi was the worst offender for this, and there was this one sound effect of villagers talking in the background that looped way too quickly and was super distracting, but thankfully I think it only showed up a couple of times. Just be prepared to have to pull your headphones away from your ears once in a while, while having to subsequently turn the volume back up once Chikage appears on screen (seriously why was this mans so quiet???). So yeah, aside from the sound design not being absolutely stellar, there were also a few typos and repeated phrases throughout the game that would pop up in the text boxes. Not enough to call the translation bad - far from it - but enough that they would assuredly appear a noticeable amount of times in every route. Thankfully there were no major grammatical errors to speak of; overall, entirely forgivable imo.

This game is long, very long. I came out to just over 56 hours by the end of it, so accounting for all the time I had left the game open while I did other things, I'd say it's at the very least a 40+ hour full playthrough if you're doing absolutely everything like I did. You'll definitely get more than your money's worth, especially if you buy these games bundled during a steam sale. It's a really well-made visual novel, no doubt - I won't say it's personally my exact cup of tea due to the heavy historical themes and low amount of romance (in this first part at least), but I plan on playing Edo Blossoms and getting closure on all the routes. I wouldn't play a game for 50+ hours if I [i]didn't[/i] enjoy it, so that being said, try it out if you're unsure. All things considered it's very likely that you won't regret it.

review_text:
Pathologic 2 surpasses its video game identity into a beautiful work of art, similar to a great novel. This game sucked me into it's world and made me connect with it and the characters in a way I never have before in other games. The more I learned about the world and the characters the more alive it all became. I started to care for these people as if they were my own friends and loved ones. This game is a masterful mix of love, mystery, connection, dread, horror, melancholy, bittersweet happiness, and more. It is truly a symphony of themes and emotions. The design of the world, its characters, the sounds, and the music creates a brilliant atmosphere that ranges from beautiful and sweet to chilling and horrendous. 

In classic survival-horror fashion you will have to manage resources, explore and learn about the world, and uncover the mysteries of the town and it's inhabitants. This game is incredibly difficult; I spent most of the game on the brink of starvation and exhaustion but it only enriched the experience. It's not meant to be easy, you are meant to struggle along and push yourself to keep going against all odds.

review_text:
This is bad.
The gameplay is just boring, repetitive and doesn't require any skill what so ever.
Every single enemies fight the same and all of it is clunky as hell.
The level design is horendous, every rooms is a variant of a spiral that make your go all around until you can get out.
The game keep throwing weirdly long sequences of vent crawling or hole/ledge sidestepping that just require you to keep pressing the forward button (the game will even take corners for you, the player inputs is reduced to minimum).

At some point in the game you are forced into the most inane and poorly designed "stealth" sequence where you have to crouch araound for long period of time to backstab dozens and dozens and dozens of blind enemies that apparently also can't hear you brutally gutter and stomp on the bodies of their friends mear feet away from them.

After 6 hours I faced the first boss... which is EXACTLY like every other enemies, execepts you can't even melee it and have to dodge shoot doge shoot dodge shoot dodge shoot dodge shoot dodge shoot for 2 phases until it just drop dead without any ceremony. And dont you DARE to miss a dodge because that will one shot you.
Oh and you'll face that EXACT SAME BOSS roughly 15 minutes later. Not the same entity, just a copy past of the same creature, because why bother even just reskining it a bit, amirit?

The game reeks of "made to look good on trailer" by people that don't know what a videogame is about.
The best example I could come up with is the melee combat, aka 90% of the "gameplay" the game has to offer.

Basically the enemy walk toward you and attack. You have to "dodge" which doesn't require any timing, you just have to press the left or right button and wait for the enemy to hit, at which point you will automatically dodge. Some time they do a two attack combo which requires you to switch side for the second dodge as you can't dodge twice on the same side during a combo.
After that you are allowed to land a couple of attacks which mean mashing the attack button.
The whole "trick" here is that you don't really know if they will do 1 or 2 attacks, so if you attack too soon after 1 attack when they decide to do 2 you will take damage.

A tiny bit into the game they spice things up by adding "tentacle points" that pop after a melee combo, you have then to shoot at it quickly of the enemy super charge (aka they just get more life).

Almost every, single, enemies with a very small couple of gimick enemies all attack the same. Every combat is the exact same. It's mind numbing.

But it gets worse, the best example of "made by people that don't understand what videogame is about" is how they WON'T let you organically chain differnt attacks.
You can unlock a "heavy attack" which is just your guy swinging slightly harder and knocking down enemies.
ANYONE that has ever played any videogame would see this as a way to then attack the enemy while its down, or stomping on it maybe.

Not this game. When the enemy is down it quickly get back up and is completely immune to any attacks while doing so. Every time the game could have had some interesting and organic gameplay enement, a choice was made to not have it.

Oh and some time the game will just randomly decide to not find your save.
You open the game, no saves. Some time it fixes itself alone, otherwise you'll have to dig around to find how to fix it. It's a very VERY comon bug that never got adressed.
And speaking of saving, to stay in the theme of "made by people that don't know gaming" this game also don't know what "saving" means.
When you go to an upgrade station, buy some ugrades, the game doesn't autosave. If you save manually, the game will pretend to have saved, but it actually doesn't, aka if you reload where you saved, the upgrades you just made won't be there, because what the game does is just... snap shot the previous autosave.
It's hillariously amateurish and bad.

The character writting is nonsensical and cringe but HEAVILY carried by outstanding acting and motion capture.
You get random tech wizard sidekick saint that act as if you were his best bud despite having just met him, the cringiest 5 foot girlboss with literally less chest than the male protagonist, that does its hardest to act intimidating but only succeed at being the most obnoxious bitch ever... until she magically switch into best friend mode too...
It's just bad.

The only thing I could say is that the artstyle and general look of the game is good, everything else is awful.

I forced myself to beat the whole thing, then try the two DLCS.

Riot Mod simultaneously deliver the best combat this game ever could, mostly by making guns actually do damages, while hilighting how limited the enemy roster (There is basically 4 enemies and 1 boss, and two of these enemies are basically the same) and awful the mele combat are.

The Last Transmition is ... there I guess. It literally doesn't add ANYTHING to the story, give you a new melee weapon toward the end that completely trivialize combat (but makes it still boring) and... has the weirdest "post credit scene" that comes after a 2 minute logo of the dev company instead of an actual credit (seriously, it was almost sureal, just the logo, glitching out more and more, without you unable to leave, for 2 or 3 minutes, and then that weird joky post credit scene that completely undermine the whole ending)

In the end I can confirm that I hated my time with the game and it never picked up.
It felt short, small and the most basic version possible of what should have been a larger game, but still drag on for aaaaages forcing you to go trough the most mindnumbing story, tedious level design and assenine combat I've ever seen.

But now? 
Frankly it's just mentally exhausting to play at this point and absolutely not new or returning player friendly like it used to be.

It's just event after event to grind for some item you'll probably use for 5 minutes then rip out of your ship.
On top of that the in game markets are dominated by the most greedy mofos you can imagine. 
So good luck buying anything on the exchange without spending real money to sell lockbox keys. 
It's especially brutal to a new or returning player.

The game is running on barely functional spaghetti code that is riddled with bugs that have gone unfixed for the better part of a decade despite frequent player complaints.
The servers are also highly unstable and getting booted from "Server not responding" is an obnoxiously common occurance.
This game makes a Bethesda game look stable.

Well lets just say it's been a nonstop barrage of STD related garbage for literally years now and even if it's not directly related to that travesty of a show it's tainted by it in some way.
The Devs have lost touch with their players and originality.

There's rarely new story or mission related content releases for said "events" either just the same old missions over and over and over and over again.
We used to get entire seasons in a drop and it was a big thing everyone looked forward to and usually had an event with a reward actually worth playing for.

This game peaked with the Iconian War & Temporal Cold War story arcs and never managed to recapture that.
There's very little reason to start playing anymore or come back.

Good graphics, immersive environments. Even though they're good, the few maps get old after some time, but they're very fun to explore the first few times. Enemies are interesting enough to keep you on your toes and don't feel unfair. The weapons in the game serve different gameplay styles, and there's probably something for everyone (please add a pump action shotgun and something like an M1 Garand <3). 

Most of the other items feel quite boring, and are more supportive in nature. They don't really influence your playstyle much. Arcanas also feel pretty weak, most of the time I don't even care what I get. I feel like a game of this type needs heavier synergies that change your gameplay style. Arcanas should also change the way you play more. Replayability is limited by the low number of items and maps and uninteresting arcanas. As many others have said, the gunplay is very good.

Right now, it's a good shooter. Everything else in the game doesn't feel consequential, it's just some minor buffs/debuffs you apply. The game gets hard-carried by its polished base mechanics, which is a good start, but not enough to warrant the price tag of 39.99 €. To be fair, they said they won't change the price of the game after release. But right now, it's not worth the price for me. Don't go in if you expect to be able to create some kind of creative build or find interesting deep synergies that change the way you play.

review_text:
I really want to like this game, but it has too many bizarre shortcomings to work for me. The clever art style, the overall "goal" and the hybrid RTS/city builder/tower defense should combine to be a ton of fun. However, this game is probably best described as a frustration simulator; a steep difficulty curve, a relentless enemy AI, and your greatest obstacle- arguably the worst pathing/friendly AI ever coded join forces to waste your time. Your best winning strategies means nothing, as your builders will disregard your build orders, obvious pathing routes, and will even starve to death rather than survive even when food is readily available. Priorities you the player set are flatly ignored. Builders wander into enemy territory to be slaughtered without reason at least once every scenario, losing more than 2 or so is debilitating to your economy, and you're quickly overrun. Your towers and defense systems target priority is laughable, and there is no means for the player to directly control any of this to fill the gulf in logic between what is happening and what the AI thinks it should be doing. I would compare it to another game, but I genuinely can't think of any game in any of the genres Rise to Ruins taps into that relies so heavily on micromanagement that then leaves it entirely to an AI that is, at it's very best, incompetent. Credit where it's due, Rise To Ruins is a beautiful looking game, and it's clear the developer(s) put a lot of heart into the final product- I don't feel this game is "broken" for lack of effort on their part. 

Granted you're the sort who doesn't mind having to restart your scenario every 2 hours or so because your villagers all decided to wander into harms way for no apparent reason (as there's only one save slot per map per difficulty, so no quicksaving!) then this game may just be your cup of tea. If you (like me) prefer a strategy game where you are actually in "control" and not just shouting suggestions at a dimwitted AI, then Rise to Ruins is best skipped over.

review_text: I bought this game a few years ago, but since I have been going through my Steam library trying to play my short, story line Indie games, I thought I would give this a try. At first I read the other reviews talking about how wonderful this game is and how the dialogue is phenomenal and will make you sob playing it. I can assure you that this is not true. There are few instructions of how to move around in the game, meaning that it took me until nearly the end of the game before I realized I could use arrow keys to move the main characters rather than pointing and clicking the location for them to travel. The actual minigames within this are incredibly easy, such as finding items as mementos to travel through the man's memories, and this puzzle that you have to complete before travelling. It propels you along a linear story line with very little help from the player besides moving around through the map. The pixel graphics are good for their type and age, but when it comes to the dialogue, it is horrific. The dialogue appears in text boxes, and sometimes the dialogue wasn't fully in the box to be able to read. Through about half the game there was a way to make the dialogue automatically appear rather than scroll as the character is speaking, but then this option was disabled, meaning you have to watch every useless strand of dialogue appear on the screen. The dialogue itself, while it has previously been praised, is about on par with a Wattpad fanfiction writer, and uses many colloquialisms in the speech (and sometimes not even colloquialisms, but just slang that you may only use in text messages or bad stories on the internet). While I admit that the plot is a tear-jerker, this is simply because they throw additional plot twists in here almost as if it is a drama on TV, not because it makes sense in the given context. Pretty much, the story only makes you cry because they just keep adding sadness for the sake of sadness. Much of the dialogue doesn't make sense realistically, and the humor is awful. The characters aren't fleshed out at all, and while the symbolism is sweet and this contains an adorable love story, it isn't worth the 3-4 hours spent playing the game to achieve the mediocre ending. I will say, one perk is that there is a lovely violin soundtrack that is quite peaceful to listen to. Otherwise, I wouldn't bother spending the money to purchase this.

You can see that it was written by people who represent a younger generation compared to mine. Some of the jokes are funny and not time related, but many of them rely on too juvenile humor to my taste. Emos decades ago? Doesn't work..

In summary: goodish story (borrows shamelessly from movies like Memento and Inception), emotional at some points, horrible gameplay.
